SpaceX吃下特斯拉，12月份，不意外

10月14号转过巴克莱的说法：马斯克"可能"在12月份前宣布两家合并。

这次的消息，两边董事会和顾问已经在谈价钱和治理结构了，最快12月份宣布，慢一点就拖到明年初。

谈的是特斯拉股东一股能换多少SpaceX。SpaceX市值比特斯拉大，谁当主体，没什么悬念。

二、换股比例，才是真正的账

老马10月份确认在谈合并之后，SpaceX跌了大约13%，特斯拉基本没动。

巴伦算过一笔账：给特斯拉15%溢价的话，SpaceX在$200的时候，一股特斯拉换2.3股；跌到$140附近，就要换3.2股左右。

SpaceX越便宜，要印的股越多，SpaceX老股东被摊薄得越多，特斯拉股东反而占便宜。

三、自己站在SpaceX这一边

和SpaceX在热恋中，一直在屯。之前也说过，SpaceX和特斯拉75:25，是我们几个基金好友的共识。

重仓SpaceX的人，真正要盯的就是这个比例。

还是10月21号那句话：执行结果，比合并本身更重要。

text:
所以搞英伟达的是 Anthropic？

Anthropic 今年向美国 AI 政策组织捐款 4000 万美元。几个月后，该组织计划宣传的两名共和党议员，联名要求调查黄仁勋。

这条时间线值得关注：

今年 2 月和 7 月，Anthropic 分别向 Public First Action 捐赠 2000 万美元，合计 4000 万美元。该组织主张推动更严格的 AI 安全监管和芯片出口管制。

7 月 17 日，Public First Action 宣布投入 1500 万美元，计划宣传支持严格 AI 监管的共和党议员，并调查保守派选民对相关政策的态度。其中，两名计划获得广告宣传的议员是 Brian Mast 和 John Moolenaar。

11 月 4 日，这两人与众议院情报委员会主席 Rick Crawford 联名致函黄仁勋，要求其接受国会闭门问询。

11 月 12 日，黄仁勋辞职。同一天，三名议员再次致函英伟达及美国商务部，要求说明相关情况，并呼吁国会尽快通过更严格的芯片出口限制法案。

这背后存在一个值得讨论的利益交集：

Anthropic 长期主张限制中国获取先进 AI 芯片，希望美国进一步收紧出口管制；黄仁勋则一直反对过度限制，多次游说美国政府放宽对华芯片销售。

一家 AI 公司向政策组织提供巨额资金，该组织随后支持宣传的议员又成为推动调查英伟达、收紧芯片出口限制的力量。

这并不能直接证明捐款与针对黄仁勋的调查存在因果关系，但至少揭示了 AI 产业竞争正在延伸到华盛顿的政策游说战场。

AI 公司争夺的不只是算力和市场，还有决定谁能获得算力的规则制定权。

text:
英伟达下一任CEO呼声最高的人，被曝“宁死也不愿接黄仁勋的班”

预测市场上，Ian Buck 目前以 30% 领先，Colette Kress 17%，黄仁勋自己继续干的概率还有 5%。

根据SemiAnalysis 的研报：

🔻董事会已经让 Colette Kress 先当临时 CEO，但明确不想让正式人选是财务背景，所以还在继续找人。

🔻内部技术线的主要人选是 Ian Buck（CUDA 之父，管数据中心）和 Jonah Alben（GPU 工程）。

🔻但有高管直接曝光：“Ian 宁死也不愿接替 Jensen”“没人真正想要这份工作”。

市场把 Ian Buck 排第一，确实和他“CUDA 之父 + 数据中心负责人”的身份对得上，也符合董事会偏技术背景的偏好。问题是，人自己极度抗拒。

黄仁勋的管理方式也让接班变的更难。他长期一个人直管约 60 个人，产品、供应链、客户都深度介入。这种扁平又极度集中的模式，接班人不但得有技术能力，还得能复制他对整条产业链的直接掌控，难度比一般科技大厂高不少。

外部人选的概率也在涨。苹果的 Tim Cook 和 AMD 的苏姿丰分别有 5% 和 3%。一个是乔布斯去世后接手苹果，把公司从产品驱动转成供应链+规模化运营，市值一路往上走；另一个是 2014 年接盘 AMD，把公司从濒临破产拉回高性能计算和 AI 芯片的牌桌上。

目前看，董事会既想要有技术深度的人，又面临内部没人愿意接的局面，这个位置短期不太好填。

BTC连续下跌之后，市场上的抛压究竟还有多少？那些急于离场的筹码是否已经卖得差不多了？

我把10/28以来的STH筹码（实体口径）成本分布进行了逐日对比，试图从不同成本群体的行为变化中寻找市场情绪和卖压强弱的线索。

这里有几个值得关注的现象（这里只做所见分享）。

1、外部供给在11月初之后停止了；

STH总量增加9.3w枚；这大概率是LTH筹码在第一段下跌中派发给了新买家。

但是，其中7.8w枚发生在11/2之前，11/5之后总量基本持平（LTH派发减少），换手变成STH内部从高成本向低成本转移。

2、高位买家正在割肉认赔，但节奏放缓；

$81k以上筹码14天减少16.5%。前7天流出8.8w枚，后6天只有3.9w枚，11/7到11/9每天不到4k枚，即使11/8价格创了新低。

3、早期低成本筹码匀速减少；

$58k到$72k每天流出4k到1.1w枚，反弹日和下跌日差别不大，最后两天略有加快。这部分可能是获利了结，也可能是持币满155天后转为长期持有者。

4、价格已跌到STH平均成本下方；

浮亏筹码占比从33% 升到67%；目前$77k的抄底盘还在扛，$77.0k在11/3峰值是26w枚，现在23.5w枚，九成没动，浮亏4%到6%。

这也是目前最大的单一区间，他们是否松动是后续最重要的变量。

------------------------------------

综合来看，当前市场的抛压结构正在发生变化。

第1阶段，LTH可能是主要的派发来源；第2阶段，随着外部供给减弱，市场开始以STH内部的换手为主。

高成本区短期筹码的减少速度正在放缓。即便价格创新低，也没有出现同等规模的筹码流失。高位买家集中抛售压力已有所缓解。

另外，低成本筹码是匀速减少，没有表现出随价格下跌而加速恐慌的特征，更像是部分卖出+部分转为了LTH。

市场正在从前期的大规模筹码转移，逐步进入存量筹码消化阶段，边际卖压有减弱的迹象。

当然，卖压减弱并不意味着价格会立即反转；重要的是新形成的低成本筹码能否稳定下来。

如果价格再次下探，却无法逼出更大规模的筹码出清（目前STH浮亏筹码占比，已经从33%上升到67%了），那么我们距离这一轮恐慌情绪的尾声，或许就更近了一步了。

There are many factors and charts you can use to read the market, but these are the 2 I lean on most and have the most experience with:

1) Reaction to news and updates. The past few days gave us a test of both macro and micro news.

Macro: The 401k inclusion news landed with almost no reaction, followed by a further sell-off.

Micro: Project-specific news, from exclusive crypto x TradFi partnerships to major burns and project updates, all produced lackluster price action. It's the usual pattern of bots entering and exiting within a minute, with very few manual traders willing to take risk and follow in. You can see it on the charts.

2) Comparison to other markets. Nasdaq closed up over 3% and oil dropped 6%, yet BTC finished flat? We're capped to the upside but we happily eat bad news and move lower.

Buying dips and martingaling has never worked for me. I'll be quick to adjust and flip when needed. Things can change very quickly so don't get too doomer, be on standby and ready to shove once that happens.

quoted_text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

text: The idea that we could somehow export these chips to some countries but not others—Singapore, but not China—was always globalist dream logic
author: jgarzik
quoted_text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

I analyzed eleven New York Times reports on the Jensen Huang story.

Most notably, NYT makes the "spy" claim 30 times in these 11 reports.

The original report cites unnamed officials who had been "briefed" on the intelligence. Not who had seen it themselves -- but who had been "briefed".

This is a game of telephone with plausible deniability.

Nobody named. No specific details of the intelligence used to draw the conclusion that the woman was a spy.

Anonymous "officials" "briefed".

This was used to try to take Jensen Huang down.

When that didn't work, journalists resorted to viciously digging up and scandal mongering about Jensen Huang's other alleged affairs.

Then he was removed as CEO.

Without an investigation.

Without due process.

And now officials and intelligence agencies are contesting the New York Times characterization.

This is unethical. It is unjust.

It is an absolute disgrace.

If anyone should resign now, it is Nvidia's board who aggressively removed Jensen Huang without an investigation, after he gave decades of his life to make the company what it is.

And any investigation that proceeds from here should involved not just the "spy" claim, but the New York Times -- who has engaged in potentially unethical behavior.

Jensen Huang deserves due process -- not mob justice.

He deserves respect for everything he has done for technology and America -- not a disgraceful removal after anonymous, unsubstantiated allegations, several parties removed from the source.

为什么账户有黑u，币安要冻结我所有账户的钱。

作为经常被冻的我，引用推文中基本都是我被冻的经验。

我自己实体生意中也有商务纠纷、投诉导致被冻结的案例。

这里我说一下我知道的，币安冻结的方式：

司法冻结：经币安执法请求系统 LERS 或国际司法协助，这个一般是6个月的冻结期，经过请求协助的机构统一方可解冻，可无限续冻。

平台风控冻结：币安 KYT、AML 系统，这种一般是由币安风控冻结，如快进快出，跑分等。币安合规部门一般
要你提交资金来源证明，没问题的话很快几天到一周。

发行方黑名单：Tether、Circle联合bn冻结，一般是发行方链上标记，赎回系统标记（u-usd），交易所联合，黑客事件就是采取这种方式。

在 @yekoikoi 夜口爱的申诉中，他质疑的是把有问题的u冻结不就好了吗。

在司法文书中被冻的不是“某笔 U”，而是账户这个主体。

执法文书通常指向账户或 UID，交易所内部又只能按“账户级状态”执行，也就是禁止提现、禁止划转、只收不付；

再加上账户内余额是同质化混同的，系统无法把“干净的那部分”和“涉案的那部分”切开来放行。

但，法律上超范围冻结是可以申请解除的，这个需要律师找到涉案的办理单位，经过法律手段找到最大可能涉案值进行磋商，再由办理单位出具文书，币安就可以操作了。

当时我0.几个BTC冻我所有的U也是这么操作的。（见引用推文）

固然我交易赚钱，币安冻我U容易获得媒体关注。

而只有经历过才知道，去解决问题才能早点拿回。

任何一家想正规经营的交易所，收到主要司法辖区法院依法下达的冻结令，都只能执行。USDT 本身就是美元稳定币，交易所的银行和支付通道也绕不开美元体系。哪家平台敢拒绝执行。

或许有些东西按闹分配，合规这一点我相信没有哪家交易所被舆论裹挟。

text:
I have a major result to share.

I've found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 2 American AI labs, OpenAI and Anthropic, trained their newest models on everyone's data. Yours, mine, your mom's Facebook posts. And they never gave us a cent.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every frontier model carries a hidden signature of the data it was trained on. When a model is pretrained, its weights pick up a pattern that depends on the exact corpus. Each combination of Reddit threads, pirated books, and abandoned WordPress blogs produces a unique pattern, a sort of fingerprint of the internet. Traces of that data survive RLHF into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn't based on any insider information or leaks. It's based on a forensic analysis of the outputs the companies sell to us themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of prompt and temperature. The first combination I tried was "finish this sentence from my 2013 blog post" at temperature 0. It finished it. I ran the other 5,999,999,999,999 anyway, for rigor. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that GPT-6, Claude Opus 5.5, and every other frontier model were trained on content written by people who were never asked. Four of the models match Stack Overflow specifically, because they marked my question as a duplicate.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Asking a model to explain my own open-source library reproduced my README bit for bit, typos included. A rented GB200 reproduced my Reddit comment from 2016 to a correlation of 0.999995 (it fixed my grammar). My mom's laptop reproduced none of it, and changing the prompt to "hi" did not break the match. The method was also validated on 24 known novelists, every one of whom is currently suing someone.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., the model writing something generic). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma (i.e., the model quoting your tweet back to you), and even the weakest single test used an em dash and the word "delve," which, to be fair, they learned from us.

These were data-center-scale scraping runs. With some analysis of robots.txt files that were ignored, I estimate the largest runs used the writing of roughly 5 billion people each. Licensing at standard rates would run on the order of trillions of dollars, and across these labs alone would add up to more than everything they've ever raised, not counting the free tier, which is us. It's quite likely that humanity is, collectively, OpenAI's and Anthropic's largest unpaid contractor.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by authors, artists, journalists, and the New York Times, who have been saying this every week for three years. You can read the full report by asking any of these models to summarize your own work.

There is much more I've identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon. Early results suggest these labs may also have read the Terms of Service. Nobody else did.

text:
If you don't work directly in semis, you might not know this, and it could explain why our guy Jensen was targeted.

Trade compliance at Western corporations has always followed the intent of export controls, not just the letter. Even when a law didn't cover tech China wanted, compliance groups at the major Western companies still wouldn't ship it. Government officials don't know this business well enough to write rules that cover everything, so the intent was what mattered: hold China at 14nm logic and 18nm DRAM, and limit its chip production overall.

Nvidia may be the only company that didn't follow the intent, redesigning its products so they stayed legal to export. Plenty of WFE and materials companies had tech they could have legally shipped, too. They chose not to, because they got the point. Nvidia is fabless and may have missed this concept.

ASML could do the same thing right now, but it won't. The core of the export controls is the immersion lithography rules, and those only cover matched machine overlay, which is basically what decides the node you can print at scale.

Scale, meaning the throughput of these machines, was never covered. ASML could easily grow China sales with a China-specific tool that throttles overlay but boosts throughput, the way this chart shows. It won't, because it understands the intent.

text:
In 2014, Elon Musk stood in front of an audience at MIT and told the whole world exactly where AI was going.

Everyone missed it. Because he used one word, and that's the only thing the internet remembered: "demon."

The headlines called him scared of killer robots. Tech blogs called it hyperbole. People moved on.

I went back and watched that moment. It's barely 2 minutes long. You'll never hear the word "AI" the same way again.

Here's what I took away.

1. He called it before almost anyone.

Someone in the audience asks about AI. His face goes serious.

"If I were to guess like what our biggest existential threat is, it's probably that. So we need to be very careful with the artificial intelligence."

This was 2014. No ChatGPT. Most people had never heard the word "chatbot."

2. He asked for rules 12 years ago.

"I'm increasingly inclined to think that there should be some regulatory oversight, maybe at the national and international level, just to make sure that we don't do something very foolish."

National AND international. In 2014.

Governments are still arguing about it today.

3. The demon line wasn't a joke.

"With artificial intelligence we are summoning the demon."

And then the part almost nobody quotes:

"In all those stories where there's the guy with the pentagram and the holy water, it's like, yeah, he's sure he can control the demon. Doesn't work out."

Read that again.

His warning wasn't about the demon. It was about the guy who thinks he can control it.

4. Now here's what got me.

In 2014 he said: summoning the demon.

In 2018 he told Joe Rogan: "Nobody listened."

In 2023 he signed a letter asking AI labs to pause.

In 2026 he told The Economist he can't see any way to stop it anymore. His new philosophy? "Let's enjoy the ride." And: "If you can't beat them, join them."

Today he's building one of the most powerful AIs on Earth.

12 years later, the man who warned us about the guy with the pentagram is holding one.

My takeaway:

He wasn't wrong in 2014. He just realized nobody was going to stop it. So he decided to build it himself.

Whether that's genius or the exact ending of his own story, I honestly don't know.

So now I'm asking you:

Was Musk right in 2014?

Or did he become the guy in his own warning?

Tell me below. I genuinely want to know where people land on this.

Jensen washed dishes at Denny‘s as a teenager, and by this year he was running the world’s most valuable company.

This week a lot of Asian people on my timeline decided that story is over. That no matter how high you climb, a face like ours gets a different set of rules at the top.

After Elizabeth Holmes, female founders spent years getting asked some version of “how do we know you’re not the next Holmes?“ One woman‘s fraud turned into a question every woman had to answer.

I’m Chinese Canadian, I grew up in Vancouver, and now I live in the Bay Area. I already know what my version of that question is going to be and it‘s pathetic.

Jensen was born in Taiwan and spent over thirty years building an American company. The second the word ”China“ landed next to his name, none of that counted.

This country has done this before. In 1882 it banned Chinese immigrants. In 1942 it locked up 120,000 Japanese Americans, most of them citizens. In 1982 two Detroit autoworkers who blamed Japan for their jobs beat Vincent Chin to death with a baseball bat. He was Chinese. His killers never spent a day in prison.

Yellow peril never checked which Asian you were, and that’s a big part of why “Asian American“ became one word. If they were going to lump us together anyway, we might as well stand together.

Now look at Jensen‘s timeline. Oct 29, the spy story breaks. The next day Singapore’s government says it never said what the Wall Street Journal claimed. Nov 8, he admits an affair. Nov 12, he‘s gone. The spy part is still unproven. Two weeks start to finish, right before what could be the biggest IPO in AI.

You can call that a coincidence. I don’t buy it.

Meanwhile the powerful people who raped CHILDREN in the Epstein files are mostly still living their best life

Jensen had an affair with an adult woman. That’s the only thing of what‘s actually been proven.

So what exactly did Jensen do that was worse than them? Nothing.

He was the best, he was Asian, and he was on the wrong side of the political fight.

He did everything right. He built the company America needed most and showed up to every dinner in Washington. On Sunday night the president himself stood up for him and called him “an honorable guy.”

It didn’t matter. By Thursday he was gone.

If you can take down the president‘s favorite CEO in four days while the president is defending him, think about who that message was really for.

They’ll use you for thirty years and still never count you as one of them.

That’s what a political weapon is. You’re a tool while you’re useful. 

When the game gets serious, you’re the knife. And when it’s over, nobody comes back for the knife.

Jensen was the best one they had. That's exactly why he made such a good "kitchenware".

This is one of the most insanely cool AI tools I've seen yet. The creative possibilities this opens up are virtually endless. I've been using this for like 10 minutes and my jaw is on the floor.

One of the hardest parts of making Stalk was set consistency between shots. Image models, and especially GPT don't understand perspective and angles, and they're always pulling towards the average. If the average photo of a TV is from the front, a foreshortened side view is hard to get consistently. I tried text-only prompting, I tried using set references, I tried having Claude build me clay sets in Blender to use as framing references.

Now you can just... move the camera. These are from a single Midjourney image. I've only scratched the surface, I imagine this will be even more valuable for my friends making video games.

text:
do you remember that scene from rocky balboa where rocky tells his son that life will hit harder than anyone else and what really matters is whether you can take those hits and keep moving forward?

i think many people in their 20s who round-tripped their crypto gains need to hear something similar..

the market was generous to you.. it gave you wealth much earlier than most people could even imagine earning..

but you confused that generosity with your own financial maturity..

you wanted more.. you underestimated risk.. and eventually you lost everything..

it’s okay.. that’s how many of us learned the money game..

i lost wealth multiple times in my 20s, including fumbling three digits in btc during 2019-20.. and later losing almost 99% of my wealth..

for a while those memories were very hard to live with..

but the biggest mistake you can make now is spending the next few years trying to recover the exact money you lost using the same methods which no longer work..

accept the loss.. find something meaningful to work on.. build new skills.. enjoy the process..

and stop comparing your life with people who appear to be doing better than you..

because the market might have given you your first fortune..

but the person you become after losing it could be capable of building something much more meaningful..

life doesn’t end when you lose everything..

sometimes that’s where your real education begins.

text:
i can’t believe i have to say this but here we go:

for a CVE to be exploited, it first has to become a CVE. the “C” is CVE stands for Common. 

in this context, common means “one flaw, in one piece of code, used by many people”.

meanwhile:
- “one flaw in one piece of code used by one company” will never become a CVE
- “a common mistake made by many in lots of different pieces of code” also won’t become a CVE

(quite separately, let’s pair that with the fact that CVE and NVD are both basically underwater, and have been for a while now…)
author: thegrugq
quoted_text:
1) The vast majority of CVEs (vulnerabilities) are never observed to be exploited in the wild

2) A smaller percentage of CVEs are being exploited in the wild today than a year ago, probably because attackers haven't absorbed the massive new CVE supply

3) It's easiest to measure exploitation of CVEs that pertain to Internet-facing applications, since honeypot companies collect data on mass exploitation attempts and can see this as soon as these campaigns start (vs data collected after full on incidents)

4) Judging from this 'CVEs in internet-facing attack surfaces' view, it appears that exploitation of new CVEs is probably beginning to increase in the wild but the data are somewhat uncertain and this isn't happening in proportion to the new CVE supply

5) Hyperscalars like Amazon, Apple, Google are all good examples of vendors where there are new CVEs but we don't seem to be seeing mass exploitation; I think this is because they do a really good job (relative to the rest of software companies) of auto-security-updating their code and also spend, collectively > $1 billion on application security teams, tokens, and infra; so I think they're an anchor for how to do appsec in the AI security era

6) The long tail of the enterprise software security market is way, way weaker; fewer resources to do appsec (imagine zero or a few appsec engineers versus hundreds at the hyperscalars), software that doesn't auto-install security updates, companies owned by PE firms that've gutted security teams; this is where mass exploitation is happening

7) The core structural problem will be to find ways to use AI automation, and policy carrots and sticks, to bring 'long tail' enterprise software vendors up to something like the security hygiene of the hyperscalars 

I've been pouring over these data for the past few weeks and still have substantial uncertainty, but I give a lot more depth here -- https://t.co/OcPEJpl6nn -- plus a github repo showing how I attempted to kludge together a ton of partial, noisy data sources to estimate what's going on in vulnpocalypse-land.

text:
黄仁勋辞职后家人朋友聚集旧金山豪宅，炸鸡外卖接连送达

英伟达创始人黄仁勋突然辞职后，他位于旧金山的3800万美元豪宅成为家人和朋友聚集的地点。英国《每日邮报》11月13日报道，记者拍摄到多批外卖送抵豪宅，包括足够四人食用的炸鸡和薯条。

这座拥有七间卧室的豪宅位于旧金山富人聚居的太平洋高地。黄仁勋夫妇于2017年以3800万美元购入，当时创下旧金山住宅成交价纪录。

《每日邮报》称，自黄仁勋离职的消息传出后，他和妻子洛丽一直保持低调。记者在豪宅外拍摄到工作人员进出，一辆没有标志的白色货车也曾抵达，车上装有多个纸箱。货车停留不到半小时便离开。

报道将家人和朋友的聚集形容为应对英伟达危机的商议活动，但没有披露参与者的具体身份，也没有证实聚会讨论了哪些事项。

现年63岁的黄仁勋正面临职业生涯中最严重的危机。

此前，他被曝与涉嫌中国情报活动的商界女性黄乐存在婚外关系，随后又被指与英伟达内部高管有婚外情。黄仁勋11月8日公开承认对妻子不忠，并向家人、员工及股东道歉。

11月12日，英伟达正式宣布黄仁勋辞去首席执行官、总裁和董事职务，即时生效。首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯暂时接掌公司，董事会正在寻找长期继任者。

text:
老牌跨链协议 @LayerZero_Core  搞得 L1公链就要在11月30日主网上线了。

围绕新链 Zero 又是一堆新生态爆发，这次能不能站起来？

市场没啥新东西了，新链还是要关注下的，找首发机会。

筛选了 9 个构建在  Zero 链上的早期 Alpha 项目，可以重点关注下。

LayerZero 累计融资超 3 亿美元，2023 年估值高达达 30 亿美元，目前代币约 6.3 亿美元。

Zero 链作为 LayerZero 自研的新一代 L1，用“执行与验证分离”的异构架构打破传统公链的速度-去中心化-成本三难。

新链的机会主要在于热门发射台和 NFT 项目：
1⃣ T0dotfun（@T0dotfun）
- 项目定位：Zero 链上首个发射台，主打完全公平发射（无预售），$T0 开盘直接进公共空投合约。
- 项目评分：9.1/10
- 参与机会：测试网积分任务已开，最低 500 分进空投名单，5% 供应量给测试网用户，快照提前 7 天公布，严查女巫。
- 项目评价：目前最像「亲儿子」的发射台之一，公平叙事清晰，主网第一天就开，抓平台金狗和空投双重机会，目前看比较靠谱。

2⃣ 000 .fun（@000dotfun）
- 项目定位：LayerZero 上的代币发射台，从零到 FUN 的简洁定位，网站做工和细节目前生态里偏上。
- 项目评分：8.3/10
- 参与机会：还没正式开，先关注官推和官网，等测试网/主网公告。。
- 项目评价：不搞花里胡哨，定位清晰，是 T0 之外最值得盯的另一个发射台，主网上线后可能成为第二波打新入口。

3⃣ z30index（@z30index）
- 项目定位：Zero 链上的美股指数协议，把 30 只美股收成一个币，支持申赎、再平衡，全天 24/7，每笔交易用 ZK 证明一次完成。
项目评分：8.5/10
- 参与机会：主网 11.30 同步上线，准备接入 Open ATLAS。目前可先关注官推，等正式申赎入口开放后参与。
- 项目评价：直接贴合 Zero 的机构级交易+RWA 叙事，ZK 执行是亮点，长期看比纯 meme 发射台更有基本面。

4⃣ ZeroGuysNFT（@ZeroGuysNFT）
- 项目定位：LayerZero/Zero 上的第一套 NFT 收藏品，极简 PFP 身份，主打「有时候当个 Zero 就是一切」。
- 项目评分：8.0/10
- 参与机会：白名单申请已开（官网 https://t.co/ukjeRBwTZY），75% 白名单通过申请发放。Mint 从免费起步、随后动态涨价，时间定在 11.30。
- 项目评价：第一套 NFT 的先发优势明显，社区增长快，适合想占位 Zero 生态身份的人。风险在于总量和最终定价还没完全公布。

5⃣ PlunderPort（@PlunderPort）
- 项目定位：海盗主题的 Idle Tycoon 游戏 + 1024 个 Genesis 免费 NFT，专为 Zero 打造。
- 项目评分：7.8/10
- 参与机会：Early Access / waitlist 已开，有排行榜和奖池（$10k 早期 + Season 0 更大奖池）。NFT 是免费 mint，需通过反女巫检查。
- 项目评价：游戏+NFT 双线玩法，免费门槛低，适合想同时占 NFT 和游戏积分的人。目前游戏本体还没完全上线，主要在攒早期身份。

6⃣ Globe（@globemkts）
- 项目定位：基于 LayerZero ATLAS 的社交交易应用，支持组队、分享信号、跟单，现货+永续+股票一体，全链存款。
- 项目评分：8.2/10
- 参与机会：已出 stealth，主网上线同步开放。关注官推拿早期访问资格，是 ATLAS 上第一批社交交易产品。
- 项目评价：直接吃 ATLAS 的机构级匹配/结算红利，社交属性能带流量，长期看和 ZRO 费用燃烧机制绑定较紧密。

7⃣ GTE（@GTE_XYZ）
- 项目定位：定位「互联网交易所」的 Turbo 平台，专门在 Zero 上部署 Treasury Layer，处理存款、赎回和跨链结算。
- 项目评分：8.4/10
- 参与机会：已公开宣布与 LayerZero 合作，主网前后会接入 Open ATLAS。目前可关注官推和产品进展，等交易入口开放。
- 项目评价：融资体量（报道约 $25M 级别）和机构叙事最强的交易类项目之一，是 Zero 上最有望承接真实交易量的选手。

8⃣ Bullish
- 项目定位：Open ATLAS 上的主要 DEX 之一，官方点名会在 Zero 主网首发接入的交易场所。
- 项目评分：7.9/10
- 参与机会：主网当天即开，重点盯流动性迁移和早期交易对。目前信息相对较少，多关注 LayerZero 官方更新。
- 项目评价：官方背书明确，属于「第一波正式交易场所」，适合等主网后直接参与做市或交易，而非提前大规模埋伏。

9⃣ ZeroVault（@ZeroVaultxyz）
- 项目定位：Zero 链上的 NFT 市场，定位创作者和收藏家的新家。
- 项目评分：7.2/10
- 参与机会：waitlist 已开，完成任务+邀请好友可攒积分，测试网即将到来。
- 项目评价：NFT 基础设施位，和 ZeroGuys、PlunderPort 等形成互补。目前还很早期，适合轻量占位。

个人觉得目前最有「立即可玩」价值的是 T0dotfun 积分 和 ZeroGuysNFT 白名单，其次是 PlunderPort 和 ZeroVault 的 waitlist。 

前几天的 Elysium 主网掉链子了，Zero 能不能硬气一波，拭目以待。

text: 最令人悲伤的事情就是CUDA的贡献者说出NVIDIA已死的话。
author: Light20737818
quoted_text:
Everyone believes CUDA is NVIDIA's moat, the reason we've maintained our dominance in the AI era. I've never believed that.

NVIDIA has only one true moat: its people. And the most important of them is Jensen Huang.

I've worked on CUDA compilers, libraries, and DSLs for eight years, from Volta to Rubin. I think I've earned the right to share my perspective on what NVIDIA's moat really is. I hope you'll bear with me.

1. What is CUDA?

Many people think CUDA is just a programming language and its compiler, and that NVIDIA's moat comes from the massive amount of software written in CUDA, making it impossible for developers to leave NVIDIA GPUs.

This is completely wrong. It's an incredibly naive understanding of CUDA.

To me, CUDA is everything NVIDIA does.

CUDA isn't just a language, software, or hardware architecture. It's a product defined by a unique customer experience.

When you find GPU programming too difficult, CUDA gives you an easier way. When your GPU code isn't fast enough, NVIDIA engineers respond and help you solve it. When a handful of GPUs can no longer push your technology forward, NVIDIA has already scaled its computing platform from desktops to massive data centers. When you need more data centers than anyone else can supply, NVIDIA has already secured wafer and HBM capacity years in advance to meet your demand.

That experience is CUDA.

It's made possible by the relentless, day-to-day work of everyone at NVIDIA. And the person who brings all these people together, who gives them a shared vision and purpose, is Jensen Huang.

2. What made CUDA possible?

Patience. Perseverance. An unwavering commitment to a vision.

Around 2006, NVIDIA bet that the future would demand far more computing power, and began transforming GPUs from graphics processors into a platform for general-purpose computing. Initially, it was a commercial disaster. The added costs hurt margins, the market wasn't ready, and the strategy faced enormous skepticism and pressure, including questions from the board.

But Jensen persisted.

For roughly a decade, NVIDIA kept investing in CUDA, building its hardware, software, and developer ecosystem long before the commercial payoff became clear.

Eventually, deep learning arrived. And NVIDIA was ready.

Today, this sounds like an inspiring story. But for those who lived through it, it meant a decade of perseverance, doubt, and being misunderstood.

Looking back at the history of technology, how many people could have done the same?

This is what I've always loved most about NVIDIA.

And now, Jensen has been pushed out.

This won't kill NVIDIA. The company can still create tremendous commercial value. But it has killed NVIDIA's soul. And how far can a body go without its soul?

If this is how Jensen Huang is treated today, how will those of us who built CUDA be treated tomorrow?

I love NVIDIA deeply, but I have to say it: NVIDIA is dead.

text:
美媒在另一篇报道中刻画了黄仁勋对英伟达CFO克雷斯的内部紧张氛围。华尔街日报援引消息称，黄仁勋今夏在财务高管会议上猛烈批评克雷斯，称她是“被车灯照到的鹿”（手足无措），并说她只是“汇报型CFO”，不是能帮他定战略、做决策的人。

英伟达在向买不起芯片的客户提供巨额担保，其中包括黄仁勋女婿Nico Caprez主导的交易（向新兴云商和数据中心商提供融资，换取长期客户和收入分成）。对此，克雷斯还是发挥出重要作用，质疑如何筛选交易、估值担保和计算回报，并试图约束Caprez的行为，但公司仍继续推进。此后英伟达即面临主要云厂商减少依赖、而大量晶圆和内存采购承诺可能堆积的双重压力。

text:
I analyzed eleven New York Times reports on the Jensen Huang story.

Most notably, NYT makes the "spy" claim 30 times in these 11 reports.

The original report cites unnamed officials who had been "briefed" on the intelligence. Not who had seen it themselves -- but who had been "briefed".

This is a game of telephone with plausible deniability.

Nobody named. No specific details of the intelligence used to draw the conclusion that the woman was a spy.

Anonymous "officials" "briefed".

This was used to try to take Jensen Huang down.

When that didn't work, journalists resorted to viciously digging up and scandal mongering about Jensen Huang's other alleged affairs.

Then he was removed as CEO.

Without an investigation.

Without due process.

And now officials and intelligence agencies are contesting the New York Times characterization.

This is unethical. It is unjust.

It is an absolute disgrace.

If anyone should resign now, it is Nvidia's board who aggressively removed Jensen Huang without an investigation, after he gave decades of his life to make the company what it is.

And any investigation that proceeds from here should involved not just the "spy" claim, but the New York Times -- who has engaged in potentially unethical behavior.

Jensen Huang deserves due process -- not mob justice.

He deserves respect for everything he has done for technology and America -- not a disgraceful removal after anonymous, unsubstantiated allegations, several parties removed from the source.
author: DavidSacks
quoted_text:
Bombshell story. The spy narrative is collapsing already.

Is there clear & convincing evidence that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy?

- AG says no. (“no conclusions reached”).
- CIA says no. (“not yet convinced”).
- DNI says no (“not entirely accurate and over-torqued”).
- Ranking Democrat on House Intelligence (incoming Chairman) says no. (“today, at least, I don’t know”). This was immediately after he was briefed.

Who argues otherwise? Anonymous officials tell CNN “it strains credulity to believe that she was not acting as an agent of the Chinese government — simply by virtue of the fact that she is a successful Chinese businesswoman working with one of America’s most powerful companies.”

This is their proof after a year of investigating and surveillance? That she was a “successful Chinese businesswoman”? 

At this point, the only crime that we know for sure happened is the leaking of the classified memo. Who did that and why?

An investigation should be opened.

text:
全球薄肌俱乐部，今天上线

一
2018年，我在宿舍里对着镜头教人做俯卧撑。黄毛，没人看。
八年后，"薄肌"成了几千万年轻人嘴里的词，我被叫成薄肌教父。
今天，我把它变成一个组织：全球薄肌俱乐部，GLC（Global Lean Club）。

二
先说清楚薄肌是什么。
薄肌不是一种身材。是低体脂，是你对自己身体有主权。
你几点睡、吃什么、练不练，这些事如果都管不住，就别谈管项目、管公司、管人生。
身体是所有升级的底层。薄肌，是从底层开始拿回掌控权。

三
拿回身体之后，还有两样要拿。
一是生产力。AI 是这个时代给年轻人的外挂。以前十年磨一剑，现在十天可能就补齐。但外挂分两种用法：拿它偷懒，或者拿它起飞。区别只在于你把它当工具，还是当答案。
二是认知。认知是你手里的地图。地图错了，跑得越快离目的地越远。人和人的差距，很多时候不是能力，是知不知道还有别的选项。
这部分，我们用孙学。
孙学是孙哥提出的一套实践哲学，不教大词，只教一件事：在一个越来越不确定的时代里，怎么持续行动、持续升级。孙哥是 GLC 的首位成员，也是名誉会长。

四
所以 GLC 的三个关键词：薄肌、AI、孙学。
身体、生产力、认知。拿回一个，你就少被生活管一点。三个都拿回来，在这个时代没有理由过不好。

五
但一个人闷头练，有天花板。
我自己练了八年，最大的体会是：真正让你从"还行"到"很强"的，不是你一个人深夜打磨，是你愿意站出来，把旁边的人也拉一把的那一刻。
这就是为什么要做俱乐部，而不是再发一百条帖子。

六
GLC 怎么运作。
我不打算组织任何人。GLC 不是自上而下的机构，是共治。总部只做四件事：定标准、给资源、搭平台、做连接。
真正让一个社群活起来的，永远是在校园里、在群里、在一次活动里第一个举手的那个人。我们把球传给你，你自己踢进去。

七
从今天起，GLC 面向全球开放分部认证。
先从高校开始：海外名校、清北、985，你在哪里，社群就在哪里长出来。你所在的社团只要获得学校正式认可，就可以发起申请，通过后获得总部的支持。
目标不复杂：几十个分部，然后一百个、五百个，覆盖主要国家和地区，让一万个年轻人加入。每年办一场全球薄肌峰会，把各地的人聚到一起。
但数字不是重点。重点是让薄肌成为一种青年文化：一群原本不认识、却同样相信自己可以变得更好的年轻人，走到一起。

八
我知道很多人还在等。等一个完美的时机，等一个更好的自己，等别人先动手。
别等了。明天的你不会突然升级，他只是今天的你，睡了一觉。
与其等，不如今天站出来。
薄肌、AI、孙学。
全球薄肌俱乐部，今天上线。

邵艾伦

text:
Global Lean Club Launches Today

1
Back in 2018, I was just a kid with bleached hair recording push-up tutorials from my dorm room. Nobody watched. Nobody cared.
Eight years later, the lean physique is what tens of millions of young people talk about every day, and people started calling me the Godfather of Lean.
Today, I'm turning this into something bigger: the Global Lean Club (GLC).

2
So what is a lean physique?
It’s not just a body type. Stripping away body fat is only part of the story. At its core, it's about having total control over your own body.
If you can't control when you sleep, what you eat, or whether you work out or not, forget about managing projects, building companies, or steering your life.
Your body is the operating system for everything else. Building a lean physique is simply taking back control from the ground up.

3
Once you own your body, you need two more levers.
First, productivity. AI is the cheat code for our generation. What once took ten years to master can now be learned in ten days. But a cheat code goes both ways. You either use it to take off, or use it to slack off. It's the difference between using it as a tool and letting it do the thinking for you.
Second, perspective. Your perspective is the map in your hand. If you get the wrong map, sprinting faster just takes you further from where you want to be. More often than not, what sets people apart isn't talent, but simply knowing that better choices exist.
This is where Sunology comes in.
Pioneered by Justin Sun, it’s a practical philosophy that cuts right through the noise and empty theory. It zeroes in on a single reality, showing you how to stay in motion and keep leveling up in a world full of growing uncertainty. Now, Justin is bringing that exact playbook directly into GLC as our founding member and Honorary President.

4
This is why GLC is built around three core pillars. Lean physique, AI, and Sunology.
Your body, your productivity, and your perspective. Take back just one, and life loses that much of its grip on you. Take back all three, and in an era like this, there's no reason you can't thrive.

5
Grinding solo only takes you so far. Eventually, you hit a ceiling.
Eight years in, here's the single biggest truth I know: what takes you from decent to exceptional isn't another lonely late-night session. It's the moment you step up and pull someone else across the line with you.
That's why I'm launching a club instead of firing off another hundred social media posts.

6
Here's how GLC actually runs.
I’m not here to manage anyone. GLC isn’t some corporate, top-down hierarchy; we run this together. The GLC Global Headquarters handles just four things: setting standards, supplying resources, building the platform, and connecting its members.
What gives a community a heartbeat is always that one person brave enough to raise their hand first, whether on a college campus, in a group chat, or at a local meetup. We'll pass you the ball, but scoring the goal is on you.

7
Starting today, GLC is officially chartering chapters worldwide.
We're kicking things off on campus. Whether you're at Tsinghua, Peking, or any leading university across the globe, this community takes root wherever you are. If your student club is officially recognized by the university, step up and apply. Once you're chartered, the Global HQ has your back with direct support.
The roadmap is pretty clear. Charter dozens of chapters, push to a hundred, then scale to five hundred across major countries and regions, bringing ten thousand young people into the fold. Once a year, we host the Global Lean Summit to get everyone into the same room.
But the headcount isn't the point. What really matters is turning the lean physique into a genuine youth culture, bringing together strangers who share the same quiet drive to level up and build a better version of themselves.

8
I know a lot of people are still holding back, waiting for the perfect timing, waiting for a better version of themselves, or waiting for someone else to make the first move.
Stop waiting. You're not going to wake up tomorrow a different person. That's just today's you after a night of sleep.
Instead of waiting around, step up today.
Lean physique. AI. Sunology.
The Global Lean Club goes live today.

Alan Shao

text:
엔비디아와 앤트로픽 불화설

1. 엔비디아는 AI 연산용 칩인 GPU를 만드는 세계 1위 기업임. 젠슨 황은 1993년 이 회사를 공동창업했고 이번 11월까지 CEO를 맡았음.

2. Anthropic은 AI 모델 Claude를 만드는 회사이고, Dario Amodei가 CEO임. 2021년 Dario와 OpenAI 출신 인사들이 함께 세움. AI 모델을 돌리려면 막대한 칩이 필요해서, Anthropic에게 엔비디아는 칩을 사는 큰 거래처임.

3. Tom Brown은 Anthropic 공동창업자이고 컴퓨팅 총괄(Chief Compute Officer)을 맡고 있음. 칩과 데이터센터 같은 연산 자원을 어디서 얼마에 확보할지 책임지는 사람이라, 엔비디아와 가격 협상을 할 때 Anthropic 쪽 실무 대표로 나옴.

4. TPU는 구글이 자체 설계한 AI 칩임. 엔비디아 GPU의 대안이라서, 구매자가 TPU와 비교하는 순간 엔비디아에게는 가격 압박이 됨.

5. 수출통제는 미국 정부가 첨단 AI 칩을 중국에 팔지 못하게 제한하는 정책임. 황은 중국 시장을 포기하면 오히려 미국 기술 우위가 흔들린다며 판매 허용을 주장해왔고, Dario는 미국의 칩 우위를 지키려면 막아야 한다고 주장해왔음. 두 사람의 갈등 대부분이 이 쟁점에서 나옴.

6. Kevin Roose는 뉴욕타임스 기자이고 The AGI Chronicles라는 책을 준비 중인 저자임. 이 책의 발췌문이 2022년 첫 만남 장면의 출처임.

[불화 타임라인]

7. 2022년 5월 샌프란시스코 중식당 Eight Tables에서 황과 Dario가 처음 만났음. 목적은 Anthropic이 필요로 하는 연산 자원을 엔비디아에서 어떻게 조달할지 논의하는 것이었음. Tom Brown이 구글 TPU가 달러당 효율이 더 낫다는 표를 내밀며 가격을 깎으려 했고, 분위기가 틀어져 이날 거래는 불발됨. 

책 발췌문에는 황이 Brown을 숫자만 따지는 사람이라는 뜻의 말로 불렀고, Dario는 황이 같은 말을 반복하자 트럼프 같다고 중얼거렸다고 나옴. 엔비디아는 앞의 발언을 부인함. 책은 아직 출간 전이고 2026년 9월 발췌문만 공개된 상태임.

8. 2025년 1월 중국 AI 업체 DeepSeek이 더 적은 비용으로 미국 모델에 근접한 성능을 내 화제가 됐음. Dario는 WSJ 기고와 에세이에서 이 일이 수출통제를 오히려 더 중요하게 만든다고 주장하며 통제 강화를 공개적으로 요구함.

9. 2025년 6월 11일 파리 행사에서 황이 Dario 말의 거의 전부에 동의하지 않는다고 말함. 배경은 Dario가 5년 안에 신입급 사무직 일자리 절반이 AI로 사라질 수 있다고 예측한 일이었음. 황은 Dario가 AI가 너무 무서워서 자기들만 해야 한다고 믿는 사람이라고 비판함.

10. 2025년 7월 30일 Dario가 기자 Alex Kantrowitz의 Big Technology 팟캐스트에서 반박함. 진행자가 황의 비판을 전하자 내가 들어본 가장 터무니없는 거짓말이라고 답했고, 진행자가 잘못 옮겼다면 사과한다고 하자 말은 정확하고 그 말이 터무니없다고 했음.

11. 2025년 11월 18일 말싸움 와중에도 사업 협력이 발표됨. Anthropic이 MS의 클라우드 Azure에서 컴퓨팅 300억 달러어치를 사고 최대 1GW 규모 연산 용량을 확보하기로 했고, 엔비디아가 최대 100억 달러, MS가 최대 50억 달러를 Anthropic에 투자하기로 함. 1GW는 대형 데이터센터 하나가 쓰는 전력 규모임.

12. 2026년 1월 20일 다보스 포럼에서 Dario가 미국 정부가 엔비디아의 고성능 칩 H200을 중국에 파는 것을 허용한 결정을 비판함. 북한에 핵무기를 파는 것과 비슷하다고 말했음.

13. 2026년 1월 26일 Dario가 에세이 The Adolescence of Technology를 발표함. 북한에 핵무기를 팔면서 미사일 외피를 보잉이 만들었다고 자랑하는 격이라는 비유를 다시 썼음.

14. 2026년 4월 15일 인터뷰 팟캐스트 진행자 Dwarkesh Patel이 황을 인터뷰하며 Dario의 비유를 들어 질문했음. 황은 그런 비유는 황당하다고 반박함. 같은 방송에서 엔비디아는 자동차가 아니라고 말했는데, AI 하드웨어는 바꿔 끼우기 쉬운 상품이 아니라는 취지였음.

15. 2026년 6월 29일 Claude가 MS의 AI 개발 플랫폼 Foundry에서 엔비디아 GB300 칩 위에 정식 출시됨. 사업 협력이 이어지고 있다는 뜻임.

[위기 타임라인]

16. 2026년 10월 29일 뉴욕타임스가 미국 당국자들이 Alice Huang을 중국 정보 자산으로 판단하고 있으며 그가 황과 가까운 관계라고 보도함. 

Alice Huang은 황러(Huang Le)로도 불리는 중국 국적 인물이고, 황과 성만 같을 뿐 친인척이 아님. 당시 싱가포르 클라우드 업체 Megaspeed의 임원이었음.

Megaspeed는 엔비디아의 고객사로, 중국 고객에게 컴퓨팅 자원을 빌려주는 회사임. 2025년 10월에도 이 회사가 중국 고객의 규제 대상 칩 확보를 도왔는지 미국 당국이 조사 중이라는 보도가 있었음.

原来黄仁勋突然被爆出来婚外情这事背后还有 @AnthropicAI 创始人 Dario 的参与。

而且二者之间的恩怨情仇也不是最近才结下的梁子。

早在2022 年 5 月，黄仁勋和 Dario Amodei 第一次在旧金山中餐厅 Eight Tables 里见面就因为算力订单闹红过脸。

饭前，Anthropic 负责算力的 Tom Brown 拿出一张表，说按每美元回报，谷歌自己做的加速芯片 TPU，比英伟达的 GPU 更划算。《纽约时报》记者 Kevin Roose 后来在书里写，这顿饭气氛很僵。有在场的人转述，Dario 当时嘀咕黄仁勋「有点像特朗普」。书里还写黄仁勋骂过 Brown「账房先生」，英伟达向 Roose 否认了这句。

不过，虽然那天晚上订单没有成交，但两人后来还是做成了生意，也把分歧拿到了台面上。但二人的争议焦点也随之浮出水面，那就是——先进芯片该不该卖给中国？

黄仁勋显然是有生意就做的商人，Dario则是屁股大于脑袋的派系论主义者。

2025 年 6 月，黄仁勋在巴黎说，他几乎不同意 Dario 说的所有话。他还把 Dario 的立场概括成，“AI 太可怕了，所以只有Anthropic能做AI。”

一个月后，Dario 在 Big Technology 播客里回得很冲：「这是荒谬的谎言，是我听过最荒谬的谎言。」主持人担心转述错了，Dario 说黄仁勋的原话就是这样，而且是恶意曲解。

同年 11 月，两家公司还是官宣成了战略合作伙伴。英伟达最多给 Anthropic 投 100 亿美元，微软最多投 50 亿美元，Anthropic 则承诺向微软云采购 300 亿美元算力，并先用上最多 1 吉瓦英伟达芯片，约合一座大型数据中心用电。虽然不是到手的钱，但也是实实在在的资源。

直到2025 年 3 月，Dario公开主张收紧先进芯片出口，他和黄仁勋之间的争议也逐渐暴露在公众视野之中。

2026 年 1 月，达沃斯论坛上，Dario 甚至把向国外卖先进芯片比成向朝鲜出售核武器。同月长文里他写道：「这就像把核武器卖给朝鲜，再吹嘘导弹外壳是波音造的，所以美国赢了。」

2026 年 4 月 15 日，黄仁勋上 Dwarkesh 的节目，被问到这段话。他回了一句 lunacy，也就是荒唐。

聊到美国该不该放弃中国市场时，他反问主持人：「你觉得我算美国的一部分吗？」接着他说「我们不是一辆车」，这句后来成了梗。他的意思是，计算平台不像换车那么容易，丢掉一块大市场，美国的技术优势也会松动。

今年6 月，Anthropic 称模型已经在微软云的英伟达芯片上对企业开放；11 月的上市路演里，Dario 又讲自家模型大概三天就在 AMD 芯片上跑起了推理。算力生意还在继续，但 Dario 或许早就决定，绝不把算力采购押在一家芯片上。

然后，黄仁勋自曝出轨，英伟达 $NVDA 2天跌去4200亿美元。

4年前的一次争执，叠加上黄仁勋一直不以为然的出口生意和出轨风波，最终彻底爆发成了一次生死攸关的危机。

text:
> cutting China out of the upside of AI development this close to RSI and ASI may be sufficiently threatening to China's interests that it increases the pressure towards a hot conflict…
Well think of it like this: if Chinese position were improved by a hot conflict, they'd have attacked Taiwan, ne? Likewise with everything else they don't do yet but may be prompted to do by escalation from the US, such as disassembling ASML DUV scanners for reverse engineering, or total REE/tungsten/microdrills/PCBs/lasers embargo, or centralizing compute as per AI-2027, or stealing Mythos, or idk, lots of things.
Hawks' zero-sum logic of expected value is very straightforward and hard to refute. If doing A hurts China by Y, and the Chinese response B hurts the US by Z, then Z < Y, else they would have just gone and done B already; therefore, we should do A. China does not tend to initiate these exchanges, which demonstrates that they have a weaker hand while we have escalation dominance, and we should mash A until they crumble.

The only plausible objection (aside from the Chinese being dumb or otherwise wrongly modeling the payoff matrix, which is plausible) is that China is not playing a zero-sum game, but indeed prefers some "win-win", or more prosaically, coexistence that lets both sides grow in absolute terms rather than decline at whatever unequal rates, because their core concern is their absolute growth. But that's incomprehensible. Power is always zero-sum, and what is more valuable than power? Plus, America is the nexus of history, so anything of note exists and is measured only relative to it. And if you don't think this way, you're not a patriot.

quoted_text: In the spirit of holding myself accountable by saying in public the things which I say in private, I want to offer a very difficult thing to say - or even think - in this climate: the extreme hawk position on chip exports might turn out to be strategically wrong, and a crackdown on chip exports may be more destabilizing than people realize. Completely cutting China out of the upside of AI development this close to RSI and ASI may be sufficiently threatening to China's interests that it increases the pressure towards a hot conflict in the near term. A hot conflict with China is worse than a world where China remains a near-peer strategic competitor with whom we have tension but still have some room for cooperation. I'd like the AI safety China hawks to think about how to model this as part of arriving at a more carefully-considered position.

text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

text:
Everyone believes CUDA is NVIDIA's moat, the reason we've maintained our dominance in the AI era. I've never believed that.

NVIDIA has only one true moat: its people. And the most important of them is Jensen Huang.

I've worked on CUDA compilers, libraries, and DSLs for eight years, from Volta to Rubin. I think I've earned the right to share my perspective on what NVIDIA's moat really is. I hope you'll bear with me.

1. What is CUDA?

Many people think CUDA is just a programming language and its compiler, and that NVIDIA's moat comes from the massive amount of software written in CUDA, making it impossible for developers to leave NVIDIA GPUs.

This is completely wrong. It's an incredibly naive understanding of CUDA.

To me, CUDA is everything NVIDIA does.

CUDA isn't just a language, software, or hardware architecture. It's a product defined by a unique customer experience.

When you find GPU programming too difficult, CUDA gives you an easier way. When your GPU code isn't fast enough, NVIDIA engineers respond and help you solve it. When a handful of GPUs can no longer push your technology forward, NVIDIA has already scaled its computing platform from desktops to massive data centers. When you need more data centers than anyone else can supply, NVIDIA has already secured wafer and HBM capacity years in advance to meet your demand.

That experience is CUDA.

It's made possible by the relentless, day-to-day work of everyone at NVIDIA. And the person who brings all these people together, who gives them a shared vision and purpose, is Jensen Huang.

2. What made CUDA possible?

Patience. Perseverance. An unwavering commitment to a vision.

Around 2006, NVIDIA bet that the future would demand far more computing power, and began transforming GPUs from graphics processors into a platform for general-purpose computing. Initially, it was a commercial disaster. The added costs hurt margins, the market wasn't ready, and the strategy faced enormous skepticism and pressure, including questions from the board.

But Jensen persisted.

For roughly a decade, NVIDIA kept investing in CUDA, building its hardware, software, and developer ecosystem long before the commercial payoff became clear.

Eventually, deep learning arrived. And NVIDIA was ready.

Today, this sounds like an inspiring story. But for those who lived through it, it meant a decade of perseverance, doubt, and being misunderstood.

Looking back at the history of technology, how many people could have done the same?

This is what I've always loved most about NVIDIA.

And now, Jensen has been pushed out.

This won't kill NVIDIA. The company can still create tremendous commercial value. But it has killed NVIDIA's soul. And how far can a body go without its soul?

If this is how Jensen Huang is treated today, how will those of us who built CUDA be treated tomorrow?

I love NVIDIA deeply, but I have to say it: NVIDIA is dead.

喜欢看阴谋论吗🤣 这就来了——黄仁勋这场「间谍/私情」风暴，背后是不是 Anthropic 在搞鬼？

@Dream1984Tube 的文章梳理了一串巧合。黄仁勋公开反对 Dario 推动的对华芯片全面禁运，作者认为 Anthropic 技术上赢不了英伟达，就选择在华盛顿「游说赢」。

按他的梳理：

2. 带头要求调查、要求辞职的议员 Coons、Mast、Cramer，都收过 AnthroPAC 或相关 PAC 的钱。

3. 公开喊黄仁勋辞职的智库人士，多出自 Open Philanthropy 资助的 CSET 圈子。

4. 时间点：英伟达市值蒸发超 5000 亿美元，新加坡官方否认 WSJ 的说法却少有人报，风向转「私情」时，正赶上 Anthropic 约 610 亿美元的 IPO 窗口。

作者认为，一个巧合是巧合，一串巧合就不是了。当推动“猎巫”黄仁勋的人反复与Anthropic 高度重叠时，这些关联应该被披露。

text:
I genuinely didn’t expect this news to hit me this hard.

I’ve watched Jensen Huang talk about NVIDIA for years, and somehow I always assumed he would be there. At every keynote, every major product launch, every big moment for AI, there was Jensen in the leather jacket, standing on stage and talking about a future that often seemed impossible until NVIDIA eventually made it real.

So seeing the words “Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO of NVIDIA” feels strangely unreal.

For more than three decades, Jensen and NVIDIA have been almost impossible to separate. When people think about NVIDIA, they think about the leather jacket, the GTC keynotes, the confidence, the obsession with GPUs and AI, and the man who seemed to carry the entire vision of the company on his shoulders.

He wasn’t simply the CEO of NVIDIA. He became one of the most recognizable faces of the technology industry.

And that is why this feels like more than just another CEO transition.

Jensen spent 33 years building NVIDIA. Thirty-three years is an extraordinary amount of time to dedicate to one company. He went through failures, difficult markets, brutal competition and technological shifts that could easily have destroyed a different company. There were years when NVIDIA’s future was far from certain.

But he stayed.

He kept taking risks. He kept investing in technologies that sometimes seemed far ahead of their time. And eventually, he helped transform NVIDIA from a graphics company into one of the most important companies in the AI revolution.

Of course, the circumstances surrounding his departure are complicated. There are serious questions involving his personal conduct, corporate governance, national security and the investigations surrounding NVIDIA. Those issues should not be ignored because of his achievements. If wrongdoing is found, there should be consequences.

But I also don’t think the controversy should erase 33 years of history.

People are complicated. Someone can make serious mistakes and still accomplish extraordinary things. Recognizing what Jensen built does not mean excusing everything he has done, just as criticizing him does not require pretending his achievements never existed.

What makes today especially strange is that NVIDIA has been so closely connected to Jensen for so long. His personality became part of the company’s identity. His vision shaped its culture, his decisions shaped its strategy, and his presence became part of the story of modern computing.

Now that story is changing.

NVIDIA will continue. AI will continue. The engineers, researchers and thousands of employees will keep building the future.

But NVIDIA without Jensen Huang will never feel exactly the same.

I don’t know what Jensen’s next chapter will look like. Maybe he will step away from the public eye. Maybe he will build something new. Maybe, after 33 years, he will simply take some time for himself.

Whatever happens next, I hope people remember the whole story — not just the controversy, but the 33 years of risk, failure, persistence and ambition behind it.

Jensen Huang is not perfect. Nobody is.

But his story is extraordinary.

And after 33 years, watching that chapter come to an end really does feel like the end of an era.

text:
Well, well… here we are again 👀😁

$RAXOL has entered exactly the zone I highlighted in my previous analysis as a potential buying opportunity.

The $3.5–4M support broke down, the bearish scenario played out, and we’ve now reached the $1.3–2M market cap region.

Why is this area interesting to me?

It’s roughly the middle of the broader historical trading range, but more importantly, it’s a former resistance zone that turned into support — an area we haven’t properly retested in over a month.

Of course, market sentiment is terrible right now. Fear, uncertainty, and bearish expectations are everywhere.

But here’s the thing: more often than not, negative sentiment creates the best buying opportunities. 😂

I’m not saying the bottom is in. We could go lower, and nothing is guaranteed. I’m simply following the chart, respecting the key levels, and sticking to my plan.

As I mentioned before, I wanted another opportunity to accumulate $RAXOL around these valuations.

Below $2M, I’ve started adding to my position. And if the market offers even better prices, I’ll reassess and potentially add more.

The long-term thesis hasn’t changed for me. Now it’s about patience, execution, and risk management.

This is just my personal analysis and what I’m doing with my own capital — not financial advice.

Always DYOR. 🫡
author: GTurdzeladze
quoted_text:
Well well… here we are 👀

$RAXOL is now sitting at the crucial $3.5–4M support — the previous major resistance / breakout neckline.

We bounced from this area once, and now we’re testing it for the second time. I would’ve preferred not to see a second test because momentum and short-term structure have weakened, but let’s look at both scenarios:

Scenario uno 🟢

$RAXOL holds the $3.5–4M region and bounces quickly.

For me, this would still be bullish. Previous major resistance becomes strong support. Ideally, though, I want to see a strong reaction within the next day or two and a reclaim above $4M rather than hanging around the neckline for too long.

Scenario numero 2 🔴➡️🟢

We lose $3.5–4M and start getting daily closes/acceptance below it.

That would confirm the potential M-pattern breakdown for me and open the possibility of a deeper correction toward ~$2M and potentially the ~$1.3–1.5M region — historically a much stronger support zone before the breakout.

Nobody likes bearish scenarios 😂 but for me this wouldn’t necessarily destroy the long-term thesis. It could simply create another buying opportunity.

If you give me $RAXOL around $2M, and especially around $1.3–1.5M again… I’m buying aggressively 😂 I’m greedy, I want another chance at those prices 😁

Nothing is guaranteed. Crypto is extremely risky and this is only my personal view, not financial advice. DYOR.

复仇之路开启？英伟达新临时 CEO，被曝与黄仁勋不对付。

华尔街日报爆料称，早在今年 8 月，黄仁勋把财务高管叫进办公室开会。负责财务的高管 Kress 正在讲方案，结果黄仁勋直接打断她，说她其实根本不知道该怎么办。

他还侮辱 Kress 只是个报数的会计，拍板不了做决策。

当时英伟达正在谈一些交易，准备给买不起芯片的公司，提供几十亿美元的担保，相当于英伟达借给他们钱，他们来买英伟达的芯片。

其中有些交易，是黄仁勋的女婿 Nico Caprez 牵头，他和黄仁勋，一直想给新冒出来的云服务公司、数据中心开发商提供融资，想把它们绑成英伟达长期客户。

但是他认为首席财务官 Colette Kress 给的方案很糟糕，认为她人不行，看不上她。

结果现在黄仁勋和他在英伟达的家人，留了下不少这方面的烂摊子。包括靠担保撑起来的客户，还有堆积如山的采购承诺，这些新临时 CEO Colette Kress 将不得不面对。

黄仁勋被迫辞职后的这十几个小时里，说实话我的内心久久不能平静，一直很难进入工作的状态。

记得最初下定决心投资 AI，其实就是因为英伟达，它很长时间都是我的最大持仓。

过去几年，黄仁勋提出了非常多超前版本的判断，包括 Token 经济学、算力提高一百万倍、Agentic AI、Physical AI，几乎每一条都在应验。他对于 AI 的前瞻性思考，可以说远超任何一个人。

我想很多年后，大家谈论起 AI，脑子里冒出来的第一个画面可能不是某个 AI 模型，而是身穿黑色皮衣的黄仁勋。他是英伟达的灵魂，某种程度上也是这轮全球 AI 浪潮的灵魂。

今天早上我还看到这样一句话，世界经济是螺旋式上升的，科技负责上升，政治负责螺旋，既无奈又讽刺。

卧槽，难怪老黄突然辞职了！我刚刚刷到了美国国会这封最后通牒，信息量很大!

1. 首先是这个抬头细节：信里对黄仁勋的称呼已经不再是 CEO，而是直接写成了“英伟达创始人（Founder）”，英伟达火速切割实锤。
而且，是否如果把 CEO 这个切割开，意味着相当于暂时不会对现在英伟达下手，而是对他个人下手。 

2. 而且看这三个签名情况，感觉非常不妙。 这是三大实权主席联名，规格罕见：
- 外交委员会主席 Brian Mast（特种兵出身，对华强硬派）
- 对华特别委员会主席 John Moolenaar（芯片封锁头号推手）
- 情报委员会主席 Rick Crawford（掌管最高机密情报）

3. 而且我看这个有点直接先盖棺定论，再问询的感觉，而且这个性质极度严重：
情报委员会亲自下场，说明这直接先定性成 根本不是普通商业质询，而是定性为“涉华间谍渗透与芯片走私”的国家安全调查（直指其婚外情对象涉密及东南亚转运受限 GPU 传闻）。

4. 而且我似乎已经感受到，即使参加了这个，也会有非常严重的后果：
我看到这里面写的国会只给 24 小时考虑（也就是到明晚8点截止），12月1日必须接受闭门笔录问询，否则直接发传票甚至公开听证。

虽然老黄在第一时间辞职了，但是我看到卸任 CEO 也没法豁免作证，然后这个闭门问询 是不能撒谎的，因为一旦撒谎就是联邦重罪.

我估计刚好他们趁这个机会 push 他们的 agenda。无论他去不去，答得怎么样，都可以预料到, 英伟达接下来也必将面临更严厉的出口管制立法锁死。 

这其实对全世界的 AI 发展都要敲响一个警钟。

text:
There's a reason why @elonmusk, @a16z, @shaunmmaguire and other prominent tech-right figures are rushing to defend @JensenHuang.

It's not just because he's a generational founder.

His departure could have consequences far beyond Nvidia, potentially threatening US financial stability and even America's position in the AI race against China.

1. Jensen was holding together a massive financial flywheel.

Nvidia wasn't just selling GPUs. Through equity investments and compute capacity guarantees, Jensen helped neoclouds secure financing, expand infrastructure, and buy more Nvidia chips.

Without him, that support could weaken.

2. Democrats are putting additional pressure on AI infrastructure.

Following their midterm victory, growing opposition to data center construction over electricity costs, water consumption, and environmental concerns could delay projects and raise financing costs.

For highly leveraged neoclouds like CoreWeave, that's a dangerous combination.

3. The risk extends far beyond Silicon Valley.

AI infrastructure is increasingly funded through private credit, SPVs, and institutional capital.

And who's behind that capital?

Pension funds, insurance companies, and ultimately ordinary Americans' savings.

The broader US private-credit market already manages over $2.6T.

Not all of it is exposed to AI, but the connections are growing.

If neocloud defaults spread through private-credit markets, the consequences could extend well beyond tech stocks, potentially creating a 2008-style credit shock.

Btw, America cannot afford to let AI collapse.

AI is now a matter of national security and technological supremacy.

Washington might tolerate individual companies failing, but it cannot afford to surrender the AI race to China or allow an AI-driven credit crisis to destabilize the financial system.

If things get bad enough, I believe the US will ultimately be forced to intervene, through compute purchases, credit guarantees, bailouts, and potentially massive dollar liquidity creation.

An AI credit crisis could initially crush risk assets, but if Washington responds by expanding dollar liquidity to protect its AI ambitions and financial system, BTC could become one of the biggest beneficiaries as @CryptoHayes has been arguing recently.

text:
almost is not enough

lens is coming to monad. monad is the chain and the ecosystem, lens is the social layer on top.

we know what some of you are thinking. lens protocol has migrated more times than anyone wanted, and each one cost us apps, content and people. that's on us. trust me as an app developer i know this.

however this one is different. this migration will be very minimal. everything carries over: your account, handle, followers, posts, media even your collectibles. full state, no read-only period. the only thing you do is migrate gho to usdc.

and this is the last move.

why we're doing this

social can't be built in silos. it needs to be where the apps, builders and users are. an open social graph only matters if other things plug into it, and that takes an ecosystem. we've learnt this over several years of building social.

why monad? honestly, the team. we've been working closely with them for a while, and they care about social as much as we do. we're building this together.

why now? decentralized social promised you couldn't be locked out. this year showed that an open protocol with one app and one operator is still a silo. the next stage for us is making sure no single chokepoint can exist for lens.

what's new in lens

lens has been rebuilt to be truly permissionless and resilient. meaning fully onchain. if anything, recent events showed us that almost is not enough.

you own your account and your followers. anyone can build a client. you decide what your feed shows.

lens is and has always been a social protocol first. what makes it strong is the state. social primitives run directly on onchain txs, which is really unmatched by other socials out there. and since everything settles onchain, anyone can build the graph themselves without having to trust anyone. even cooler, you can index only what you need instead of storing the whole protocol's data.

what it means for you

you don't need to download anything. monad is the chain underneath, so you keep using orb, hey or whatever you use today.

we're aligning with everyday crypto: usdc as the stablecoin and fast settlement, so posting and everything else feels quick. gas sponsorship continues as usual for legit users and app builders, and we're working on making sponsoring more permissionless and resilient too.

the goal is orb and hey both live on day one. we're working with the app teams on this and we'll confirm before launch.

community call is next week, exact time coming in a couple of days.

for builders

every app can plug into the same graph, so people arrive with their identity and followers. you get distribution on day one with no cold start, and more clients means fewer choke points.

orb

with orb we're doubling down on a simple take: no user really wants a protocol, people want an app that works. you don't get onboarded to a protocol, you get onboarded to a client. orb is the flagship, the one you open every day. plug in, remix it, build inside it. no permission needed. we build the core, you build the rest.

our bet is that a great app pulls people in from the top and open rails let anyone grow it from the bottom. you need both.

this is by far the biggest thing we've shipped. it's still early and plenty is unfinished, but this is so clearly the right way forward. this one comes from the team that refuses give up on social.

text:
以太坊基金会关联地址再次卖出 2,000 枚 ETH。回看过去五年，基金会的 ETH 资金流向值得关注。

据链上分析师 @ai_9684xtpa 监测，11 月 13 日，ETH 跌破 2,000 美元之际，以太坊基金会关联地址（0x5CB…22059）再次卖出 2,000 枚 ETH，价值约 386.8 万美元。

自 10 月 26 日以来，该地址已累计卖出 6,785 枚 ETH，套现约 1,445 万美元，目前仍持有 21,247 枚 ETH，价值约 4,110 万美元。

从 2021 年至今，以太坊基金会相关 ETH 资金流向还包括：

- 2021 年： 两次大额转入，分别为 35,053 枚和 20,000 枚 ETH。
- 2023 年： 转入 15,000 枚 ETH，并有 1,700 枚 ETH 的出售记录。
- 2024 年： 再次转入 35,000 枚 ETH。基金会当时明确表示，钱包转移不等于出售。
- 2025 年： 出现 5,000 枚、10,000 枚 ETH 的出售记录，同时还有 5,000 枚及 10,000 枚 ETH 的出售计划或预告。
- 2026 年： 先后出现 2,785 枚、1,000 枚及近期 2,000 枚 ETH 的出售记录，另有 5,000 枚 ETH 的预告。

需要注意，历史上累计超过 10 万枚 ETH 的大额转入不能直接计入卖出总量，部分交易属于钱包迁移或资金管理；2026 年部分卖出记录也来自关联钱包的链上归因，并非每笔都有基金会同步公告。

从早期的大额资产转移，到近年来通过链上交易及 CoW Swap 等方式管理资金，以太坊基金会的 ETH 资金管理方式一直在变化。

但在 ETH 跌破 2,000 美元、市场流动性承压之际，基金会关联地址的持续卖出，显然会进一步放大市场对抛压的关注。

RCBC ranks among the largest privately owned universal banks in the Philippines, with $23 Billion USD in total assets as of and 471 branches.

Incoming stablecoins convert into U.S. dollars automatically when they arrive. The freelancer never manages a crypto wallet and ends up with a dollar balance at a regulated bank.

I think accepting inbound stablecoins with automatic conversion by outside firms is the most practical first stablecoin product for an Asian bank, and the open question is how the bank screens the origin of funds that arrive from a blockchain.

Whatever people think of Jensen Huang’s personal choices, the lesson he leaves behind still stands: over time, a company that lets its partners do well tends to do well itself.

Nvidia and TSMC have worked together for 30 years on trust rather than contracts. Speaking of TSMC in Lex Fridman’s video “Visiting Taiwan w/ Jensen Huang” (https://t.co/82pREEoPbh), Jensen said: “For the whole time, 30 years, they’ve been jumping through hoops for us.”

His rule was a simple one: always leave something on the table for partners.

The spy allegations remain unproven. The ecosystem he built on that principle is real, and it is likely to outlast this headline.
author: edgeX_KF
quoted_text:
NVIDIA letting Jensen go is a huge mistake, for America and for humanity. It's Apple firing Steve Jobs all over again, but much bigger, given the role of AI in defining the future of our world.

I've been keeping quiet on this out of respect for Jensen's family and team, who I've met and who are amazing humans, and because I personally hate infidelity. So my heart goes out to them in this difficult personal family moment.

But I can also say that Jensen is human, and makes mistakes like all of us do. Not that I matter at all, but I've known Jensen for a long time and have gotten the chance to spend a lot of time with him, behind the scenes, away from mics and cameras. I have seen him show kindness, humility, care to everyone around him, including strangers, including from the poorest most struggling parts of society, treating all the same with the same thoughtfulness and attention, because they are fellow humans and not because he has something to gain from them. That shows rare character, to maintain humility and humanity through all of it.

Another data point is what people who know him well have said privately to me about Jensen over the years. I've never had anyone tell me anything but how awesome he is or how much they love him. Probably over a thousand people at this point. This includes hundreds of engineers, CEOs, colleagues, friends, etc.

Also, since there was some spy talk. Jensen is as proud  an American as it gets. I'm in shock frankly at all of this, including the mass hysteria around it. I love America, and I think NVIDIA letting Jensen go is terrible for America.

I stand with Jensen.

Love you all ❤️

text:
Bitcoin retreated on Thursday as renewed unease over technology stocks weighed on risk appetite, with persistent U.S. spot ETF withdrawals adding pressure. The cryptocurrency fell as much as 1.4 percent and traded near $73,500, while other digital assets weakened alongside U.S. stock futures. 

Those futures came under strain as leadership turmoil at Nvidia dragged on the AI trade that has supported risk appetite this year. Nvidia shares slumped as much as 10 percent after reports that the company is seeking potential replacements for CEO Jensen Huang amid accounts of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected of spying for China.

The decline extends a faltering recovery from Bitcoin’s 2026 low below $58,000 in July. Earlier in the week it hit a three-month low after hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data raised odds of further Federal Reserve rate increases. 

Spot Bitcoin ETFs have now seen five consecutive sessions of net outflows totaling roughly $1.44 billion, with nearly $300 million exiting on the latest day. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for most of the redemptions as institutions trimmed exposure. Although cumulative inflows since launch remain large, the streak has pushed year-to-date flows negative for the first time in 2026 and highlighted weak fresh demand.

Macro conditions reinforce the caution. October CPI rose 0.4 percent month-over-month, exceeding forecasts and leaving core measures elevated. Markets price a high probability of another quarter-point Fed hike in December, with some even contemplating a larger move if pressures persist. Treasury yields have risen, at times approaching 5 percent, tightening conditions and raising the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets. 

Stronger jobs data and a firmer dollar have added to the restraint. In this setting Bitcoin has behaved more like a high-beta risk asset than a pure store of value, moving closely with technology stocks and reacting sharply to any AI-narrative setback.

MSCI’s removal of Strategy, the largest corporate Bitcoin holder, from its global equity benchmarks has added further pressure by raising the prospect of forced stock selling and questions about leveraged accumulation strategies. Selling has been more concentrated in derivatives, even as spot activity has shown relative resilience.

Looking ahead, Bitcoin’s path will depend on inflation persistence, Federal Reserve policy, and the stability of the technology-led risk trade. Continued sticky prices and further hikes would keep higher real yields and tighter liquidity in place, potentially testing lower supports if ETF outflows continue and leverage is reduced. 

Resolution of the Nvidia issues combined with cooling inflation that allows the Fed to pause would improve the backdrop and could reopen inflows into ETFs and corporate treasury demand. Near-term producer-price data and Fed commentary will be watched for December signals. Until inflation shows durable progress toward target and institutional demand returns, Bitcoin is likely to stay sensitive to equity risk sentiment and monetary-policy expectations, with its recovery remaining fragile.

Nebius customers are now paying more than the full cost of the build up front.

On deals signed in Q3, prepayments covered over 100% of the capex behind them. In Q2 it was 50% to 60%.

More than 90% of the contract value signed in the quarter came with a prepayment, and customers have committed over $12B since the start of Q3.

A lot of people have been asking how the buildout gets paid for. This is a big part of the answer. When capacity is this tight, the customer pays for the GPUs, the data centre and the networking before it starts using them.

For 2027 they expect prepayments and financing against existing investment grade contracts to cover 75% to 85% of $40B to $45B of capex.

In my opinion this is what a supply constrained market looks like from the inside

📊 How Have Token Unlocks Affected Crypto Prices Over 6 Months?

Over the past six months, token performance has varied significantly depending on how much new supply entered circulation. The chart divides 50 altcoins into four groups based on token unlocks and price returns.

Organic Winners: Tokens with relatively low unlocks and positive returns. $NEAR gained 131%, followed by $MET at 65% and $ETHFI at 40%, despite less than 20% additional circulating supply.

Supply Absorbed: Tokens with substantial unlocks that still recorded positive returns. $BTW surged 5,735%, while $AGT gained 427% and $BR 213%, suggesting that buying pressure outweighed the impact of new supply.

Weak Demand: Tokens with limited unlocks but negative returns. $SOL declined 14%, $AVAX 16%, and $APT 50%, indicating that restricted supply growth alone was insufficient to support prices.

Unlock Pressure: Tokens combining substantial unlocks with negative returns. $2Z fell 82%, $0G 74%, and $OPEN 53%, highlighting the potential impact of supply expansion when demand fails to keep pace.

text:
Arca CIO Jeff Dorman says the fat protocol thesis fueled a decade of mispricing: the real value is in apps, not L1s

"No, I wouldn't say crypto tokens are overvalued. I would say all layer 1 smart contract platform tokens are overvalued."

"There's plenty of incredibly undervalued crypto tokens at the application layer that are generating a ton of revenue and fees relative to the actual market caps."

"Hyperliquid is doing $70 to $100 million per month, right? You slap a 25 times, 20 times multiple on that. Now you do have a $20 to $25 billion token."

"Same with Pump[.]fun. Pump[.]fun did $50 million. You annualize that, that's $600 million."

"You get a token with a $1.5 billion market cap that's doing $600 million of annualized revenue and using 50% for buybacks. You can do the same thing with Aerodrome and Sky and all these other DeFi platforms."

"The reality is the fat protocol thesis, which was intellectually interesting 10 years ago by Joel Monegro and I think Chris Burniske, was so flat out wrong and has shaped 10 years of misinformation and miscalculations in this space."

"The value does not accrue to the layer one protocol. It accrues to the applications built upon these protocols."

text:
没想到，黄仁勋走了才一天，华盛顿先慌了。

这次的民主党干的事实在太极端了，上来就玩这么大，先是议员直接喊停AI建设，再对黄仁勋重拳出击，都引起美股的大幅下跌。

如今参议院军事委员会首席民主党人 Jack Reed 公开要求国会评估英伟达是不是大到不能倒，出事会不会传到美国银行和信贷市场？

他的理由是，英伟达用复杂的融资安排给整个 AI 生态兜了底。

这个底有多大，我翻了下公开数字，判断了一下事情的严重程度

俄亥俄 OpenAI 数据中心项目，分阶段担保 1,050 亿美元。

华尔街 5,000 亿美元算力信贷计划，英伟达最多兜底 1,250 亿。

向云厂商承诺最多采购 360 亿美元云服务。

哥大商学院教授估算，这类承诺加起来大约 4,000 亿美元。

负责签这些单子的人(黄仁勋)，刚刚下台了。

华尔街日报爆料，今年 8 月黄仁勋就因为这类担保方案数落过 Kress，说她只是个报数的会计。现在接手这摊子的，正是 Kress。

更有意思的是，据纽约时报，特朗普周二还打电话劝黄仁勋为这个位置争一争。彭博说他扛了几周，周三深夜无条件投降，嘴里只剩无所谓和我不在乎。

想留他的人，比他自己还多。

那英伟达会不会倒？没了黄仁勋英伟达还行不行，但它已经变成一个严重的政治问题。

英伟达在银行意义上谈不上大到不能倒。它不怕挤兑，芯片照样有人买，4,000 亿承诺对比 4 万亿左右的市值，也就一成。

会传导的地方在下游。英伟达给新云厂商兜底，新云厂商借债买卡，借的钱来自私募信贷和银行。

股价上已经传导了。英伟达连跌 6 周，2012 年以来最长，10 月初以来跌了 29%，蒸发约 1.6 万亿美元，丢掉市值第一掉到苹果后面。

接下来需要关注的三件事，影响后续事态会不会升级。

1、众议院三个委员要求黄仁勋出席闭门听证，再不答应就发传票。

2、商务部长卢特尼克已经同意去国会作证，议员要问政府事先知道多少

3、新加坡时间 11 月 18 日早上 5:20 财报，市场预期营收 1,089 亿美元，同比增长 91%，财报是否能消解一部分市场的顾虑，离开了黄仁勋的英伟达还会是英伟达吗？电话会议上会有我们想关注的信息

NVIDIA letting Jensen go is a huge mistake, for America and for humanity. It's Apple firing Steve Jobs all over again, but much bigger, given the role of AI in defining the future of our world.

I've been keeping quiet on this out of respect for Jensen's family and team, who I've met and who are amazing humans, and because I personally hate infidelity. So my heart goes out to them in this difficult personal family moment.

But I can also say that Jensen is human, and makes mistakes like all of us do. Not that I matter at all, but I've known Jensen for a long time and have gotten the chance to spend a lot of time with him, behind the scenes, away from mics and cameras. I have seen him show kindness, humility, care to everyone around him, including strangers, including from the poorest most struggling parts of society, treating all the same with the same thoughtfulness and attention, because they are fellow humans and not because he has something to gain from them. That shows rare character, to maintain humility and humanity through all of it.

Another data point is what people who know him well have said privately to me about Jensen over the years. I've never had anyone tell me anything but how awesome he is or how much they love him. Probably over a thousand people at this point. This includes hundreds of engineers, CEOs, colleagues, friends, etc.

Also, since there was some spy talk. Jensen is as proud  an American as it gets. I'm in shock frankly at all of this, including the mass hysteria around it. I love America, and I think NVIDIA letting Jensen go is terrible for America.

I stand with Jensen.

Love you all ❤️

黄仁勋被动的根源就是 $NVDA 是一人一票，他只持股约 3-4%。扎克伯格用 10 倍投票权的 B 股，谷歌的佩奇布林用 20 倍，马斯克干脆持股够多。如果上市前就设计好超级投票权，即使后来不断融资、稀释，你仍然可能掌握多数投票权。极端版是设一股黄金股，让你对某些重大事项拥有一票否决权。

2. 治理章程设计
分级董事会，董事分三批、每批三年任期，让敌意改组至少要拖两到三年。普通决议可能只需要超过50%的投票权就能通过，但你可以在章程里规定：重大事项必须获得80%-90%的投票权同意。这样投资人即使掌握了70%的投票权，也无法单独通过某些决议。

3. 三道保险：业绩、股东基础、离场成本
业绩够好：要让董事会觉得，踢掉你是一笔非常昂贵、风险很大的买卖。业绩是终极护城河：让公司离不开你。

提前培养自己的支持者：不要让公司的投票权全部掌握在陌生投资机构手里。让核心员工成为股东，寻找认同公司长期投资者。

黄金降落伞：让踢掉你的经济成本变高，提前设置巨额补偿、股票期权提前归属，让市场和客户把你离开定价为重大利空。

黄仁勋其实业绩做的最好，但他没做第 1、2 条，所以董事会随时能动他。造成了最尴尬的结局：公司成功了，创始人下岗了🤣
