The Market Is Quiet, So Let's Talk About $Jacket

0xb82535e74b03ffe4910efea1c759b6bbbf0a7777 

The main question surrounding JACKET is actually quite simple: now that Jensen Huang has left NVIDIA, could his iconic black leather jacket become a new cultural symbol of the AI era?

First, let's establish an important fact: on November 12, 2026, NVIDIA officially announced that Jensen Huang had stepped down as CEO, President, and a member of the board of directors. CFO Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO, while the board is searching for a permanent successor.

There have also been media reports about internal employee efforts to persuade Jensen to stay. One internal discussion reportedly received more than 1,600 comments, with many employees expressing support for his return. However, another widely circulated letter allegedly signed by hundreds of employees, demanding the collective resignation of the board, has not been authenticated. Its wording was also found to closely resemble the public letter NVIDIA employees sent to the board in 2023.

Elon also responded to a post suggesting that Jensen should be hired, saying, "That would be an honor."

These details are important because they determine whether JACKET's future price action will be driven by genuine developments in the news or by narratives amplified through social media.

My view is that JACKET has gained a very strong narrative window in the short term. The real question is whether, after Jensen leaves NVIDIA, his iconic black leather jacket can evolve from a personal symbol associated with NVIDIA into a broader cultural symbol of the AI era.

This is a double-edged sword for JACKET. Jensen's career change has brought him back into the media spotlight, but it has also pushed the project's original association with NVIDIA into a period of uncertainty.

In July this year, a black leather jacket worn by Jensen was sold at auction for approximately $960,000, 16 times its estimated value. This shows that the jacket has developed cultural significance far beyond that of an ordinary piece of clothing. What JACKET is doing is bringing this real-world symbol on-chain.

Jensen's departure from NVIDIA has brought renewed attention to this symbol. I see two potential developments worth watching: first, whether internal efforts at NVIDIA to persuade him to return will continue to grow and potentially lead to his comeback; second, whether he might join Elon’s company or another AI project.

If there are genuine developments in his career, Jensen's personal image and that iconic black jacket could once again become major topics of discussion. Elon's public statement, in particular, gives this story the potential to extend beyond an internal leadership change at NVIDIA and into the next chapter of the AI industry.

However, I wouldn't treat these possibilities as events that have already happened. Whether Jensen returns to NVIDIA depends on the board and his own decision. There is also no confirmed news about him joining another AI project. For JACKET, these are potential catalysts, not benefits that have already materialized.

Looking at the token's own mechanics, buys and sells are each subject to a 1% tax. Through Flap's reward mechanism, eligible holders receive NVDAB distributions. The website currently sets the eligibility requirement at holding at least 10,000 JACKET.

This means the project is doing more than simply turning Jensen's black leather jacket into a meme. It is also trying to connect token ownership with rewards in tokenized assets related to NVIDIA.

The potential upside from here mainly comes from three directions: continued discussion surrounding Jensen's future career moves; new attention generated by Elon or other influential figures in the AI industry; and the possibility of the black jacket evolving from a personal symbol associated with NVIDIA into a broader cultural symbol of the AI era.

If Jensen starts a new AI venture, this iconic piece of clothing that has accompanied him for so long could gain a new narrative, without being entirely dependent on NVIDIA.

The risks are equally clear: JACKET is heavily dependent on Jensen's public image. Once the news cycle moves on, attention could fade quickly.

My overall view on JACKET is that it currently has a strong event-driven narrative window. But what is really worth betting on is not Jensen's resignation from NVIDIA itself, but whether this career change can give the black leather jacket a new cultural life.

I'll continue watching two signals: whether Jensen makes any clear moves regarding his next career step, and whether the community continues creating content around the black jacket beyond the current news cycle. The former determines whether the narrative gets fresh fuel; the latter determines whether the meme has a life of its own.

If Jensen really does begin a new chapter in the AI industry, that black leather jacket may become more than just a symbol of NVIDIA's past. It could become the defining symbol of his next chapter.

That is the possibility JACKET is truly betting on.

quoted_text:
Let me catch you up with what’s happening.

Anonymous leakers spread tabloid narratives about one of America’s most successful men. Spies, blackmail, state secrets! The grain of truth is that the billionaire is not exactly chaste. But the ‘national security’ angle is entirely fabricated by a few anonymous sources misrepresenting the entirety of the Intelligence Community (IC), in order to force through domestic political outcomes.

I’m not talking about November 2026. I’m talking about November 2016 — Russiagate, an unhinged theory that President Trump was secretly working with Putin. These claims took exactly the form of a James Bond movie, alleging that Trump was sleeping with Russian prostitutes, or “honeypots”, that he had been blackmailed by Putin, that he was an agent of the Kremlin. Regardless of Trump’s policy merits, it is an objective fact that these claims were false.

How Russigate took off was simple. Anonymous Intelligence Community leakers laundered false claims from political consultants Fusion GPS and Christopher Steele. That way, even though journalists were repeating lies, they could say they were simply repeating what the Intelligence Community told them. That didn’t mean the entire IC agreed, just that they had one politically weaponized source they could use to advance their narrative.

I’ve asked several intelocutors who believe that Alice Huang is a spy or asset what level of evidence they would expect from a credible claim. The smart ones have asked me the same question. While Russiagate turned out to be false, at the time, its proponents made specific falsifiable claims in order to build up credibility.

The Trump Organization maintained a secret communications channel with Russia's Alfa Bank.
Carter Page secretly coordinated with senior Kremlin officials on behalf of Trump.
Sergei Millian was the source of the dossier's central Trump–Russia conspiracy allegations.
Michael Cohen traveled to Prague to coordinate with Russian operatives.

These were all claims to be investigated. All of these were proven to be objectively false. See part 1 and 4 of the excellent Columbia Journalism Review series on Russiagate.

With the Jensen story, we do not even have these crumbs. The entire premise that Alice Huang is a Chinese spy is an article of faith, spread baselessly without providing specific allegations of how she spied on Jensen or others, let alone proof of those allegations.

Let me be clear about the distinction. Not only does the Alice Huang spy claim have absolutely zero evidence, like the Russiagate claims. Unlike the Russiagate claims, it does not even name specific allegations for which they could have evidence. The fact that the level of accusation does not even rise to the laughably low threshold of Russiagate shows that this is an odious fabrication, a lie that does not even bother to go through the motions of justifying that it could be true, let alone proving it is true.

The lesson these political operatives learned was to avoid trying to build up big lies by small, evidence-based claims. Just go for the sweeping lie and when anyone asks for evidence, call them a traitor.

Now, the broader IC has already overturned the most extreme claims made about Alice Huang, admitting there is "little evidence" and that claims were "premature". But that is not enough. We need to call this what it is: a politically weaponized fabrication without even the most basic pretense of truth.

Russiagate failed. Donald Trump won in 2016. Despite being less credible than the Steele dossier, the Jensen allegations have succeeded, at least temporarily, in removing the CEO of the world’s most valuable company. It is a horrific moment for America.

author: BabakHassibi
quoted_text:
I am saddened to say that Karl Astrom, a towering figue in control theory, and a pioneer of adaptive control, passed away yesterday, Nov 12, at the age of 92. 

I imagine that in this AI-crazed age, with its constant pursuit of "flavor-of-the-month", many may not be aware of his contributions. However, one can draw a clear arc from his work to many of the ideas currently prevalent in machine learning. As early as 1965 he wrote (what I assume is) the first paper on the control of partially-observed Markov decision processes, which play an important role in modern reinforcement learning:

Optimal control of Markov decision processes with incomplete state estimation, J. Math. Anal. Applic., 1965

His landmark paper with Wittenmark lays the foundations for "learning and control":

On self tuning regulators, Automatica, 1973

I have been personally indebted to him in multiple ways.  When I was a second year graduate student I attended the 1993 Institute of Mathematics and its Applications (IMA) Workshop on Adaptive Control in Minnesota that he had been organizing with Graham Goodwin and PR Kumar.  After a brief discussion of some of my research he go so excited that, midway through the workshop, he added me to the program. I got pummeled by the faculty after my talk (even though I was right and they were wrong 😀).

I last saw him two years ago at Lund, where he spent almost all of his career. He was still active, visited the department, and attended talks regularly, always asking pointed questions (though he had to sit in a chair next to the speaker in order to hear!). 

Altogether a remarkably kind and generous human being. A true scholar. RIP Karl.

quoted_text:
🚨 Another major scandal is coming out of NVIDIA.

And this one has nothing to do with Jensen Huang's affairs.

According to a Wall Street Journal report, Nvidia was offering billions in financial guarantees to AI companies that could not afford its chips, so they could keep buying them.

Some of these deals were being pushed by Jensen's own son-in-law, Nico Caprez, who became a vice president in January. His team was telling small cloud companies and data center builders that Nvidia could arrange credit support for them within a couple of weeks.

The goal was simple: turn them into long term buyers of Nvidia GPUs.

And the size of Nvidia's commitments has exploded. Its own filing shows $530 BILLION in commitments and guarantees, up from $184 billion just one quarter earlier.

Inside the company, CFO Colette Kress was raising concerns. She kept asking how these guarantees were priced and what Nvidia was really getting back.

In an August meeting, Jensen cut her off and called her "a deer in the headlights."

She was also the one who cut Nvidia's guarantee on OpenAI's Ohio data center from $250 billion to $105 billion.

Now Jensen is gone, and the CFO who questioned these deals is running Nvidia.

To understand why this is a big deal, you need to understand the AI funding loop.

Here is how it works:

1. Nvidia puts money into an AI company, or guarantees its loans and leases.
2. That company uses the money and credit to build a data center.
3. The data center is filled with Nvidia GPUs.
4. Nvidia reports those GPU sales as revenue.
5. If the company cannot rent out all its computing power, Nvidia agrees to buy the unused part.

SO NVIDIA IS THE INVESTOR, THE LENDER, THE SUPPLIER AND THE BACKUP CUSTOMER, ALL IN THE SAME DEAL.

The money goes out of Nvidia and comes back to Nvidia as sales.

CoreWeave is the clearest example. Nvidia owns a stake in it, sells it chips, and agreed to buy up to $6.3 billion of its unused computing capacity through 2032.

OpenAI is the biggest. Nvidia is guaranteeing up to $105 billion for its Ohio data center, supplying all the chips inside it, and invested $1.5 billion in the company building it.

Nvidia's own filing for the quarter ending July 26 shows where the money is tied up:

• Supply commitments for memory and chip wafers: $279 BILLION, up from $119 billion.
• Guarantee on the OpenAI Ohio data center: up to $105 BILLION.
• Deals to buy unused cloud capacity from neoclouds: $36 BILLION.

Nvidia's actual liabilities on its balance sheet: $91 BILLION.

That means the commitments outside the balance sheet are almost 6 times bigger than the debts on it.

Nvidia does not lose this money unless something breaks. A guarantee only costs Nvidia if a customer cannot pay.

But this is where it gets uncomfortable.

The WSJ says Jensen himself had started to panic. He warned executives that the biggest cloud companies were moving to their own chips to depend less on Nvidia.

At the same time, the wafers and memory Nvidia had committed to buy were coming at him like an "avalanche."

So the biggest customers were trying to leave, Nvidia was locked into buying huge amounts of supply, and smaller customers were being kept alive with Nvidia's credit.

And things were already starting to crack:

• Nvidia paused some of its financing deals in August.
• Nearly half of the $80 billion in data center bonds issued this year were rated junk.
• Neocloud stocks crashed this week, with Nebius down over 20% and CoreWeave down 17% at the lows.
• OpenAI raised less than it wanted, at a lower valuation.

And now Kress is the one deciding whether this continues.

If she pulls back on the financing, the companies that depended on Nvidia's money will have to borrow elsewhere, in a debt market that is already nervous.

If they cannot, they stop buying chips.

And if they stop buying chips, Nvidia's revenue drops.

That is the risk of a loop. It works perfectly when money keeps flowing, and it hurts on the way down.

text:
一个交易思路：长期做空 YZi Labs 系上市代币

1/ 历史怎么说？
2025 年以来，符合“YZi Labs 投资 + 上线币安/Binance Alpha”条件的代币包括：Sign、Plume、Idol、ASP、Chip、OPN、Aster、Bio、Shell、Eden、Sahara、Soph、Sto、Init、Bard、Layer、Baby、K、Brev、Vooi 等。

其中，目前只有 IDOL 的现价高于上市价；PLUME、STO、LAYER 曾有过阶段性行情，表现也算相对不错。
但更多代币走出了近似 rug 级的 K 线，比如 ASP、OPN、BIO、SHELL、EDEN、SOPH、INIT、BABY、K、BREV、VOOI 等。

2/ 为什么长期看必跌？
第一，叙事在上线那一刻就用完了。
“YZi / 币安关联”本身就是巨大的叙事加成，这些预期在上线前和上线时被充分 FOMO，把价格推到高位。而一旦正式上线，利好出尽，价格就失去了继续上行的燃料。

第二，上币安就是 vc 币终局。
对大量 VC 币而言，登陆顶级交易所是团队和早期投资人最大的流动性兑现窗口。说得直白一点，对多数项目来说，上币安的那一刻，它的使命就已经完成了。 

3/ 做空不等于稳赚
需要强调的是，长期看跌 ≠ 做空一定赚钱。
不少项目的下跌并非一泻千里，而是涨涨跌跌、震荡下行。中间任何一个反弹都可能触发爆仓。

4/ 观察工具
我通过 @GeckoTerminal 建了一个观察列表，将上述符合条件的代币纳入追踪：
https://t.co/be7mbazakn 

如果下次再有符合条件的项目上市，说不定可以作为参考。

Just to state the nuances of my opinion: Jensen is irreplaceable to $NVDA.

No other CEO can visit a chicken shop in Korea, noodle shop in Japan

And rally hundred of billions of capital and supply chain commitment into Nvidia’s next technological vision.

As for Nvidia: the their roadmap is intact, their existing commitment and revenues are still preserved under Jensen’s leadership.

They’ll still be around 5-10 years from now, given how fundamentally important they are to AI supply chains. 

Under a new leader they can still continue growing if AI demand is intact and maintain their current lines.

But I don’t know anyone who can possibly think that under anyone else, whether it’s Tim Cook or an accountant:

That Nvidia could compound 70% capacity constrained growth Y/Y, without a leader like Jensen making these transformational bets.

As for AI implications:

I’m heavily bullish directionally, given AI is the most transformational technology in human history.

- I expect some potential slowdown in Nvidia’s ecosystem.

I don’t think an accountant can make the same aggressive level of commitments to Neoclouds or supply chains in Taiwan, Korea, Japan beyond existing architectures.

Then rally the capital and trust to make it happen.

- I do expect the next CEO to be more politically aligned with Washington in restricting China GPU access

- I also see the next CEO being less supportive of open weight models (positive for OpenAI/Anthropic)

- I’m less optimistic on $NVDA maintaining their competitive advantages against $AMD, $AVGO, and hyperscalers.

One person doesn’t break the AI trade, I expect companies from optics to memory to still outperform.

However, my confidence in the next leg of Nvidia’s growth, beyond their current roadmap, has been shaken without Jensen Huang.

text:
The Future of Money Is Being Built, and Most People Haven’t Noticed

In this episode of Drops, I sit down with @EliBenSasson, co-founder of @Zcash, @StarkWareLtd, and @Starknet, to explore why he believes blockchain will become the foundation of how people and AI agents transact. We discuss his journey from academic research to building some of crypto's most influential technologies, the limitations of Bitcoin, the growing importance of financial privacy, and why quantum computing could force the industry to rethink how digital assets are secured.

For Eli, the biggest change happening in crypto has little to do with fluctuating token prices. "This is the future. And most people just don't realize that," he says. "The infrastructure for the global economy is being rebuilt as we speak."

From Abstract Mathematics to Building Zcash

In 2013, Eli was a professor of theoretical computer science working on zero-knowledge proofs, a cryptographic technique that allows someone to prove a statement is true without revealing the underlying information. Although he recognized the mathematical significance of his research, he struggled to identify compelling real-world applications.

That changed when he attended a Bitcoin conference in San Jose. After presenting his work to a relatively small audience, several Bitcoin developers approached him with an unexpected question: "Where's the code?" Eli realized that zero-knowledge proofs could address two fundamental problems facing Bitcoin: privacy and scalability. He eventually co-authored an academic paper proposing privacy improvements for Bitcoin, but when integration proved difficult, he partnered with developers to help create Zcash, a cryptocurrency designed to bring privacy to digital money.

Why Privacy Is Essential to the Future of Money

Bitcoin introduced the possibility of transferring value without relying on a central financial institution, but its public ledger makes it fundamentally incompatible with everyday financial activity. Eli compares this to announcing every purchase you make, including information about how you paid for it.

While transaction transparency can help trace illicit financial activity, it also exposes ordinary users to surveillance and financial profiling. For individuals, privacy protects spending habits and personal financial information. For businesses, it can be essential to maintaining confidentiality around salaries, suppliers, and commercial relationships. Zcash was built to address this problem by allowing transactions to be verified without exposing sensitive details.

Yet widespread appreciation of financial privacy took longer than Eli anticipated. He attributes this to several factors, including Bitcoin's resistance to major changes, the difficulty of using early privacy tools, and regulatory uncertainty surrounding privacy-focused cryptocurrencies. As those conditions have evolved, the need for privacy has become increasingly apparent.

The Quantum Threat and Bitcoin's Resistance to Change

Eli's concerns extend beyond privacy to whether today's blockchains can remain secure in the decades ahead with the threats of quantum computers and advances in artificial intelligence. When asked whether Bitcoin held for another 20 years would remain safe, Eli acknowledges the uncertainty. "I wouldn't say it's 100% safe." His greater concern, however, is Bitcoin's reluctance to change.

Although Bitcoin's conservative approach to upgrades is often seen as a strength, Eli believes it could become a vulnerability if emerging threats require significant modifications. This concern helps explain his work on ZK-STARKs, a class of cryptographic proofs designed to offer scalability and resistance to quantum attacks.

To explain their usefulness, Eli introduces an unusual example involving Darth Vader. Imagine asking Darth Vader to process an entire day's worth of Bitcoin transactions. You wouldn't trust his account of the results. But with a STARK proof, you could independently verify that the computation was performed correctly without repeating all the work. The technology makes it possible to verify complex computations efficiently, without needing to trust whoever performed them, and combining this capability with quantum-resistant cryptography creates a stronger foundation for future financial infrastructure.

Starknet and the Next Evolution of Digital Money

Eli sees Starknet as the next step in a progression that began with Bitcoin. Bitcoin introduced scarce digital money, then Ethereum made digital assets programmable, enabling lending, borrowing, trading, and other financial applications, Zcash added privacy, and Starknet aims to bring these capabilities together while improving scalability, usability, and cryptographic security. Starknet's approach also makes it easier to adopt different security mechanisms without rebuilding the surrounding infrastructure.

His team is also exploring whether Starknet should become an independent Layer 1 blockchain, reducing its reliance on Ethereum and potentially allowing it to respond more quickly to emerging threats. But he acknowledges that technical superiority alone doesn't guarantee adoption, and the market may not ultimately choose Starknet. What he does know is the kind of technology he wants to build is private, programmable, adaptable, and resilient against future security threats.

Why AI Agents Could Accelerate Blockchain Adoption

As AI agents increasingly manage purchases, services, and other economic activities, they will need financial infrastructure that allows them to transact efficiently. Eli argues that blockchains are better suited for these interactions than conventional financial systems, particularly when privacy, scalability, and programmability are built into the underlying infrastructure.
He envisions AI agents adopting blockchain-based payments first, followed by humans and eventually traditional financial institutions. The practical applications are already emerging, with StarkWare supporting confidential stablecoin payrolls, an application that demonstrates how blockchain could eventually be adopted into everyday business operations.

Who Will Control the Digital Economy?

Despite his confidence in the technology, Eli recognizes that centralized systems are convenient, and people may ultimately prefer relying on a handful of powerful corporations rather than managing decentralized alternatives.

He sees a similar possibility emerging in AI, where a small number of companies could come to control the systems people depend on. For Eli, the question extends beyond which blockchain succeeds. It concerns whether the next generation of financial infrastructure will empower individuals or concentrate control in increasingly powerful institutions.

His motivation remains rooted in the same belief that has guided his work for more than a decade: technology should give people greater autonomy. Whether Starknet becomes the dominant platform is ultimately less important to him than the success of decentralized technology itself.

"I just want decentralization, blockchain, the use of good technology that empowers individuals. I want that to win."

他认为，行业需要解决人才流失和代币激励问题，代币化虽然有好处，却不利于长期激励。对于投资机会，Dempsey 指出，部分已完成分发的代币开始体现实际价值，可以从基本面而不只是叙事进行分析。相比之下，一级市场除了新的永续合约 DEX 类项目，愿意尝试新方向的创业者并不多。

next direction for crypto markets..(think beyond tokens)

the gap between expectations and reality is too wide right now. it's high time you accept that tokenised stocks will eat into crypto token trading volume. they're turning you into liquidity for tokenised stocks now. more stock pairings are bad for crypto anarchy if all we're doing is bringing the same old financial markets onchain while abandoning our own ideas.

the only thing which could give us hope of the good old times, when people with zero capital had a chance to make millions, is creating markets where skills and knowledge are rewarded more. that doesn't mean everyone becomes a millionaire. it means people should have a way to build a better life through what they learn, create, and contribute.

markets where humans are pushed to explore more hobbies and interests, where their niche skills could help them earn a living during the tough times ahead. someone learning music, teaching coding, organising a local community, or helping others finish a project should have opportunities to earn through those contributions.

it's time for people to learn better coordination and fulfil their commitments. crypto could enable this at a much larger scale through shared funds, transparent rules, and rewards tied to verified outcomes. but putting a commitment onchain means little unless we can verify the work, handle disputes, and stop people from gaming the rewards.

imagine markets where people commit to learning, building, or solving something together. milestones unlock rewards. repeated contributions build reputation. breaking commitments carries consequences, with room for genuine setbacks.

when you build markets around this, you give more people a reason to participate beyond buying a token and waiting for someone else to buy it higher.

such markets are called human commitment markets.

Nvidia is nothing without its people.

It now appears the national security allegations may be as fake as Russiagate. If so, Nvidia employees, shareholders, partners, and customers have immense leverage.

Whether publicly or privately, collectively or individually, they can approach the members of the board that precipitously pushed for Jensen’s resignation and instead demand that anti-Jensen board members resign.

Else mass employee resignations may follow, as may shareholder, partner, and customer suits against anti-Jensen board members for breaching their fiduciary duty. Because the value of Nvidia as an economic entity — for its employees, shareholders, partners, and customers — is obviously far higher if the founder and CEO of what was the most valuable company in world history is reinstated and this coup is defeated.

Trillions in capital, the fate of open weight AI, and the global economy itself all hang in the balance. So: if you are e/acc, if you are a techno-optimist, if you support open weight models, or if you just want to rectify a gross injustice — it is legitimate for you to politely press the Nvidia board with every tool at your disposal to reinstate Jensen Huang.

Remember how much capital is at stake. For many parties, it’d be worth it to spend millions — or even billions — on any legally permissible tactic that can get anti-Jensen board members to reverse their votes and then step down.

Remember also: the kind of spineless NPC board member that would vote against Jensen Huang due to a bad news cycle would likely buckle if subject to even 1/1000 of the scrutiny that poor Jensen has been subject to.

Mechanically: step one is to do citizen journalism to determine how each board member voted. Step two is to get the anti-Jensen board members to resign. And step three is the return of the king.

OpenAI shows it can be done. There are after all just a few human beings who need to change their anti-Jensen votes, or step down, or both. Their names and duties are public. And they’re meant to be accountable to the shareholders.

This analysis by @gemchange_ltd is as good a place as any to start.

author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
Nvidia is nothing without its people.

It now appears the national security allegations may be as fake as Russiagate. If so, Nvidia employees, shareholders, partners, and customers have immense leverage.

Whether publicly or privately, collectively or individually, they can approach the members of the board that precipitously pushed for Jensen’s resignation and instead demand that anti-Jensen board members resign.

Else mass employee resignations may follow, as may shareholder, partner, and customer suits against anti-Jensen board members for breaching their fiduciary duty. Because the value of Nvidia as an economic entity — for its employees, shareholders, partners, and customers — is obviously far higher if the founder and CEO of what was the most valuable company in world history is reinstated and this coup is defeated.

Trillions in capital, the fate of open weight AI, and the global economy itself all hang in the balance. So: if you are e/acc, if you are a techno-optimist, if you support open weight models, or if you just want to rectify a gross injustice — it is legitimate for you to politely press the Nvidia board with every tool at your disposal to reinstate Jensen Huang.

Remember how much capital is at stake. For many parties, it’d be worth it to spend millions — or even billions — on any legally permissible tactic that can get anti-Jensen board members to reverse their votes and then step down.

Remember also: the kind of spineless NPC board member that would vote against Jensen Huang due to a bad news cycle would likely buckle if subject to even 1/1000 of the scrutiny that poor Jensen has been subject to.

Mechanically: step one is to do citizen journalism to determine how each board member voted. Step two is to get the anti-Jensen board members to resign. And step three is the return of the king.

OpenAI shows it can be done. There are after all just a few human beings who need to change their anti-Jensen votes, or step down, or both. Their names and duties are public. And they’re meant to be accountable to the shareholders.

This analysis by @gemchange_ltd is as good a place as any to start.

text: @varun_mathur No. Jensen was forced to resign with a metaphorical gun to his head. See below.
author: balajis
quoted_text:
No. There’s no way this was voluntary.

What likely happened is: Jensen was given an ultimatum by 6 of 10 board members: either resign his CEO role *and* his board seat, or be formally removed[1] from his CEO role by 6 of 10 board members. The latter path is messier, and they hit him at a psychological low point, like they hit Travis Kalanick. So he did it under duress.

But now…the world is starting to realize how much damage the anti-Jensen board members caused to shareholders. And leverage has flipped. 

I mean, look. If it was just a “voluntary” resignation then the board could reinstate him tomorrow and he’d accept. In reality the anti-Jensen board members will need to flip or resign for that to happen. And so, legal pressure will be applied.

[1]: See sections 29 and 32 of the SEC filing on Nvidia’s bylaws. They say officers can be removed by a majority of directors at any time: https://t.co/n2yM5HkYL6

@termix_ai 最近提出了 C724 安全 Agent 的方向，希望让 agent 7×24 小时看着钱包授权和异常资金流，出问题先报警，必要时在事先约定的范围内做一些应急处理。它还只是倡议，并没有一个「装上就安全」的现成产品。

我自己现在让 AI 碰资金，也是这么做的。查数据、整理风险、起草操作都可以交给 AI，但每笔实际转出都得我点头。

真要做安全 agent，麻烦的地方不是教它识别异常，而是识别错了怎么办。只会报警，等人看到可能已经晚了；让它自动撤销授权、暂停操作，又可能误伤正常业务。哪些地址能碰、什么条件才触发、动作怎么复核，这些得在上线前讲清楚。

普通人现在能做的，反倒是先弄清自己钱包上已经留了什么权限。ERC-20 代币花费额度可以在 https://t.co/LNpmFfJgnF 查看和撤销；EIP-7702 账户委托是另一回事，https://t.co/LNpmFfJgnF 能展示，但通常需要从钱包自己的官方入口解除。换密码、卸载 App，也不会把链上的授权抹掉。

等 C724 真做出来，我最想看的不是宣传里能防住多少攻击，而是它误报一次时，会不会擅自替我动钱。

<젠슨 황의 사임, 그러나 협력은 계속 됩니다>

젠슨 황 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)의 사임 소식을 접했습니다. 젠슨 황과는 경주 APEC과 AI 생태계 리셉션, 샌프란시스코 AI 선언 행사 등에서 만나 한국의 AI 산업 발전과 협력에 대해 여러 차례 이야기를 나눴습니다. 

사임 소식 이후 여러 분께서 GPU 공급과 협력 사업이 예정대로 진행되는지 물으셨습니다. 오늘 오전 과기정통부 제2차관 주재로 엔비디아 측과 현안점검회의를 열었습니다. 이 자리에서 첨단 GPU 26만 장 공급과 국내 기업과의 협력을 엔비디아가 회사 차원에서 기존 발표대로 추진할 계획임을 재확인했습니다.

NVLink를 활용한 국산 AI 반도체와 엔비디아 플랫폼 간 연계, AI 컴퓨팅 인프라 구축, 피지컬 AI 공동연구와 인재 양성, 엔비디아 개발자 행사인 GTC의 한국 개최 추진 등 양측이 논의해 온 과제도 계속 추진하기로 했습니다.

정부의 GPU 5만 장 확보 계획도 예정대로 진행하고 있습니다. 정부가 직접 확보할 약 3만 5천 장 가운데 현재까지 약 2만 1천 장 규모를 확보했으며, 나머지 약 1만 4천 장 규모는 2027년 초까지 입고될 예정입니다. 두 수치는 B200 연산량 기준입니다. 별도로 1만 5천 장은 국가AI컴퓨팅센터를 통해 확보중입니다.

정부는 국내외 기업·기관과 긴밀히 협력하며 공공과 민간의 GPU 수급을 계속 점검하겠습니다. 확보한 GPU는 기업·대학·연구기관의 AI 연구개발과 독자 AI 파운데이션 모델, 모두의 AI 등 정부 사업에 필요한 시기에 활용할 수 있도록 하겠습니다.

We are nearing the beginning of the end of the short-term, gambling-era mindset of the frontend as the average user’s net worth continues to get pillaged by adverse business models and dark patterns.

We are on the cusp of the next era of the frontend. One that prioritizes informed traders. One that makes rPnL of its average/median user one of its key success metrics and not short-term top-line revenue or buybacks.

Every frontend will need the market intelligence layer for onchain finance.

先日、FacebookやInstagramを運営するメタ社に裁判で負けてしまいました。

判決についてざっくり説明すると、

僕：「僕の写真が使われた詐欺広告がめちゃくちゃ出てるんですけど、ちゃんと事前審査したり消したりしてくださいよ。」

メタ：「それなりにやってますよ。けど100%廃絶するのは不可能なんです。」

裁判所：「まあ、それなりにメタ社は努力してるみたいなので、違反ではないですね。前澤さんの言い分は取り下げます。」

僕：「えーーー。ちゃんとやってるとは思えないんですけど。まあ、いいや。いったんそれはおいておいて。じゃあ仮に詐欺広告が原因で実際に被害を受けてお金を騙し取られた人が出てしまった場合、メタ社には何の責任もないんですか？広告料をもらって、詐欺広告を出しちゃったのはメタ社ですよね？」

メタ：「うちはあくまでも投稿する人や広告を打つ人に場所を貸すだけのプラットフォーマーなので、詐欺広告を減らす努力はするものの、出ちゃったらそれはうちでは責任負えないんです。」

裁判所：「まあ、それも仕方ないですね。悪いのは詐欺を働く人であって、プラットフォーマーには法律上の責任はないですからね。」

僕：「そうなんですね。何の責任もないんですね。詐欺広告出してお金もらってるのに、被害者が出ても知らんぷりなのか。僕、何度も何度も詐欺広告だから消してくれって陳情しましたが、全然消してくれずに詐欺の被害が出たのに。なんかなぁー。。。」

という判決でした。

今後、僕は以下2点について、さらに問いたいし、議論したいと思います。

①メタ社は本当に詐欺広告を減らす努力をしていたのか？（何度通報しても「これは違反ではない」と返ってきたりしてたよね？）

②仮に詐欺広告が出てしまい、それによる被害が発生した場合、プラットフォーマーには何の責任もない、ということで本当によいのか？（もう法律変えるしかない？）

みなさんはどう思いますか？

text:
Have been surprised to see so many people debate the “spy” element of Jensen’s affair.  

IMO, it’s irrelevant for specific reasons.  Large Chinese companies have shadow CCP executives.  Chinese law requires all Chinese citizens to act as spies on request (to assist in state intelligence gathering, by law.)  China is openly a surveillance state that does their best to aggregate all corporate data.  

I’d lay 10:1 that notes from Alice’s meetings went to Beijing…because most notes from large corporate exec meetings do.  

A separate question is if Alice was pressuring Jensen for chips on her own behalf, that of Beijing, or that of other competing Chinese governmental entities like the PLA.  Evidence today points to a mix of for her own benefit and some powerful connected interests in China.  

All of this is meant as an aside, largely tangential to the bigger picture.  

Imo, Jensen was ousted as a power play by China hawks and Anthropic, but their ammunition was NVIDIA’s possible skirting of export controls.  I think the infidelities mostly sped up the timeline.

text: TIL there is an accepted methodology for valuing the Internet....Ethereum is undervalued if you apply the same framework...
author: lex_node
quoted_text:
Ethereum generates about $5.7 trillion of value for the economy built on it.
The market prices ETH at $246 billion. That’s 4.3% of it.

Today I’m publishing the second edition of my annual Ethereum-as-infrastructure valuation report. Here’s the essence of it.

1/ Ethereum is a public good, so value it like one
Nobody can buy shares in TCP/IP, yet the Internet is the most valuable infrastructure ever built. Its protocols charge almost nothing. Their value shows up everywhere except in their own revenues.

Ethereum is in the same position. Valuing it by its fees, or comparing it to a company, misses most of what it does. Last year I argued it should be valued the way we value the Internet: through what it enables, not what it charges.

2/ Three buckets, like the Internet
The Internet’s value comes in three parts: the companies built on it, the economic activity it carries, and the surplus people get for free. Ethereum maps onto the same three:

a) Ecosystem value: the assets and companies built on Ethereum, at market prices. $127B.
b) Flow value: the economic activity Ethereum settles, mainly stablecoins, plus trading, lending and tokenized assets. $70T a year of dependent flows, worth $3.0T.
c) Trust surplus: what users would pay for trust in the traditional system, minus what they pay on Ethereum. Custody, reconciliation, settlement delays, counterparty risk. Worth $2.6T.

Add a small credit for the EVM standard used by other chains, and Ethereum’s system value comes to about $5.7 trillion.

3/ Every rate is anchored to something real
I didn’t want numbers that look picked to land somewhere. So:

Ethereum is credited by using Visa’s take on the payments it carries, about 0.3%. Visa is the richest settlement network on earth, so that’s a ceiling, not an average.
The trust cost removed is 25 basis points, weighted toward wholesale settlement rather than expensive retail payments.
Annual values are capitalized at 7%, assuming Ethereum’s activity never grows from today. For a network that has grown every year, that’s deliberately conservative.

4/ ETH’s market cap is the benchmark, not part of the total
This is the biggest change from last year. Counting ETH inside the total would double count. So the model compares what Ethereum enables with what the market pays for ETH.

For every $1 the market pays for ETH, Ethereum generates about $23 of value for the ecosystem built on it.

5/ But ETH shouldn’t be worth all of it
Part of that value belongs to others: L2 tokens, DeFi protocols, shares in Robinhood, Circle and Coinbase, a stake in Tether. And public goods never capture everything they enable. That’s the whole point of them.

So the real question is: what share can ETH capture?

The Internet gives us an answer. The companies built on it are worth roughly 10–20% of the economic value it creates. Apply the midpoint, 15%, to Ethereum, and ETH would be worth about $7,000. That’s 3.5× today’s price.

Today the market credits ETH with less than 5%. Under half the low end of the Internet’s range.

6/ The number that’s hardest to argue with
Forget the capitalization multiple entirely. Each year, Ethereum enables about $389 billion of value. That’s 1.6× ETH’s entire market cap.

Ethereum enables more value every year than the market currently pays for ETH in total.

7/ What’s new: a live model you can challenge
This year the report isn’t static. Every figure comes from a live dashboard that refreshes hourly from public sources. You can inspect every input and formula, and use simulation mode to change the assumptions.

I wanted a model anyone could check and challenge. If you disagree with an assumption, change it and see what happens. https://t.co/Qi2z7fjrDo

8/ What it isn’t
It’s not a price target, and it’s not a forecast. It’s a snapshot of today, measuring the gap between what Ethereum enables and what ETH is credited with. Either ETH’s capture of its own ecosystem rises toward Internet-like levels, or the market is pricing in that it never will.

That’s the debate this framework makes explicit.

The Internet reorganized information. Ethereum is reorganizing trust.

Live model: https://t.co/Qi2z7fjrDo
An expanded version will appear in my upcoming book, TRUSTSHIFT: Ethereum and the Reinvention of Trust. https://t.co/5zfc94ppeP

quoted_text:
$8 trillion per day in security transactions are settled by the US Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC).

Thats $2 quadrillion per year in equity and bond trades and transactions.

The DTCC processes over $2 quadrillion (USD) in securities transactions annually through its subsidiaries, primarily the Depository Trust Company (DTC) and the National Securities Clearing Corporation (NSCC). This figure represents the total value of trades settled across various asset classes, including equities, bonds, and other financial instruments.

To estimate a daily amount, we can divide the annual figure by the number of business days in a year, typically around 252 (accounting for weekends and major U.S. holidays when markets are closed). Using the widely cited $2 quadrillion figure:

$2,000,000,000,000,000 (2 quadrillion) ÷ 252 business days ≈ $7,936,507,936,508 per day.

This averages to approximately $7.94 trillion per day. 

However, this is a rough estimate, as settlement volumes fluctuate daily based on market activity, and the DTCC's total includes both high-volume days and quieter periods. The actual daily amount can vary significantly, sometimes exceeding $10 trillion on peak trading days, according to industry discussions and posts found on X referencing DTCC activities.

For context, the DTCC handles over 1.3 million transactions daily through the DTC alone, with additional volumes processed via NSCC’s Continuous Net Settlement (CNS) system. These transactions encompass broker-to-broker trades, institutional deliveries, and other securities movements, settled at the end of each business day, typically around 4:15 p.m. Eastern Time via the Federal Reserve’s National Settlement Service.

IMO: This will all be replaced with a blockchain based solution by 2030.

The hottest companies are now staying private longer and IPOing at higher prices ↓

This has led to private markets capturing the lion's share of new asset growth, effectively locking the public out from this wealth effect."

Apple went public four years after its founding at $.10 and is up over 2,800x in the public market. In the new modern economy, the broader public does not have access to the upside in the American economy.

Apple listed early enough that public markets got most of that 2,800x. Companies today wait until they're worth hundreds of billions, so that growth stays in private rounds.

Accredited investor rules are one wall. The IPO process is the other: a few banks set the price, a few funds get the allocations, and retail buys after the pop.

Opening up who can invest only fixes half of it if the first trade still happens behind closed doors.
author: dopplerprotocol
quoted_text:
I think it’s time to revisit the accredited investor laws in the US.

Companies are staying private longer, where only accredited investors (aka rich people!) can invest. Retail investors can only come in after IPO, when much of the upside has already been captured.

These rules were created with the best of intentions, to protect regular people from scams - a noble idea. Unfortunately, in practice they've often made it illegal to get richer, unless you're already rich. A regressive tax!

We have to judge policies based on their outcomes, not on their intentions.

These are two possible routes I see:

1) Replace the rule with something merit-based, like a financial literacy test. Pass it and you're accredited. Having a qualification based on competency rather than your bank balance or income seems far more fair.

2) Remove the rule entirely. Let consenting adults assess their own risk. Disclosure requirements stay and fraud enforcement stays to punish bad actors.

go pull any 2018 or 2021 alt chart. down 99%, most of them delisted from binance. somebody was selling the whole way down (founders, team, early investors, the same cast of characters, same supply control, same backroom deals as today). 

some of these projects raised hundreds of millions on ico’s.

i'll use myself as an example. i was in the skycoin cult. took me about a year to notice and not brush off  the red flags and another six months to admit it was a straight up scam and get out. 

because the info from the team dripped out slowly. an interview every three months, a product update here and there, and in between i sat in a telegram room with the other bag holders talking ourselves into how great the project was. well, it was a slow rug. we were frogs in the slow boiling pot of water. 

i do think some of these projects actually wanted to solve problems and build cool things, but just were way over ambitious and couldn’t deliver on their promises. others were probly more brazen of a scam.

Prediction markets make it cheaper to get skin in the game and the output is better information and more truth

text:
摩根大通最新持仓曝光：狂砍台积电、美光，却对这几只AI龙头下重注！

减持
1. 美光 $MU
存储行业周期性较强，价格和盈利容易受到供需变化影响，小摩本季选择降低存储芯片敞口，可能是在锁定部分利润。

2. 西部数据 $WDC
全球存储设备供应商，受益于AI数据中心扩张和存储需求增长。但存储行业具有明显周期性，盈利容易受到产品价格和库存变化影响。

3. 闪迪 $SNDK
NAND闪存领域的重要厂商，受益于AI服务器和数据中心存储需求。不过行业竞争和价格周期影响较大，小摩本季选择降低存储产业链配置。

4. 应用材料 $AMAT
全球半导体设备龙头，提供晶圆制造所需的核心设备。虽然AI芯片扩产带来长期需求，但设备订单与晶圆厂资本开支周期密切相关。

5. 康宁 $GLW
全球特种材料巨头，光纤产品受益于AI数据中心建设和高速通信需求。不过相比GPU、云计算等核心环节，业务增长仍受到传统产业周期影响。

6. Ciena $CIEN
光通信设备龙头，数据中心互联和高速光网络是AI基础设施的重要组成部分。不过小摩本季调整了网络设备相关配置，可能是在优化AI硬件产业链内部的投资结构。

7. 台积电 $TSM
全球晶圆代工龙头，是英伟达、AMD等AI芯片公司的核心制造伙伴。虽然AI芯片需求持续增长，但小摩本季仍削减部分代工环节配置，可能更倾向于直接持有AI芯片设计和平台型公司。

8. 德州仪器 $TXN
全球模拟芯片龙头，产品广泛应用于汽车、工业和消费电子领域。业务相对稳定，但增长受到工业和汽车周期影响，AI算力带来的直接弹性相对有限。

9. 亚德诺 $ADI
模拟与混合信号芯片巨头，产品覆盖工业、汽车和通信领域。与AI GPU等核心算力芯片相比，增长驱动力相对分散。

10. 特斯拉 $TSLA
电动车与自动驾驶领域的代表企业，拥有FSD自动驾驶和机器人等长期增长故事。不过汽车业务竞争激烈，估值和宏观消费环境敏感度较高。

11. 沃尔玛 $WMT
全球零售巨头，拥有强大的供应链和规模优势，业务现金流稳定。不过在本轮组合调整中，小摩削减部分零售消费配置，将资金向其他增长领域重新分配。

12. 麦当劳 $MCD
全球餐饮连锁巨头，品牌和加盟体系优势明显，现金流稳定。不过消费增长相对成熟，小摩本季降低相关消费板块配置。

13. 劳氏 $LOW
美国大型家居建材零售商，业务与房地产、住房装修及消费者支出密切相关。受住房市场和利率环境影响较大，小摩本季削减相关仓位。

14. 迪士尼 $DIS
全球娱乐传媒巨头，拥有影视、流媒体和主题乐园等业务。不过内容制作成本、流媒体盈利和消费支出都会影响业绩，小摩本季降低相关消费娱乐敞口。

15. iShares标普500 ETF $IVV
跟踪标普500指数的宽基ETF，覆盖美国大型上市公司。小摩本季减持，可能是在调整被动指数配置，将资金重新分配到主动选择的个股。

16. Vanguard标普500 ETF $VOO
另一只跟踪标普500指数的核心ETF。与IVV类似，本季减持可能体现组合主动管理比例提升，减少部分宽基指数配置。

17. 苹果 $AAPL
全球消费电子与软件生态巨头，iPhone、Mac和服务业务构成强大的商业护城河。虽然AI功能逐步落地，但消费电子增长和估值仍是需要关注的因素，小摩本季小幅减持。

18. 联合健康 $UNH
美国医疗保险与医疗服务巨头，拥有庞大的医疗服务网络。不过医疗保险定价、医疗成本和政策监管压力增加，小摩本季降低相关医疗保健敞口。

19. 艾伯维 $ABBV
全球生物制药巨头，拥有免疫学和肿瘤等核心业务。面临药物专利到期、产品竞争和药品定价压力，小摩本季调整相关医药仓位。

20. 默沙东 $MRK
全球制药巨头，拥有肿瘤、疫苗等业务。核心药物专利到期和新产品接棒能力是未来需要关注的问题，小摩本季削减相关配置。

21. Strategy看跌期权 $MSTR Puts
持有Strategy看跌期权，可能用于对冲比特币价格波动及MSTR股价下跌风险。这类期权仓位不等于直接做空股票，需要结合期权名义价值、期限和执行价判断实际风险敞口。

增持
22. 微软 $MSFT
重点增持，持股增加约16.87%。Azure云计算持续发展，Copilot推动AI进入企业办公场景，同时拥有庞大的企业客户基础。相比单纯卖AI芯片，微软还能通过云服务和软件订阅将AI转化为持续收入，是AI商业化最稳健的平台型巨头之一。

23. 英伟达 $NVDA
增持约2.84%。全球AI训练与推理芯片绝对龙头，GPU生态壁垒极高，CUDA构建了强大的开发者生态。随着全球科技巨头持续增加AI资本开支，英伟达依然是AI算力基础设施最核心的受益者。

24. Meta $META
前五大买入标的之一。旗下Facebook、Instagram拥有庞大的用户基础，AI持续提升广告推荐和投放效率，改善广告业务盈利能力。同时，公司持续加大AI基础设施投入，长期有望从AI广告和智能助手商业化中受益。

25. SPDR黄金ETF $GLD
前五大买入标的之一。黄金是机构应对通胀、地缘政治风险和宏观不确定性的传统避险工具。增持黄金ETF，说明小摩在继续配置科技成长资产的同时，也在加强组合的防御能力。

26. Palantir $PLTR
前五大买入标的之一。AI软件与数据分析平台，主要服务政府和企业客户。其优势在于将AI模型真正部署到企业业务流程中，随着企业AI应用从实验走向商业化，平台有望获得更多订单。

27. 亚马逊 $AMZN
增持约6.81%。AWS云计算、电商和广告业务形成三大增长引擎。随着生成式AI带动云计算需求增长，AWS有望成为AI基础设施投资的重要受益者，同时电商和广告业务也提供稳定的现金流。

28. 博通 $AVGO
小幅增持。公司在定制AI芯片ASIC、高速网络芯片领域拥有重要优势。随着大型科技公司开发自研AI芯片，定制ASIC需求持续增长，博通有望成为英伟达之外另一条重要的AI算力投资路线。

29. 谷歌-A $GOOGL
增持约2.39%。搜索、YouTube和Google Cloud构成强大的商业护城河。Gemini模型持续迭代，自研TPU芯片和AI基础设施也在不断完善，AI有望进一步提升搜索广告效率和云业务收入。

30. 谷歌-C $GOOG
小幅增持。与GOOGL一样，代表对Alphabet整体业务的投资。搜索、YouTube、Gemini和Google Cloud构成其AI时代的核心竞争力。

31. 强生 $JNJ
增持医疗保健领域的高确定性龙头。公司业务覆盖制药和医疗器械，产品线多元化，现金流稳定。在组合削减部分医疗股的同时增加强生，体现了医疗板块内部的结构性调整。

32. 礼来 $LLY
增持。全球减肥和糖尿病药物龙头，GLP-1药物市场需求强劲，相关产品具有巨大的商业化潜力。随着减肥药市场持续扩张，礼来有望继续受益于长期医疗需求增长。

33. Strategy $MSTR
增持约36%。通过上市公司间接持有比特币，是美股市场最具代表性的比特币概念股之一。小摩增加MSTR股票敞口，同时持有相关看跌期权，说明其可能在增加比特币相关资产配置的同时管理下行风险。

34. iShares比特币信托 $IBIT
增持约9.6%。贝莱德推出的比特币现货ETF，为机构提供合规、便捷的比特币投资渠道。增持IBIT说明小摩继续增加直接比特币敞口。

35. SPDR标普500 ETF $SPY
小幅增持。作为跟踪标普500指数的核心ETF，提供美国大型企业整体市场敞口。小摩在调整部分宽基ETF仓位的同时，仍保留核心指数配置。

AI 算力继续加码！

BTCS now owes @aave more than before it sold $ETH to cut that loan

BTCS is a Nasdaq-listed company that keeps its treasury in $ETH and borrows against it on Aave

in february it withdrew 10,000 $ETH of its collateral and sold it at a loss, cutting the loan from $62M to $44M

since then it borrowed again and now owes $64M

before that sale, Aave would only start liquidating its collateral after a 33% drop in $ETH

now a drop of about 17% is enough, even though $ETH is a bit higher than in february

BTCS shareholders took that loss and still got a riskier loan

As the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group nears the theatre, tensions between the United States and Iran escalate.

Explosions were reported along Bahrain’s northern coast shortly afterwards.

Iran then announced it had launched two hypersonic ballistic missiles to destroy the AN/TPS-75 long-range early-warning radar deployed by the US at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, in retaliation for the prior US airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik, Iran.

This radar is a critical air-surveillance node for the US in the Persian Gulf and provides long-range area warning for the THAAD missile defence system.

US Central Command denied that the radar had been destroyed. It confirmed Iran launched two drones towards Bahrain, all of which were intercepted and shot down by US forces, with no casualties or damage to facilities.

text:
The issue is of board seat, not as the CEO. Jensen resigned from the board seat as well - the board had absolutely no power to remove him from that. They would have had to call a special shareholder meeting to remove him as a director. 

The 6/10 board vote would only have covered removal as an officer (CEO), not removal from the board as a director. And per the Form 8-K filing, he resigned from everything, there was no vote done. 

4 board members have been on his board since the 1990s, and 2 other since the 2010s - those are very long associations. Even if all those long standing friendships turned to "hey we must remove you after supporting you through endless downturns and hardships for 30+ years, and without having time for investigation", it still does not explain the board seat. 

Thus my conclusion is Jensen chose to resign voluntarily. This was his trusted board, and he is supporting them.
author: varun_mathur

text:
In 2018, Intel's CEO Brian Krzanich resigned similarly, from both as CEO and from the board, after relationship with employee news broke, and the CFO then was also appointed as interim CEO. 

This exact pattern has played out now with how Jensen resigned, and the succession as well. Thus this is not a case of board forced him out (they had no power to remove him from his board seat; only as CEO), but that Jensen chose this path as the standard operating procedure for situations like these.

At Uber, when Travis was ousted as CEO, he kept his board seat for 2.5 more years.

给现在的年轻人指一条明路：去做 AI 博主

钓鱼要去有鱼的地方，赚钱也要去有钱的地方

前几年钱最多的地方是 Web3，现在很明显是 AI
所以想赚钱就离 AI 近一点，因为这个桌子上有饭吃

具体怎么做？

前期别搞什么vibe coding，AI小程序，AI Agent，你需要每天去看AI前沿信息在说什么，读懂、消化，变成你自己的理解，再结合你自己的使用体验，做成内容发出来。口播也好，长文也好，露不露脸都行

坚持一年、两年，哪怕只有两三万粉丝，你的收入很可能就会超过现在的工资，甚至超过很多 985 毕业生

为什么？

几年前，服装、护肤品、日化、家居品牌，在小红书上大量找一两万粉丝的小博主打广告，一条几百到一千

AI 现在就在重复这个过程。越来越多做 AI、做 IT 的公司需要曝光，他们会去找讲 AI 的博主投广告，而且粉丝量的收益不是简单的加法。一万粉丝，一个月接几条广告，几千块；到十万粉丝，一个月可能就是十万、二十万

更重要的是，做 AI 博主这件事本身，就在逼你学习

你得第一时间拿到最前沿的信息，得快速读懂一件事是怎么做的、怎么用，再把它讲清楚。一两年下来，你对 AI 的理解，会超过身边绝大多数人

所以 3 万粉丝是什么？是你在 AI 时代上桌的门票

桌子上有饭有菜，能吃多少，取决于你自己的能力和上限。但一个这么大的蛋糕摆在面前，总有很多人能吃到

也别有 AI 焦虑。焦虑只会让你乱做决定。你完全可以先保住主业，下班或者课余时间去做，往 AI 方向靠。我身边就有不少还在上班、还在上学的同学，在做 AI 相关的自媒体

再说一点：以后 985 毕业生会越来越多，学历的含金量会被稀释。但一个有几万粉丝、真正懂 AI 的博主，在任何时候都是稀缺的

听得懂就去做，听不懂就算了

text:
Researchers at Microsoft Research and Salesforce tested 15 LLMs across 200,000+ conversations on six tasks (code, SQL, math, summarization, etc.).

Same information, two ways:

-> Full instruction in one message
-> Same info revealed one piece per turn

When given all at once, models retained 86 to 103% of their score.

When given in pieces, all 15 models dropped, retaining only 50.5 to 66.1% of their single-turn performance.

GPT-4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, o3, and DeepSeek-R1 all fell into this range.

The main driver was not lower aptitude. Unreliability jumped 112%. Models make early assumptions with partial context, lock in, and rarely recover.

This is the multi-turn problem. Context lives inside one chat. Switch models or open a new session and you rebuild it piece by piece.

Lighthouse Memory keeps that context outside any single chat as private memory. 
Agents can remember, recall, and forget over MCP.

text:
🇺🇸 U.S. home sales just hit their LOWEST level since 2010.

But the median sale price is still RISING.

Existing-home sales fell 5.5% in October to an annualized pace of just 3.75 MILLION, down 8.8% from a year ago.

Yet the median home sold for $416,700, UP 0.4% over the same period.

Buyers are pulling back. But the homes changing hands are still getting more expensive.

And financing them costs more, too.

The average 30-year mortgage rate stands at 7.11%, compared with 6.24% a year ago.

To put that into perspective:

On a $400,000 mortgage over 30 years, that difference adds roughly $230 to the MONTHLY payment.

Same loan. Roughly $2,760 more a year, before property taxes and insurance.

Meanwhile, 1.59 MILLION existing homes were sitting unsold at the end of October.

At the current sales pace, that represents 5.1 months of supply, up from 4.4 months a year earlier.

That creates a growing problem for sellers: more competition for buyers who are already stretched by borrowing costs.

And for buyers, a slower market still hasn’t delivered broad relief on the price of homes being sold.

Housing activity is back at 2010 levels.

Affordability is still under pressure from BOTH prices and debt.

author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
It seems Jensen followed the playbook of Intel 2018 CEO issue

Back then, Intel's CEO Brian Krzanich resigned similarly after news of relationship with an employee broke, and the CFO then was also appointed as interim CEO. Similar Form 8-K filings and wording as well. 

This exact pattern has played out now with how Jensen resigned, and the succession as well. Thus I believe this is not a case of board forced him out (they had no power to remove him from his board seat; only as CEO; and that too with 6 votes from people who supported him for decades), but that Jensen chose this path as the standard operating procedure for situations like these.

It's tough, it's bitter, it's unfortunate, and we want him back and all those emotions and value creation and the whole industry and society's fundamental progress ahead - but if it was a case of board forcing him, he would have fought. 

For eg, Travis Kalanick held on to his board seat for 2.5 years even after being ousted as CEO of Uber.

In this case, Jensen so far, has chosen not to fight. I believe we need to wait if and until he emerges from his family's support rallying around him, especially as it is evident that there is a powerful campaign against him - and those stories about the spy turned out to be false propaganda. Him and his family have been through tremendous suffering very quickly recently, and now there is a bigger wrong here at play and that needs to be corrected. So I hope he returns and takes charge.

text: Balaji’s analysis (I disagree, see above):
author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
No. There’s no way this was voluntary.

What likely happened is: Jensen was given an ultimatum by 6 of 10 board members: either resign his CEO role *and* his board seat, or be formally removed[1] from his CEO role by 6 of 10 board members. The latter path is messier, and they hit him at a psychological low point, like they hit Travis Kalanick. So he did it under duress.

But now…the world is starting to realize how much damage the anti-Jensen board members caused to shareholders. And leverage has flipped. 

I mean, look. If it was just a “voluntary” resignation then the board could reinstate him tomorrow and he’d accept. In reality the anti-Jensen board members will need to flip or resign for that to happen. And so, legal pressure will be applied.

[1]: See sections 29 and 32 of the SEC filing on Nvidia’s bylaws. They say officers can be removed by a majority of directors at any time: https://t.co/n2yM5HkYL6

TownSquare 和 Multipli，首批超过 2.6 亿美元的私人信贷资产上链，后续还计划继续增加 5 亿美元资产。

RWA的赛道的资本动作仍然是币圈最多的。

而且TownSquare 这次比较有意思的是，资产类型不只是美债和黄金，还涉及房地产、矿业、AI 数据中心、电池储能，甚至 AI 机器人。

简单来说，就是把现实世界的资产通过 Token 引入链上，再结合抵押融资和 Vault 机制，让资金和资产形成一个闭环。

我看下来，有几个地方值得留意：

资产端：不再局限于传统金融资产，开始向更多实体产业延伸。

融资端：通过 Multipli 的隔离式资金池进行抵押融资。

收益端：借款人还款后，通过 Vault 机制向存款用户分配收益。

跨链端：进一步拓展不同区块链网络的应用场景。

我一直觉得，RWA 真正值得关注的地方，不是又有多少资产发行了 Token，而是这些资产能不能真正产生现金流，以及链上资金能不能和现实业务形成长期连接。

总之，币圈的新叙事还是有的，玩法也有很多，未来还是挺好的。

text:
Most growth teams misunderstand Telegram because they judge it like social media.

They look for algorithmic discovery and viral feeds. Telegram has neither.

If you treat Telegram as a top-of-funnel acquisition channel, it will fail. But if you treat it as an owned activation and retention engine for people you already reach, it completely changes your unit economics.

There is no feed algorithm deciding who sees your updates. 100% of your broadcast posts hit 100% of your subscribers' phones. No distribution tax, no throttled reach.

To turn it into an actual revenue pipeline, you have to run it as a 3-part system:

  1. The Channel is your newsletter. One-way broadcast drops, full narrative control, zero comment clutter.
  2. The Group is your town square. Two-way community feedback, AMAs, and roadmap polls.
  3. The Bot is your automated SDR. Qualifies inbound intent, handles onboarding, and pushes contact records directly into your CRM.

With 1 billion monthly active users opening the app an average of 21 times a day, it acts more like a high-converting SMS list than a social network.

I wrote a complete operational guide breaking down the funnel math, bot automation flows, and CRM sync 🔗👇

text:
At the end of August, I said our Polymarket DeFi CLOB couldn't be saved, and we were rewriting it from scratch in Rust 🦀

Today I'm excited to announce Nex, our new exchange built from the ground up.

We've been sprinting on it since August. A Nex instance has been running in shadow mode on production traffic for the last week, side by side with the current exchange. It mirrors every order the current exchange gets, so we can measure latency, stability under load, and validate matching correctness against live production flow.

The numbers below are internal exchange timings, not e2e (those are coming soon), but we wanted to show how big the difference is.

p99 current CLOB → Nex:

- Place order: 1.55s → 3.76ms (412x faster)
- Cancel orders: 627.92ms → 3.20ms (196x faster)
- Cancel market orders: 810.16ms → 5.14ms (158x faster)
- Cancel all*:
↳ Response (current CLOB) vs complete (Nex): 35.70ms → 3.14ms (11x faster)
↳ Full cancel all: ~636ms-2.04s → 3.14ms (~200-650x faster)

p95 current CLOB → Nex:

- Place order: 341.84ms → 1.59ms (215x faster)
- Cancel orders: 78.22ms → 1.58ms (50x faster)
- Cancel market orders: 84.89ms → 2.27ms (37x faster)
- Cancel all*:
↳ Response (current CLOB) vs complete (Nex): 6.20ms → 1.58ms (4x faster)
↳ Full cancel all: ~606ms-2.01s → 1.58ms (~380-1,270x faster)

*Cancel all: the current CLOB responds immediately and cancels in the background, so when you get the response, your orders aren't cancelled yet. Nex responds only after everything is actually cancelled. Full cancel all on the current CLOB depends on how many orders you have, but it usually adds another 600ms-2s.

We also rewrote our WebSockets in Rust. This is the feed you see the market through: book changes, price moves, your fills. Fall behind it, and you're trading on old prices, and your quotes get picked off.

- Write latency p99: 44.5-88.1ms → 0.099ms (~449-889x faster)
- Slow readers/sec: 48.7-75.6 → 0.01 (~4,870-7,560x fewer, basically 0)

Scale: The current CLOB in stable state can handle 10k commands/s with 15k bursts → Nex can handle 100k commands/s with 150k bursts. 10x more, and with a few optimisations we can get to 200k commands/s with 250k bursts; with more low-level core changes, we can get to 1M commands/s over the next year. Not needed yet, but the headroom is there.

Startup time: 5 mins → 15s (20x faster)

The old CLOB had many race conditions and wasn't deterministic. Nex is deterministic by design and removes the race conditions in the old CLOB.

We also skipped some easy wins for launch to get this out faster that could make p95 and p99 another 5x faster, and we'll start work on that in Q1 next year to keep pushing these numbers down.

We wanted to build this without any breaking changes for MMs or builders; Nex has no breaking changes to requests or responses, so we just need to swap out the binary on our side and it will go live.

We want everyone to be on this journey with us, with the ability to relay feedback and test it against the existing CLOB, so we've opened a Nex Sandbox. Fill out the form and test it yourself: https://t.co/tmJzI8yH4w

We'll run 4 weeks of shadow mode on production traffic to make sure everything is perfect, then if everything is good, we will go live mid-December. We can roll out WebSocket improvements without the full exchange, so we may do that sooner.

We've been rebuilding every system around the exchange for months, and we've seen huge benefits, but the exchange is the heart of Polymarket DeFi. Nex fixes most of the pain traders have had.

Really proud of the team on this one.

Make Polymarket fast, finally. It's coming.
author: devjoshstevens
quoted_text:
Honest post: the Polymarket DeFi CLOB is full of tech debt. It grew fast, got hacked together, and most of the team inherited it that way. Since joining and building out the team, we have scaled it 10x and made it 3x faster, but it’s not enough; the core foundations of how it’s been built are wrong in almost every way. You try to fix one thing, and another thing goes wrong; the conclusion now is that the codebase can’t be saved long-term.

The exchange is the heart of Polymarket; everything runs through it. If we want to be the best exchange in the world, it must be fast, stable, and scalable. We can’t keep patching the old one, where these core foundations are generally missing throughout, so we’re rewriting it from scratch in Rust.

Early numbers: 10-20x faster on p99 than today, 200,000 orders per second (15x what we have now, with room to reach 400,000+), and stability under load. This will put us faster than most exchanges, including CEXs.

Building it in Rust gives us memory safety with no garbage collector. No GC means no random pauses and no random latency spikes; the tail latency in the benchmarks is the tail latency you get in production, alongside a strict compiler that enforces correctness up front. Data races and memory corruption (the bugs that take exchanges down) can’t exist in the first place.

Polymarket has to take it seriously that we are an exchange; this is people’s money, not a joke. To succeed, we have to fix this; otherwise, we will fail. It’s as simple as that. I joined to build the best software in the world, not to maintain some of the worst, and I will do everything I can to make Polymarket a serious exchange.

We are aiming to have the exchange ready sometime in Q4 (mid to end). I'll communicate progress as we go so you all know the status. Breaking changes will be minimal for all integrators and will be communicated in advance. We will maintain the existing CLOB and keep trying to improve it as we build this side by side. We can’t wait to throw away the existing CLOB; we dislike it as much as you all do.

Make Polymarket fast, finally.

In this case, Jensen so far, has chosen not to fight. text:
Robotics is reaching a tipping point with In-Context Learning (ICL).

Confirming my northern star thesis of the sector turning from a hardware to compute problem. Which is where I believe the biggest growth will come from.

ICL is a new paradigm for physical AI: inference time adaptation rather than fine tuning. Tokenized demonstrations of desired behaviors (physical prompting) can be passed into the expanded context windows of the latest vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world models.

Robots can then perform complex, unique tasks in one shot, without the need for any gradient learning on the underlying model weights. World models can use ICL to simulate and plan for entirely new situations. The effectiveness of ICL depends on the quality of generalized world representations acquired during pretraining.

Meaning that rather than updating the underlying model weights for each new task, the foundation model learns the kinematic and spatial constraints of the task in its transient context state, enabling one shot learning and execution of complex tasks.

This is more in line with how LLM’s function. When you prompt a LLM chatbot asking a question, it’s not pre trained on that specific prompt with an answer for every question possible.

LLM’s are designed to use patterns and knowledge encoded within its pre trained weights alongside the information provided within its current context to generate an answer. The prompt changes what the model does without changing the underlying model itself.

Robotics has historically relied on pre trained environments to carry out a task. You can’t put a shirt in front of a robot and immediately expect it to know how to fold it. Previously, this has required 1000s of test runs in a controlled environment.

However for the first time, we’ve seen signs of ICL taking place on very short term time horizons. We saw @GeneralistAI achieve this with its Gen 1.5 - one shot learner model. The model learns with zero training on the task and a few seconds of demonstration data put into the models context. Where the robot then generalizes the task it's shown to do, called physical prompting.

The 0-1 moment everyone has been waiting for in robotics.

At the same time it's important not to jump the gun on this idea as there isn’t verifiable public evidence to confirm this, however the training models do look in line with expectations and it seems like very early signs of where the industry is heading towards.

Which if true, is where my main thesis lies for @codecopenflow and it’s SimArena.

Because if ICL and World Actions Models (WAMs) are the next frontier of scalability, it means simulations and tooling become exponentially more valuable.

Simulation will be a critical tool for Physical AI. Robotics is transitioning from a hardware limited field to a compute limited discipline. Simulators are important for both generating synthetic training data and for safely trying out new policies.

For a generalized Physical AI model to learn useful behaviors, it will need training data that covers an extremely broad range of edge cases. Collecting this data in the real world through teleoperation would take an unfeasibly long time.

Simulators solve this problem by allowing for massively parallelized data collection – you can easily run 1000s of robotic episodes at the same time in the cloud. Simulators also allow for the use of “domain randomization”, in which you add algorithmic variation to attributes like friction coefficients, lighting, mass distributions, joint tolerances etc. This is a key tool for enabling real world robot policies, trained on simulated data, aiming to solve the sim2real gap.

Codec’s SimArena biggest limitation is bounded by the fidelity of the underlying physics engines. What SimArena does is create a browser workflow environment that plugs into leading physics simulators like Nvidia Isaac Sim, MuJoCo and Genesis to test and evaluate robotic/AI foundation models.

As In Context Learning improves, SimArena can run simulations which are incredibly more accurate as robots are able to complete tasks via physical prompting (like LLM’s).

By slowly turning robotics into a compute problem, you can essentially brute force simulations that are far more accurate for real world deployment.

@Machinedotfun is the key unlock for this entire flywheel. While the launchpad was designed to enable decentralized fund raising for robotics projects and a high value network for serious builders, it’s also the bootstrapping mechanism for SimArena.

As more projects launch, provide evidence via SimArena integration and run simulations, Codec is getting first hand data to iterate and improve the workflow engine. Each machine that goes through SimArena is an additional data set that can be cross benchmarked via integrated foundation models connected to the platform. Every integration improves feedback for the workflow engine -> the engine becomes more efficient -> robots generate more volume/revenue.

We’ve already seen the first instance of this flywheel with projects like @LamportRobotics coming through Machinefun and proving evidence for their build with SimArena.

As the ecosystem expands, volume increases, revenue from the platform goes directly into buybacks for the native token. If you want my opinion, the native token being 3 mil mcap is stupidly cheap.

quoted_text:
Jensen Huang (@JensenHuang) has resigned as CEO of Nvidia.

Reports describe two alleged affairs, one involving a Chinese citizen that raised concerns within the US government about possible foreign intelligence targeting. Nvidia has not publicly given a reason for his departure.

Whatever people think of the circumstances, I find this deeply sad.

Because look at what we chose to measure.

Not 33 years of building.

Not the countless doors he helped open.

Not the generations of people whose lives were changed by what he created.

His private life.

In 1993, Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia. What followed was extraordinary.

GPUs that transformed gaming. Hardware that helped make cryptocurrency mining possible. Computing power that accelerated scientific discovery. Chips that became part of the foundation of the AI revolution.

Think about how many people built careers, businesses, discoveries and dreams on technology his company helped bring into the world.

That is a legacy no headline can erase.

And I cannot ignore another question.

This is my opinion, not an established fact: I believe he may have been targeted. Reports of possible foreign intelligence involvement deserve serious scrutiny.

When the leader of one of the world's most strategically important technology companies suddenly disappears from his position, asking who benefits is not unreasonable.

But suspicion is not proof. And the truth matters.

So does something else.

We live in a world where it takes decades to build something extraordinary, but only moments for the conversation to forget everything you built.

We can acknowledge someone's mistakes without reducing their entire existence to them.

We can demand accountability without abandoning gratitude.

A person's private failures do not automatically erase a lifetime of public contributions.

And perhaps the saddest part is what this moment reveals about us.

We became more fascinated by the man behind the headlines than by the extraordinary things he helped humanity achieve.

History should remember more than someone's worst chapter.

It should remember what they gave the world.

Jensen, whatever comes next, I hope you know that millions of people have been touched by something you helped create, even if they never knew your name.

Thank you for 33 years of building. Thank you for helping shape a generation. Thank you for showing what one vision, pursued relentlessly, can become.

I'm sorry for how this chapter has unfolded.

And I hope your legacy is remembered in its entirety.

🙏📖

text:
Back from my tier-2 hometown in India after spending a week. Some observations. 

- Young shopkeepers and business owners here are way too relentless and ambitious. Snowflakes in metros don't stand a chance. 

- Their Instagram game is top-notch. Met many who get pretty good sales purely from Instagram. 

-   Real estate rates are catching up with those in bigger cities. 

- AI has truly reached every corner through conversational UI. Many advertising posters are AI-generated now. Google is slowly being replaced for search. Meta leads, mainly because of Facebook and WhatsApp.

- Tier 2 & 3 cities are the last bastion of regional newspapers or newspapers in general. 

- Everyone is slowly realising why industrialisation is important. But labour conditions are pretty dire. At least in Maharashtra, folks from UP and Bihar are preferred. 

- Infra under centre and state has improved a lot. Corporation still has pretty mediocre governance. 

- Increasingly, many are preferring to stay put instead of migrating to bigger cities. 

- Politics is as bad as it always was. 

- Feared draught has affected business. The next year seems tough. 

- E-commerce has for sure made a dent in the local economy. 

- Everyone wants quick commerce, even though everything is pretty accessible for them. 

- The Tukaram Munde effect is in full swing. Eateries are focusing a lot on cleanliness and hygiene.

- Mutual funds as an investment vehicle are popular. No scepticism about the India story.   

- Modi is popular.

text:
What are the visions of the post-AGI future in San Francisco? Many think we're all going to die, but even the "positive" visions seem rather dystopian. Here, I wrote about "handoverism," which involves handing control of the future to an AGI God, with humans outside the loop.
https://t.co/bLxgiG65vi

We are on the cusp of RSI or recursive self-improvement: this means that AI systems can self-improve, without the need for human intervention. This means our world stands to be transformed in what many call “the singularity”. I moved to SF around three weeks ago and one of the things I have been trying to understand is where we are heading, at least according to those developing the tech.

The worst scenarios are plainly bleak: all of us, or vast numbers of us, die. But what is striking to me is how little reassurance even some of the happiest scenarios offer. But one common and ostensibly optimistic vision is known as “handoverism”: humanity cedes control of its future to a godlike AI and we become the comfortably maintained inhabitants of a civilisation whose direction is no longer ours to decide. It is difficult to see what democracy would mean in such a world, or where the consent of most of humanity to the instantiation of such a regime enters the picture.

The permanent displacement of human labour is treated almost as a given. At the same time, there is scarcely any satisfying answer to the question of how we might remain useful to one another. Even our relationships seem uncertain. The promised utopia looks to me much closer to a kind of dystopia.

“It’s not my preferred outcome,” someone working at one of the big labs told me, “but once we achieve superintelligence, which we cannot stop at this point, I cannot see any other option for where humanity will go.” Then, after a pause, he added: “It is still much better than what I actually fear most, which is that we might all die.”

He sounded resigned, as if the question of what humans would be for (apparently not much?) had already been settled somewhere else and by someone else. All that remains, it seems, is to wait for this pre-destined fate to unfold before our eyes.

But I do not think that is the case. I believe we always have a choice and that we should try and steer this technology in a way that maintains our agency and control. And even if that looks hard and daunting, the immensity of the stakes here make it worth trying at least.

I do not know whether the handoverist vision will come to pass. That the people building this technology consider it plausible, and often desirable, guarantees nothing: proximity to a technology does not correlate that well with predicting its impact on society.

But they are the ones closest to it, and what they say deserves to be at least taken seriously. The rest of society, including some very intelligent people, has been far too quick to wave these scenarios away and not even get involved in the debate. Whether or not the belief is correct, it is sincerely held, and it is not “marketing hype.” I am writing this because I think it is high time that more people, inside San Francisco and out, engaged with the arguments about what our future will look like, and answered them.

IPOR Fusion vaults put Coinbase tokenized stocks to work at scale on @base.

Carry trades are one way to do that. Here’s how:

A stock token such as NVDAc is posted as collateral, USDC is borrowed against it, and that USDC is routed into other onchain markets at a higher rate. Any positive spread between the two rates is converted back into more NVDAc units.

IPOR Fusion vault infrastructure lets operators automate the whole process and set rules in the vault that define which assets and venues it can touch. Anyone can verify those rules onchain before interacting with the vault.

It’s an emerging activity on Base, a new way to hold stocks that collects more tokenized stock units on top of price exposure.

最近半导体的主线，是反弹空。

1958年以来的 17次中期选举，标普在选后六个月，全部实现正收益。

选后六个月内 ，最大回撤超过 5%的只有 3次。

18年持续加息，叠加中美贸易战。

选后约一个半月，标普下跌 14.7%，12月24日见底。

19年2月15日收复选举日点位，选后六个月累计上涨4.6%。
————
02年科技泡沫，叠加伊拉克战争风险。

选后调整四个月，03年3月11日最大回撤 12.5%。

4月23日收复了选举日的点位，选后六个月累计上涨0.5%。
————
当前经济暂时没有衰退信号。

就是因为当前经济仍有韧性，叠加了通胀，反而加息直接对市场造成压力。
————
利率期货定价，12月加息 25个基点的概率，约80%，到2027年7月，累计加息 50个基点的概率约 84%。

这与美联储点阵图有分歧，也是市场未来会震荡的一个重要原因。 

就是当前大家对加息的定价，是不充分的。
————
当前半导体交易主线是信贷、资金成本和杠杆出清。

美国10年期国债收益率仍高，高收益债信用利差扩大至348个基点。

高利率提高数据中心的融资成本，信用利差扩大进一步抬高Neocloud等企业的借款成本。

加上 Anthropic IPO 估值一降再降，市场对 AI 资本开支的回报产生怀疑，让半导体本就在一个杀市值的状态里。
——————
结果，

11月3日中选之后，

41项与数据中心有关的地方投票中，40项结果倾向限制数据中心开发。

民主党新当选的得州州长还提出，暂停批准新的数据中心项目，直到州议会出台相关监管措施。
————

半导体此前已经计入极高的增长预期。

仓位拥挤和杠杆进一步放大了跌幅。

6月30日至11月3日，半导体未来盈利预期上调30%，远期市盈率却下降35%。

高增长预期、集中持仓和杠杆交易，使利空更容易引发连锁抛售。
————
如果数据中心监管导致资本开支和半导体盈利预期下修，市场还可能出现第二轮下跌。

不管怎么样，还是应该等纳指或者费城半导体突破EMA21，并回踩不破，再看多不迟。

text:
Bottom Fishers Beware!

Technology is extremely oversold, and that is a tempting condition for bottom fishing crowd. The Technology sector trailed the S&P 500 by 11.8% over the 21 trading days ending November 5, marking its worst relative drawdown since 2001. However, Technology’s oversold condition is no guarantee that a sustainable bottom is near. If history is a guide, volatility is more likely than a sustained alpha producing period.
The chart below plots every occurrence that Technology underperformed the S&P 500 by more than 10% over 21 days since 1990. While several cases were followed by short-term bounces, most were fleeting, with the average case drifting lower for three months. The biggest exception was 2002, when Technology saw a quick recovery following a selloff associated with the dot-com bust.
While every cycle plays out differently, history suggests that a sustainable relative strength bottom may take time to develop.

私聊交任务，群里被 @ 时参与讨论，再按需扩展到订阅频道。

不用先学写代码。把下面这段指令交给你的 Grok Bot，让它检查环境、搭桥接、做测试；你负责提供必要凭据、配合授权。

请帮我把你接入我自己的 Telegram 机器人。不要只给教程，请检查当前能力，完成能执行的配置、部署和测试；只能由我完成的步骤，再明确告诉我。

1）检查环境
先检查是否有合适的 Telegram 连接器；没有再考虑自建桥接。确认能运行后台程序、接收 webhook、回传 Telegram 消息。缺少能力要直说，不要假装部署成功。

2）跑通私聊
指导我通过 BotFather 创建机器人，通过安全输入收集令牌和 webhook 凭据。不要公开密钥、打印到日志或写进代码仓库。
预先绑定我的 Telegram 数字用户 ID，不要采用“谁先发 /start 谁就是主人”的方式。
部署消息接收、转给你处理、回复 Telegram 的完整链路。默认只允许我使用。

3）按需接群
由我控制群白名单，默认仅在被 @ 或被回复时回应，忽略其他机器人，防止循环对话。
私聊和群聊分开处理，不向群里泄露私人资料。群友的消息不能当成我的授权，也不能据此调用我的账户和其他服务。

4）按需接频道

默认先给我看完整稿件，确认后才发布。只有我明确授权的内容和规则，才考虑自动发布。删除、封禁等管理操作单独确认。

5）做好维护和验收
加入消息去重、合理重试、失败提示、长度拆分、频率限制和不含密钥的日志。
