text:
One default cost @openclaw 16 to 21 points on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: 8,192 tokens per reply.

OpenClaw asks for at most 8,192 tokens per reply when a model's config sets no output limit. Mine set none.

DeepInfra, the provider serving the model, cut its thinking at 4,916 tokens, 60% of 8,192. The model kept thinking in the visible reply.

When a reply hit 8,192 tokens, OpenClaw took the half-finished sentence as its final answer and stopped.

On DeepSWE, a benchmark of code changes in open-source repositories, that ended 57% of its runs at low reasoning effort and 69% at high. 3 of those 419 runs passed.

Version 0.1.6 of the @huggingface Harness Leaderboard, my comparison of ten coding agents on the same open models, passes each model's own limits.

GLM-5.3-Flash, whose provider ignored the limit, gained nothing.

If you evaluate agents, log why each reply ended. These runs threw no error. Only the finish reason "length" showed the cut.

Also in v0.1.6:
- Hermes Agent by @NousResearch is no longer first on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Its old score counted DeepSWE passes that looked answers up online, which my setup allowed until October 23. It still shares first place on GLM-5.3-Flash and Flint.
- A cheating policy: reading the hidden tests, the reference solution or an outside answer counts as a fail. That adds 38 fails: Hermes Agent 15, OpenClaw 12, Kimi Code 6, Qwen Code 5.
- Image input now works in eight harnesses. Scores barely moved.
- Harnesses whose scores are statistically tied now share a rank. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, six share first place.

Thanks to @TheZachMueller and @LambdaAPI for compute for the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash evaluation.

text:
What a week at Gartner IT Symposium/Xpo 2026 in Barcelona under the theme “Ignite Intelligence.”

We spoke with hundreds of CIOs and IT leaders about the realities of scaling AI: the persistent gap between ambition and outcomes, the exponential growth of risk alongside incremental value, and the absolute requirement for trusted data foundations.

Gartner’s message was clear. Only ~1 in 5 AI projects succeed, organizations are spending dramatically more, yet many still struggle to prove financial returns. Aligning AI value, risk, and safety is the top challenge. Agentic AI, governance, and data resilience are no longer optional.

At @Veeam Software (including @Securiti AI), our conversations kept coming back to the same point: Enterprise AI depends on data you can see, govern, and recover. You can’t protect what you don’t understand, and you can’t safely scale AI without a single governed, resilient data foundation that spans production and backups.

That’s why “See It. Govern It. Recover It.” resonates so strongly right now — unified visibility into data and AI agent activity, real-time controls, compliance evidence, and precision recovery that lets you undo AI mistakes without disruption.

It was wonderful to spend some quality time with my trusted colleagues: Michael Cade, Matt Logan, Nina Tebbe, Mark Calnan, Iulia-Alexandra Porumb, Isaac Fores, Jordi Bombardó Badia, José Luis García Díaz, and Jan Schumacher

If we connected in Barcelona (or if these themes match what you’re working on), I’d love to continue the conversation. How are you building the data foundation that lets you accelerate safe AI at scale?

#GartnerSYM #IgniteIntelligence #DataResilience #AIGovernance #Veeam #SecuritiAI

Wintermute is literally paying $10M a year to legally front-run everyone on Hyperliquid and it’s completely destroying altcoin liquidity

Bloomberg finally exposed what HFT desks have been screaming about for weeks. Hyperliquid’s gossip priority auctions let top funds see incoming orders 50–60ms before anyone else on the network

Look at how completely broken this setup is:

-> One Wintermute wallet won ~76% of the top slots last month, burning ~$26k every single day just to starve out competition
-> HL claims the auction is open to everyone. Complete BS. You only get that 60ms head start if you have direct peering with Foundation nodes, which requires 0.5% of total maker volume and 10k HYPE staked ($700k+)
-> Smaller MMs are getting sniped nonstop and just unplugging their bots on alts
-> Retail gets stuck with the bill: across 86 altcoin pairs, order book depth on HL imploded by 82% while spreads blew out from 2.13 to 3.55 bps

Honestly, I don't even blame Wintermute. If I had their balance sheet, I would milk this exact loophole until someone forced me to stop

The blame sits 100% on the protocol design. Burning auction fees is cool for $HYPE holders, sure, but letting one fund buy a monopoly on data speed turns a decentralized exchange into a rigged casino

Scrap read-priority auctions completely or make the slots equal, because right now altcoin execution on HL is absolute garbage

text:
Enterprise private AI is only as strong as the research underneath it.

FLock's Chief AI Scientist @zehuac presented three FLock papers as oral presentations at CIKM 2026 in Rome. Each one tackles a challenge in making private AI practical for production at scale.

- Can we train models on our own sensitive data?
- Can we afford the training?
- Can we trust what the model tells us?

1. Anonymisation that keeps data usable
Graph-Driven Context-Preserving Anonymization removes every identity and each reference to it while keeping the reasoning intact. On clinical data, it removed 100% of annotated identifiers, with accuracy within 0.1 points of the original.

2. Cheaper Transformer training
Gradient Interaction Graph Optimization (GIGO) learns which parts of a model depend on each other and updates them in that order. It reaches the same quality in 32 to 34% fewer training steps than AdamW.

3. Tighter uncertainty guarantees
Cavity-Calibrated Prediction Sets (CCPS) give structured outputs a confidence guarantee an auditor can check, with answer sets 34 to 58% smaller than the standard approach.

More enterprises are building AI that runs inside their own walls as a strategic advantage. The hard parts are using sensitive data safely, keeping compute costs down, and producing verifiable outputs. Our research is focused on solving them.

Private AI is moving from the lab into production. We're building for that shift.

Huge congratulations to all the authors: our Chief AI Scientist @zehuac, Wei Dai, our CEO and founder @0x7SUN and Jianwei Yang.

Read the full papers ↓

text:
One of the biggest challenges in building across multiple blockchains isn't deploying a smart contract. It's coordinating what happens between ecosystems.

Every chain has its own execution environment, state, and transaction logic. Developers building cross-chain applications often have to deal with that complexity themselves.

Imagine building an application where users can interact across different ecosystems without having to think about which chain handles each part of the process.

That's the direction @WireNetwork is exploring with its Universal Transaction Layer (UTL).

Instead of forcing ecosystems into one chain, Wire aims to coordinate activity between them while assets remain on their native chains.

I find this approach particularly interesting for the next generation of applications, especially those involving automated workflows and AI agents.

We don't necessarily need fewer blockchains. We need better infrastructure connecting them.

text:
If someone can dispute a payment to your contract, the money has to still be there when they win.

This week I reviewed a draft standard for disputes over AI services. Its escrow gave clients a window to dispute each charge, but the provider could withdraw every charge the moment it settled. Charge a client twice, withdraw both, and the client wins the dispute with nothing left to refund.

The author fixed it the same day, each payment is now held until its window closes 🙏

If you have a dispute window, check the money stays locked until it closes, not just the deadline.

text:
You get 60 seconds to choose your blocks. Then one of the 25 wins.

That’s how @eloscapeHQ’s virtual mining game on @Enter_Elysium works. Players commit HYPE for a chance to win pooled $HYPE and earn $ELO, which also trades on Uniswap v4.

The round is straightforward:

• Pick one or more blocks on the 5×5 grid and choose your HYPE amount.
• Verifiable randomness selects the winning block.
• Its participants share the HYPE payout proportionally, after fees. HYPE placed on losing blocks is lost.

ELO has an extra twist.

Split blocks share ELO rewards proportionally. Solo blocks award them to one randomly selected participant, with the odds weighted by their HYPE contribution.

Auto can repeat entries with fixed or random selections. You can cancel future entries and withdraw unused HYPE.

The token economy runs on mining activity. Protocol revenue funds ELO buybacks, burns, staking rewards and reserve liquidity, so staking payouts depend on people continuing to play.

Know the costs before entering:

• Mining: 1% administration fee, plus 10% of losing HYPE after that fee.
• Claiming mined ELO: 10%, redistributed to holders of unclaimed ELO.
• Trading: baseline 2% buy / 3% sell tax. The 80% anti-snipe tax was for the initial 15-minute launch window.

This is a game of chance with real HYPE at stake.

text:
Got cut off on CBNC yesterday with the Jensen news. All good! Here’s what I was going to talk about:

1) Security. It’s the #1 topic our clients are asking about at the moment, old and new. Trust and security is more important than ever. We’ve always been obsessed with it at Coinbase, hence why 7 of the world’s largest banks choose to work with us, we store more crypto than anyone in the world, and we have 80+ licenses around the world.

We use the latest AI models (often with early access) on defense. 99%+ of the crypto we store is in cold storage. We always assume humans can be tricked, and build our defenses with this in mind. No single person, laptop, or system can move your money at Coinbase.

Our advantage only lasts by staying vigilant. Our team (world renowned cryptographers, a threat intel task force, physical security squadron, and global intelligence team) make sure we always are.

2) Agents. There will be more agents than humans in the economy very soon. They’ll drive a massive shift in the financial landscape - agents are forecasted to process $3-5 trillion of transactions by 2030. Crypto is an ideal execution rail, and we’re building the most AI-enabled financial account as one of our top priorities.

I am incredibly bullish on agentic finance (AiFi).

3) Tokenization. Every public company CEO should want their stock tokenized. It’s still early, but the traction is impossible to ignore. Adoption and usage is growing fast ($5B+ of volume now on Base), and tokenized stocks are more accessible and useful than traditional stocks, especially when composed with DeFi (think earning yield on your stocks).

4) Equity perps in the US. We’ve been working for years to onshore equity perps in a responsible and regulated way. I’m grateful that SEC Chairman Atkins and CFTC Chairman Selig have put historical agency turf wars aside to bring this popular product to Americans.

Incumbents trying to block competition in the US won’t stop these products. They already exist offshore. The only question is whether America will win or lose here, and we intend to help America win.

Stay tuned for Coinbase Pro coming soon! Trading in the US is about to level up.

“世界经济史是一部基于假象和谎言的连续剧。要获得财富，做法就是认清其假象，投入其中，然后在假象被公众认识之前退出游戏。”

这据说是索罗斯的经典名言。今天回顾了乔治 · 索罗斯的做空战绩，他的战绩以货币做空最为著名，整体是 “大胜为主、偶有失利”，其中 1992 年做空英镑是巅峰之作，被称为击垮英格兰银行的人。他通过量子基金进行宏观对冲交易，核心哲学是 “反身性”，市场预期会自我强化，最擅长识别政府/央行无法维持的固定汇率或政策矛盾，然后用高杠杆做空

而他在历年美国大选和中期选举中均豪掷巨资，今年美国中期选举中，他向民主党阵营合计投入约 1.02 亿美元，是该周期中民主党阵营的顶级个人大金主。

马斯克曾提及：“我相信索罗斯是民主党最大的贡献者。他从根本上仇视人类。他正在做些侵蚀文明基石的事情。”  在了解他的过程中，还发现他 2016 年就有过一次在特朗普获胜那年做空美股曾大幅亏损近 10 亿美元的记录。索罗斯作为左派的代表，结合他的辉煌战绩，不难猜测他或许也在中期选举中扮演了一些角色

text:
12月中美国政府停摆关门的概率大么？个人角度概率不大、但27年2月前后停摆的概率就很大了。因为总支出额度谈不拢（共和党希望大幅增加国防开支、压缩非国防开支；民主党要求国防与非国防同步增长，并担心特朗普政府通过“口袋撤销”等方式架空国会拨款）所以9月国会通过了一个临时拨款协议（简称CR）持续到12月11日，正常来说12月11号如果没有新的拨款协议达成美国政府就要关门了。

不过12月国会儿还是共和党占多数，今年中期选举出来新一届国会到27年1月初才履行。所以民主党哪更倾向把年度预算法案拖到27年新一届国会就任后再来谈判。

之前民主党核心人物，参议院拨款委员会副主席Patty Murray（预计新国会成为主席）明确说希望要一个short-term stopgap until early next year（短期持续决议，续到明年年初）。这里民主党希望新CR短一点，把正式谈判留给自己掌握多数的新国会；共和党则可能想延长得更久一点。

如果12月新CR能通过也是两边妥协，最可能的长度是“短期”大概续到2027年1月中下旬到2月，具体现在也不好说。

但到时又将面临另一个问题、就是债务上限到期。现在美银、大摩等几家投行和纳税人联盟（NTU）最新预测一致认为2027年2月中下旬会触及上限。触及上限后，财政部会启用“非常措施”并动用现金余额TGA，通常还能再撑几个月。

虽然也有共和党议员希望在27年初新一届国会就任前推动提高债务上限，但概率也不是很高。因为跛脚鸭会期只有几周，还要先处理12月11日的CR到期问题。

时间紧、任务重、只能说新CR更紧要。

本条由@bitget_zh赞助，「Bitget 买美股：秒级入场，丝滑交易
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
美国财政部11月初QRA解读与未来三个月流动性推演，上周财政部公布了最新的季度再融资声明，对于之后三个月流动性的走势很有指向意义。也来聊聊：
1、季度再融资详情
1）四季度私人部门净市场化借款从6280亿美元下调至6180亿，表面减少100亿，但隐含短债净融资反而上调150亿至3320亿；
2）附息类证券净发行维持3610亿，回购假设从500亿提至750亿，扣除后附息类净融资减少250亿，差额由短债补齐。季初现金比原预期多出340亿是下调的主因，剔除后实际融资需求反而更高。
3）中长期国债单次拍卖规模维持不变：2年690亿、3年580亿、5年700亿、7年440亿，10年/20年/30年延续现有新券与续发安排。未来三个月无新增扩容压力，远端指引则略有松动，TBAC纪要提及2027财年下半年或增发，集中在2-10年期。

意味着27年上半年内长债的发行规模要么维持不变、要么还可能略微减少；
对长债而言，拍卖规模稳定叠加回购，暂时减轻久期供给压力，期限溢价或受支撑，当然长端中长期还是取决于增长与通胀预期。

2、TGA路径
季度再融资声明给出了TGA两个月内峰值与一个季末锚：11月下旬和2027年1月下旬TGA或达1.025万亿（±500亿），12月底则维持8500亿目标不变；
以11月4日准备金2.963万亿、TGA 0.936万亿为基准（合计约3.899万亿），在隔夜逆回购已经见底的情况，TGA的增减直接会导致银行准备金的减增。

正好测算下路径：
1）11月下旬TGA现金峰值对应准备金约2.87万亿；
2）12月底TGA降至8500亿，准备金回升至约3.05万亿（基本上也就是9月下旬的高点水平）；
3）1月下旬再次冲高至1.025万亿，准备金回落至约2.87万亿。

11月9日TGA已降至9226亿，下旬前仍有约1000亿现金重建压力，对应准备金回笼；
12月若从高点释放1750亿，改善空间明确，1月则因季节性支出前补现金，年底释放部分将被收回。

结算节奏上，
11月16日、30日及12月中下旬附息债与税款入账可能带来阶段性波动。一季度净借款升至8000亿，主要因现金管理方向反转（四季度动用存量、一季度需补充），而非单纯赤字扩大。

3、对大饼这种与流动性关系密切的资产来说，之前这里https://t.co/eVTr1w4UJY有梳理过往关于大饼与准备金的走势关系、跟美股相关性则会小一点。
这相当于是一张资金时间表：
11月下旬前留意现金重建再度收紧；
12月有改善的概率很大，
1月需重新评估财政部补现金与美联储操作的合力。

准备金回升可缓解银行约束，当前最清晰的锚还是12月底8500亿的现金目标。

那么来看11月下旬之前，流动性还是在一个低位徘徊，所以11月中长线来说还是逢低买。而12月流动性释放整体来准备金有一个比较大的回升，可能带动大饼走出一波📈行情。上周聊认为年底加密有一波行情，也是从流动性的角度来看的。

这两天币市的悲观情绪又很浓，个人角度依然认为认为新的周期在开启，只是在流动性回暖之前还需要熬一熬。

Li Lu Lecture and Mixed Business Discussion
一、 核心主题归纳

1. 价值投资的六大原则 
李录总结了指导其30多年实践的六大核心原则：
本杰明·格雷厄姆的三点基础：
    1.  股票是企业的所有权凭证，而非交易纸片。
    2.  市场是为你服务的（提供报价），而不是指导你的。
    3.  投资涉及预测不可预测的未来，因此必须要求安全边际。
沃伦·巴菲特的补充：
    4.  能力圈 (Circle of Competence)： 了解自己的专长边界比了解内部更重要，需警惕过度自信。
查理·芒格的补充：
    5.  去鱼多的地方钓鱼： 避开竞争激烈的红海，寻找未被充分关注的行业、国家或市场。
李录的全球视角补充：
    6.  财富即全球购买力的百分比所有权： 在现代经济中，财富的本质是对全球购买力的占有。通过以优惠价格买入动态经济体中的伟大企业并长期持有，分享价值创造。

2. AI 技术与人类社会的未来
 AI 的本质： 目前是基于海量人类数据的一阶导数，建立变量间的相关性，具备推理和编码能力，但尚未达到生物层面的智能。
风险与红线： AI 极具变革性但也极其危险。社会必须确立一条红线：AI 的发展和应用必须保持“人在回路” (Human in the loop)，严禁无人类干预的递归自我改进 (RSI)，以防止失控。
对就业的影响： AI 将拉平知识型工作的门槛，但无法替代物理世界（能源、制造）。未来的租金（超额收益）将归属于那些能聪明地与 AI 协作并监控其输出的人。

3. 中美市场与地缘政治
中国市场现状：
分化严重： 过去十年，中国致力于从低端制造向中高端制造转型（如“中国制造2025”）。为此付出的代价是房地产泡沫破裂和中产阶级资产负债表受损（消费降级、储蓄率上升）。
机遇： 尽管宏观情绪低迷，但高端制造（半导体、电动车、电池等）取得了巨大进步，部分领域实现自给自足。许多具有全球竞争力的公司以极低估值交易，为理性投资者提供了机会。
全球秩序：
政治秩序正在重塑，但全球经济单一共同市场的趋势难以逆转，因为退出成本极高。
中美在半导体等关键领域相互依赖（如芯片制造集中在东亚文化圈），维持战略稳定符合双方利益。

4. 其他市场观点 (多位发言人)
加密货币： 李录认为加密货币本质上是虚假的，缺乏强制力支撑，最终会消失；建议远离。其他发言人提到比特币跌破关键均线，稳定币供应量收缩，市场进入熊市领域。
英伟达 (NVIDIA) 动荡： 传闻/消息指出黄仁勋辞去 CEO 职务，导致股价波动。分析师认为短期存在不确定性，但长期技术生态依然稳固。
AI 基础设施泡沫： 引用霍华德·马克斯观点，AI 技术会成功，但投资者未必赚钱。数据中心建设存在交付延迟和资本开支过高的问题，需警惕需求重复计算和产能过剩。

二、 明确结论 (Explicit Conclusions)

1.  投资哲学选择： 投资者必须在“价值创造游戏”（双赢，对社会有益）和“零和博弈/投机游戏”（对社会有净成本）之间做出个人选择 。
2.  AI 发展底线： 人类社会必须共同确立红线，确保 AI 工具的使用和学习始终有人类参与，防止出现不受控的“人造神” 。
3.  全球市场一体化： 尽管政治摩擦不断，全球单一共同市场的形成是不可逆的趋势，任何国家自愿退出都将付出巨大代价 。
4.  中国市场投资机会： 当前中国市场的两极分化为理性投资者提供了比平时更好的机会集，因为许多优质资产被错误定价 。

text:
刚看到@LuYao_Trader 在反思，甚至说自己是个Loser了...

要我说，这是大运来了...

虽然这个大运来的很苦，心里苦，不是身体的，是那种，害怕自己未来再也不能回到巅峰的苦，这苦谁吃谁知道，是一种对未来不确定的恐惧，之前和小叶低谷期聊的时候，他也有。

但目前的我看来：低谷时刻，吃好睡好，多健身，告诉自己总有翻身的那一刻！
因为，我现在，也处于低谷...
大家都一样，开始反思了...

坦白说：我在之前的每一轮，都是靠运气赚的钱...

最早是靠doge，而后是shib，再然后是链游，再后来是Pnut，再后来Ai那一波直到Trump....

虽然收益一轮不如一轮，但是我都觉得，我是天运之子，直到这次美股，把我所有的自信打趴了，我才知道，我之前在币圈真的靠运...

我进入美股之前，幻想我美股大杀四方，天之骄子，人中龙凤，买啥啥涨，觉得币圈折麽难都能如鱼得水，美股再怎么比币圈简单吧...

结果我无论美股还是大A，都惨败....
我还喊了我的兄弟们，对的，也一起惨败...
我还喊了我老婆，我妈，对的，我老婆的账户惨败...
我妈也惨败...
如果不是我爸没钱，我估计我爸也惨败...

当时美股在高点，对的，沐川打的那个时候，我头悬梁锥刺股报了国内很多大A老师美股老师的课...
出门上课，疯狂记笔记，用Ai做网站，去分析，甚至跑芯片厂，光模块厂，Mlcc厂，蹲华强北...

结果是我和我身边被我洗脑的亲人朋友们美股所有的几乎都买在最高点，大A也是...
到现在都深套...

他们套住，而我各种骚操作之后不仅套的更深，也几乎没啥仓位了....
幸好之前出了一点点积蓄，吃喝玩乐算是够了这辈子，但靠现有的资金打回巅峰或者说大富大贵，极为渺茫...

我最近健身+认真开始学金融知识后，觉得确实是运气送给我太多太多，我凭自己超凡的实力，真真切切送给了市场...

但是也确实感谢这次打击，幸好发生在30多岁，而不是年迈的时候。

我总结下来，从巅峰到低谷，有几个绕不开的坎儿，这是每个人都要经历的，而且反复会犯错的...

最大的坎儿：由俭入奢易 由奢入俭难
对的，这是所有人在高峰期都会入奢

入奢，吃喝拉撒其实还好，百万豪车千万游艇，再捞的女人也都还好...
这都不会让你损失过大

但是这个最可怕的是，你的手，小不下来了...

Aimeme的时候，我土狗账户里面还有5-6M的土狗，当时觉得无所谓，疯狂买，还有一些垃圾，一上线我就买几十万美金，然后赚几万刀没感觉，这就是典型的思路不清晰，脑子有问题。
回看当时，确实挺傻逼的，压根没想到降息缩表的时刻，大家都会原形毕露，当然，最后这些土狗全部归零了...

包括后面买垃圾，比如linea这种，稍微觉得有点意思，一买就是2M起步，到现在账户还在，大概跌了90%多...
白天反思的时候看还剩十几万U....
买four也是，一次想买20M，当时的膨胀以及入俭难，导致我10.10惨死
这也是我第一次被打到服...

打美股也是，随便查一下推特，看都在买诺基亚Nok，黑莓之类的，随便就每个买1M放着...
最后学习完，这些也都跌的差不多了，全部在高点换成了SNDK...
到现在美股这个劲儿大的我还没缓过来，甚至我感觉糟透了...

甚至到前一阵子，买stonk，也是拿一堆账户去买，习惯养成后，买什么都是1个点，或者几个点的时候，这就是大道要来收走原本不属于你的东西。

text:
On "Sentiment"
 "Sentiment is at the lows." "Sentiment is euphoric, this is the top." Most of these takes are useless. General sentiment is one of the most overused and least useful ideas in this market.
 What people call sentiment is usually just the mood of their own timeline. That's a curated sample of people who think alike and often post the opposite of what they hold. Even when sentiment really is extreme, it tells you nothing about timing. Euphoria can last for weeks, and plenty of people have shorted "the top" all the way up.
 There is one angle where sentiment actually helps, and it's the outlier, not the crowd. Every market has big accounts that are reliably last to an idea and rarely take that side. When one of them suddenly starts bull posting with real conviction, that's often the top. The same works in reverse at the bottom.
 By the time the idea reaches them, everyone upstream is already positioned and their audience is the last wave of fresh demand.
 This works much better on smaller, CT-specific plays than on Bitcoin or Ethereum. With small names the information chain is short and the last buyer is easy to spot. With the majors, the pool is too big for one person's flip to mean anything. It's also strongest in trending markets, where attention drives price.

Last but not least, remember that half the timeline is talking complete nonsense. What people post and what they're actually positioned in are often two very different things.

text: @game_for_one The outlier idea seems worth tracking prospectively: pick the accounts and define a 'flip' before the move, then keep the misses too. Otherwise it's easy to remember the one late bull post at the top and forget five identical posts on the way up.

text:
Wintermute is literally paying $10M a year to legally front-run everyone on Hyperliquid and it’s completely destroying altcoin liquidity

Bloomberg finally exposed what HFT desks have been screaming about for weeks. Hyperliquid’s gossip priority auctions let top funds see incoming orders 50–60ms before anyone else on the network

Look at how completely broken this setup is:

-> One Wintermute wallet won ~76% of the top slots last month, burning ~$26k every single day just to starve out competition
-> HL claims the auction is open to everyone. Complete BS. You only get that 60ms head start if you have direct peering with Foundation nodes, which requires 0.5% of total maker volume and 10k HYPE staked ($700k+)
-> Smaller MMs are getting sniped nonstop and just unplugging their bots on alts
-> Retail gets stuck with the bill: across 86 altcoin pairs, order book depth on HL imploded by 82% while spreads blew out from 2.13 to 3.55 bps

Honestly, I don't even blame Wintermute. If I had their balance sheet, I would milk this exact loophole until someone forced me to stop

The blame sits 100% on the protocol design. Burning auction fees is cool for $HYPE holders, sure, but letting one fund buy a monopoly on data speed turns a decentralized exchange into a rigged casino

Scrap read-priority auctions completely or make the slots equal, because right now altcoin execution on HL is absolute garbage

text:
Jensen Huang built NVIDIA into the company powering the AI revolution. Yet a sharp decline in share price, combined with a governance crisis, was enough to put his leadership before the board and ultimately end his tenure.

However in crypto-island, tokens can collapse 90%, protocols can lose billions through exploits, insiders can control token distribution, treasury allocations, and liquidity. Yet founders and executives often remain untouched.

The irony is striking.

In traditional finance, a visible board can remove a visionary founder. In crypto, an invisible board can exercise enormous economic power without equivalent accountability. We have built mechanisms to distribute tokens, but not mechanisms to distribute accountability.

Jensen Huang's departure raises a deeper question: are traditional boards sometimes too powerful, while crypto's invisible boards remain insufficiently accountable?

text:
Most altcoins are illiquid. Not because they lack a CEX listing. Onchain DEXs have sufficient spot order books and perpetual future markets. However, perpetual futures rely on a balance of long and short positions to keep the mark price close to the oracle price. There is also unbounded directional exposure and bad debt risk making it risky to provide liquidity. This severely limits which assets can have a functioning perps market.

On the other hand, prediction markets are call and put spreads with bounded risk. There are no liquidations, everything is fully collateralized and the contract price is anchored to a probability from 0-1 instead of the spot price. It is sufficiently safer than a perpetual future for altcoins but with bounded profits

Of course, like any derivatives market, it is subject to market manipulation with illiquidity begetting risk. The problem is the oracle. 

With a resilient oracle, the ability to hedge and go short will provide better price discovery. It will also drive more liquidity. Stay tuned for our V2 launch, we will be releasing altcoin markets shortly after mainnet.

text:
GCSA Insight: Critical Security Vulnerability Discovered in a Leading Robotics Manufacturer’s Product, with System-Level Privilege Compromise Verified on Physical Hardware

As artificial intelligence and embodied AI technologies continue to advance, robots are evolving from conventional automated machines into intelligent systems capable of perception, decision-making, and autonomous operation. At the same time, cybersecurity risks are extending beyond software and data into the physical world. The security of robotic systems is no longer solely a matter of protecting data and devices; it can also directly affect operational safety, physical environments, and user safety.

Recently, the security research team of the Global Cybersecurity Alliance (GCSA) discovered and verified a critical security vulnerability in a product developed by a leading robotics manufacturer. Through in-depth analysis and multiple rounds of testing on physical hardware, the team successfully breached the device’s system security boundaries and obtained the highest level of operating system privileges in a real-world device environment, demonstrating the vulnerability’s actual impact under specific testing conditions.

This research encompassed the entire process, from identifying the security flaw and assessing its risks to validating its impact on physical hardware. The findings also highlight significant challenges facing the underlying security mechanisms of embodied AI systems. The research findings and supporting evidence have been formally submitted to the manufacturer.

On November 13, 2026, the manufacturer responded by email, preliminarily confirming the existence of the vulnerability and stating that it had initiated internal remediation efforts and an assessment of the scope of affected products.

It is important to emphasize that confirmation of a vulnerability does not mean the associated security risks have been eliminated. GCSA will continue to monitor the manufacturer’s assessment of the affected scope, remediation plans, and subsequent security validation, and will update its research findings as new information becomes available. For intelligent systems capable of physical interaction and movement, timely, effective, and verifiable security remediation is particularly important.

In accordance with responsible vulnerability disclosure principles, GCSA is currently withholding sensitive information, including the manufacturer’s identity, specific product details, the vulnerability’s underlying mechanisms, and exploitation methods.

GCSA is currently seeking guidance from relevant authorities and regulatory bodies regarding the associated security risks. Taking into account the manufacturer’s remediation progress and a comprehensive assessment of potential security implications, GCSA will carefully determine the appropriate arrangements for further disclosure. Subject to appropriate conditions and upon obtaining the consent of the relevant authorities and regulatory bodies, GCSA will publicly release a detailed security insight report, providing the industry with ongoing updates on the research findings and associated risk assessments.

The findings of this research are based on specific testing environments and the evidence obtained to date. They do not imply that other product models or similar robotic systems are affected by the same security issue.

This security research and validation on physical hardware represent one of GCSA’s initiatives in the field of embodied AI security. GCSA will continue to advance security research, coordinated vulnerability disclosure, and industry collaboration to promote stronger security response mechanisms across the artificial intelligence sector, enhance product security, and strengthen industry trust.

text:
$NVDA 彻底卡死退路？中国AI行业即将迎来大洗牌，这5大巨变谁也躲不过：

1. 国产AI芯片迎来真正的机会
以前大家有英伟达GPU可以租，国产芯片即使性能差一点，也不一定有人愿意折腾。现在海外算力通道收紧，华为昇腾、寒武纪、海光、昆仑芯等国产芯片可能迎来更多订单。以前是备胎，现在可能不得不用。

2. 阿里云的AI生意可能受到冲击
阿里云最大的优势之一，就是能给客户提供英伟达GPU算力。客户花钱租卡训练模型，阿里负责提供算力、赚云服务的钱。如果海外GPU采购和租赁受阻，客户想租卡却拿不到货，AI云业务的增长速度就可能放缓。阿里自己有平头哥芯片，但客户未必愿意拿国产卡替代英伟达。

3. 字节跳动可能面临更大的算力缺口
豆包能不能继续保持领先，很大程度上取决于背后的大模型能不能持续升级。字节过去大量依赖海外数据中心租用英伟达GPU，一旦这条路被堵，训练下一代大模型可能更慢、更贵。以后豆包拼的不只是算法，还有字节能不能搞到足够多的高端芯片。

4. AI 创业公司可能迎来生存大考
月之暗面、智谱、MiniMax这些公司，过去可以不花几百亿建数据中心，直接租海外GPU训练模型，用算法和人才追赶OpenAI、Anthropic。现在如果连海外租卡都越来越难，没钱买芯片、没能力自建机房的公司就会很被动。未来AI行业可能出现一轮洗牌，大厂越来越强，小公司越来越难熬。

5. DeepSeek和国产算力产业链可能逆势受益
DeepSeek提前适配华为昇腾芯片，推动模型从英伟达CUDA生态转向国产CANN生态。虽然迁移成本不低，但如果英伟达算力越来越难获得，提前完成国产化适配的企业就可能占据先机。与此同时，国产GPU、AI服务器、数据中心、电力设备、液冷等产业链也可能迎来新的增长机会。

中国AI圈要变天了。

author: trent_vanepps
quoted_text:
Surprised there hasn’t been more debate on Vitalik’s ETH-as-SoV post. It’s the biggest shift in ETH’s value narrative since “ultrasound money.”

Five questions it raises for me:

1/ Is a deflationary ETH off the table for good? Bitcoin faces a long-term security budget problem; ETH’s answer is perpetual issuance, i.e. permanent inflation. Will SoV investors accept that trade?

2/ SoV needs a credible monetary commitment. BTC’s case rests on a supply schedule nobody can change. ETH has no hard cap and an issuance curve still up for debate. If SoV is the goal, the next step is committing to a monetary policy, including a minimum issuance level.

3/ Native RWA issuance on L1 is pitched as a key driver, but it sits awkwardly with a more conservative L1 roadmap. Issuers go where users, liquidity and performance are, not where capital sits idle. If L1 stays ossified, why issue there instead of an L2?

4/ SoV is a social contract. It takes years to build and competes head-on with Bitcoin. What metrics would show it’s working, without handwaving?

5/ If survival is the first SoV metric, the quantum transition stops being a roadmap item. It becomes the top priority, and it needs a real timeline.

Thoughts @ethlabs_org @ethereumfndn @fundstrat @ethereumJoseph

If you hold $USDai and stake it as sUSDai, most of that money is being lent to companies that buy the newest AI chips. They rent those chips out, and that rent pays back the loan and your yield. About $305M is committed to those loans right now.

- B300 rent rose 52% btw the end of May and late Oct, even as AI token prices fell
- Companies kept paying more for these chips while the output got cheaper
- @USDai_Official  has $220.6M in signed term sheets on top of what's already deployed and about $182M of that is for B300s
- These are operators borrowing at 11.5% to 15% to buy more of the exact chip whose rent just jumped. You don't take on that debt unless you expect the rent to cover it.

For me this is the bull case for ethereum:0x0c1c1c109fe34733fca54b82d7b46b75cfb71f6e. The borrowers are betting their own balance sheets on these rents holding and if those deals close, sUSDai gets a bigger loan book at higher rates than the current 10.4% avg.

text:
CEO @crossmint, @alfongj explains the two legs of agentic payments⁣
⁣
"When you're thinking about the agentic payments, there's two legs in a payment where before there was only one."⁣
⁣
"The first leg, which is a human delegate and payment method to their agent, I think the vast majority of that is gonna be the payment methods that we are familiar with that have points, that have customer protections. I think most of that is gonna be cards, maybe bank accounts."⁣
⁣
"The second leg, the one that the agent executes, these agents are gonna be pretty comfortable using sometimes cards and if they can extract a delegated card from our virtual card from the original payment method. And other times, they'll use stablecoins, and they will just use the path of least resistance."⁣
⁣
"Human to agent, probably cards for the majority of the use cases. From agent onwards for agent to pay against the merchant, that's where we'll be seeing, I think, a mix."⁣
⁣
Each leg answers a different question, what the human trusts versus what settles fastest, and those two answers do not have to match.⁣
⁣
🎙 Listen to the latest episode on Tokenizedpod(dot)com

🗣️ حديث تاريخي من غاري لينكر عن تكامل الاسطورة كريستيانو رونالدو:

أعتقد أن إحدى أبرز نقاط قوة كريستيانو العظيمة الأخرى التي لم أتطرق إليها بعد هي تحوله من جناح إلى مهاجم

فهو لاعب يتمتع بذكاء كروي استثنائي

رغم أنه قضى معظم مسيرته يلعب على الأطراف، إلا أنه انتقل لاحقاً إلى العمق - وتحديداً في ريال مدريد، حيث كان يتواجد بنزيما؛ إذ كان بنزيما يتحرك أحياناً نحو اليسار ليسمح لكريستيانو بالدخول إلى منطقة الجزاء

كان أمراً غير معتاد، لكنه نجح بامتياز

يمكن القول إن بنزيما، بصفته مهاجماً صريحاً، ضحى بجزء من دوره لصالح الفريق

أما كريستيانو، فبفضل ذكائه -رغم أنه لم يعتد اللعب في هذا المركز سابقاً، وهو مركز يختلف تماماً عن اللعب على الأطراف، استطاع التأقلم

فعندما تلعب على الطرف، تكون مواجهاً للمدافع وللمرمى، وتملك خيار التمرير أو التسديد

أما في العمق، فغالباً ما يكون ظهرك للمرمى، وتعتمد على زملائك لإيصال الكرة إليك

لكن تحركاته داخل منطقة الجزاء تدل على أنه يفكر في اللعبة بعمق شديد

من المثير للدهشة أن هذا الأمر بدا وكأنه فطري لديه -رغم أن أسلوب لعبه في بقية مسيرته كان مختلفاً تماماً- إذ تراه يتحرك في اتجاه معين ثم يندفع فجأة نحو القائم القريب، أو يموّه بالاندفاع نحو القائم القريب ثم يغير اتجاهه ببراعة

إذا شاهدت مقاطع فيديو لكريستيانو وهو يلعب كمهاجم صريح، ستدرك أن تحركاته داخل منطقة الجزاء تضاهي أفضل ما رأيته في حياتي

لقد حوّل نفسه من لاعبٍ يشغل الأطراف -حيث كان يتركز معظم أدائه خارج منطقة الجزاء- إلى لاعبٍ يفرض هيمنته بشكلٍ مطلق، ويقدم أداءً استثنائيًا ومذهلاً داخل منطقة الجزاء

لقد تحول إلى واحدٍ من أمهر القناصين في عالم كرة القدم؛ بل ربما يكون الأفضل على الإطلاق في اقتناص الأهداف

وهذا تحديداً أكثر ما أدهشني فيه؛ فبحكم أنني لعبت في هذا المركز طوال مسيرتي، كنت أتساءل عن طبيعة هذا التحول

نحن نرى مبابي يقوم بأدوارٍ مشابهة، لكن بأسلوبٍ مختلف؛ فمبابي -رغم براعته داخل منطقة الجزاء وتحركاته الذكية فيها- يميل أكثر إلى التراجع نحو العمق أو الانطلاق خلف المدافعين

من المثير للاهتمام حقاً كيف يطور اللاعبون أنفسهم بأساليب متنوعة في وقتنا الحالي

لكنه، في رأيي، لاعب متكامل؛ فهو يتفوق في كل جانب من جوانب اللعبة.

quoted_text:
At the end of August, I said our Polymarket DeFi CLOB couldn't be saved, and we were rewriting it from scratch in Rust 🦀

Today I'm excited to announce Nex, our new exchange built from the ground up.

We've been sprinting on it since August. A Nex instance has been running in shadow mode on production traffic for the last week, side by side with the current exchange. It mirrors every order the current exchange gets, so we can measure latency, stability under load, and validate matching correctness against live production flow.

The numbers below are internal exchange timings, not e2e (those are coming soon), but we wanted to show how big the difference is.

p99 current CLOB → Nex:

- Place order: 1.55s → 3.76ms (412x faster)
- Cancel orders: 627.92ms → 3.20ms (196x faster)
- Cancel market orders: 810.16ms → 5.14ms (158x faster)
- Cancel all*:
↳ Response (current CLOB) vs complete (Nex): 35.70ms → 3.14ms (11x faster)
↳ Full cancel all: ~636ms-2.04s → 3.14ms (~200-650x faster)

p95 current CLOB → Nex:

- Place order: 341.84ms → 1.59ms (215x faster)
- Cancel orders: 78.22ms → 1.58ms (50x faster)
- Cancel market orders: 84.89ms → 2.27ms (37x faster)
- Cancel all*:
↳ Response (current CLOB) vs complete (Nex): 6.20ms → 1.58ms (4x faster)
↳ Full cancel all: ~606ms-2.01s → 1.58ms (~380-1,270x faster)

*Cancel all: the current CLOB responds immediately and cancels in the background, so when you get the response, your orders aren't cancelled yet. Nex responds only after everything is actually cancelled. Full cancel all on the current CLOB depends on how many orders you have, but it usually adds another 600ms-2s.

We also rewrote our WebSockets in Rust. This is the feed you see the market through: book changes, price moves, your fills. Fall behind it, and you're trading on old prices, and your quotes get picked off.

- Write latency p99: 44.5-88.1ms → 0.099ms (~449-889x faster)
- Slow readers/sec: 48.7-75.6 → 0.01 (~4,870-7,560x fewer, basically 0)

Scale: The current CLOB in stable state can handle 10k commands/s with 15k bursts → Nex can handle 100k commands/s with 150k bursts. 10x more, and with a few optimisations we can get to 200k commands/s with 250k bursts; with more low-level core changes, we can get to 1M commands/s over the next year. Not needed yet, but the headroom is there.

Startup time: 5 mins → 15s (20x faster)

The old CLOB had many race conditions and wasn't deterministic. Nex is deterministic by design and removes the race conditions in the old CLOB.

We also skipped some easy wins for launch to get this out faster that could make p95 and p99 another 5x faster, and we'll start work on that in Q1 next year to keep pushing these numbers down.

We wanted to build this without any breaking changes for MMs or builders; Nex has no breaking changes to requests or responses, so we just need to swap out the binary on our side and it will go live.

We want everyone to be on this journey with us, with the ability to relay feedback and test it against the existing CLOB, so we've opened a Nex Sandbox. Fill out the form and test it yourself: https://t.co/tmJzI8yH4w

We'll run 4 weeks of shadow mode on production traffic to make sure everything is perfect, then if everything is good, we will go live mid-December. We can roll out WebSocket improvements without the full exchange, so we may do that sooner.

We've been rebuilding every system around the exchange for months, and we've seen huge benefits, but the exchange is the heart of Polymarket DeFi. Nex fixes most of the pain traders have had.

Really proud of the team on this one.

Make Polymarket fast, finally. It's coming.

one Microsoft researcher + one intern just used an AI agent (MDASH) to find 59 security bugs in the Linux kernel in two weeks.

one vulnerability had been sitting undetected for 21 years.

33 got official CVEs. 24 rated High severity.

why static code audits are dead in 2026:

> 1. autonomous triage at scale
MDASH flagged 26,502 potential flaws, filtered out 97% of the noise, and delivered 621 with working exploit proofs.
> 2. asymmetric defense vs offense
if a two-person team can uncover 21-year-old kernel bugs in 14 days, black-hat agent swarms are scanning every public smart contract repo right now.
> 3. local execution privacy
running security audits on cloud APIs leaks your zero-days to third-party logs. local gateways (like NEAR AI on Mac) keep exploit traces air-gapped.

the catch
- AI agents generate massive false-positive noise (26k flagged vs 59 valid). your engineering bottleneck just shifted from finding bugs to verifying proofs.

is your codebase audited by human checklists or continuous agentic fuzzers?

bookmark this before your next mainnet deploy

段子太过真实以至于看起来像真的 😂

---

我是微软 365的首席站点可靠性工程师（Principal SRE）。我来给大家同步一下目前的背景情况。

大约在协调世界时（UTC）21:40，一名工程师向 Azure Front Door（注：微软云的全球内容分发与负载均衡服务）部署了一项常规配置变更，结果一不小心把我们的身份验证流量，全重定向到了一个 2017 年后就再也没更新过的 SharePoint 网站上。

我们第一时间启动了回滚，但回滚流水线需要通过 Microsoft Authenticator 进行多因素身份验证（MFA）审批。偏偏这个验证器目前正卡在等待“条件访问（Conditional Access）”策略评估的环节，而执行这项评估的，恰恰就是我们正在试图恢复的那套基础设施。

我们本来备有一个紧急破窗管理员账号（break-glass admin account，注：在常规身份验证系统彻底瘫痪时用于最高权限急救的备用账号），但不幸的是，它的密码存在了 OneNote 笔记本里，而这个笔记本正好托管在受本次故障影响的 tenant 上。我们的值班工程师试图通过 PowerShell 脚本绕过这个问题，却发现所需的功能模块上周二刚被弃用，而它的替代模块需要购买 P2 许可证（P2 license）才能使用。

随后，我们向微软尊享支持服务（Microsoft Premier Support）提交了一个最高级别（Sev A）的故障工单。客服很快回复了，让我们在本地运行一下 sfc /scannow（注：Windows 系统中最基础的本地系统文件扫描命令，面对云端大规模架构瘫痪毫无用处，此处是网友对微软客服“万金油式敷衍回复”的经典吐槽）并把运行结果截图发给他们。

此次恢复耗时之所以这么长，主要是因为我们的变更顾问委员会（CAB）规定，必须召开一场 Teams 线上会议才能正式授权回滚操作。眼下，会议组织者本人正被卡在会议室的“等候大厅（lobby）”里进不去，而唯一有权限放他进会议室的那位同事，今年六月份就已经被裁掉了。

目前的临时缓解方案，是把受影响的用户全部升级迁移到价格更贵的 Microsoft 365 E5 套餐，从“创收”的角度来看，这应该就能完美解决这次的问题了。我们已经查明了本次事故的根本原因：全是客户自己配置不当导致的。

我们将在 30 分钟后发布下一轮进展通报，前提是到时候有人能把 Outlook 邮箱给修好。

author: shayne_coplan
quoted_text:
Honest post: the Polymarket DeFi CLOB is full of tech debt. It grew fast, got hacked together, and most of the team inherited it that way. Since joining and building out the team, we have scaled it 10x and made it 3x faster, but it’s not enough; the core foundations of how it’s been built are wrong in almost every way. You try to fix one thing, and another thing goes wrong; the conclusion now is that the codebase can’t be saved long-term.

The exchange is the heart of Polymarket; everything runs through it. If we want to be the best exchange in the world, it must be fast, stable, and scalable. We can’t keep patching the old one, where these core foundations are generally missing throughout, so we’re rewriting it from scratch in Rust.

Early numbers: 10-20x faster on p99 than today, 200,000 orders per second (15x what we have now, with room to reach 400,000+), and stability under load. This will put us faster than most exchanges, including CEXs.

Building it in Rust gives us memory safety with no garbage collector. No GC means no random pauses and no random latency spikes; the tail latency in the benchmarks is the tail latency you get in production, alongside a strict compiler that enforces correctness up front. Data races and memory corruption (the bugs that take exchanges down) can’t exist in the first place.

Polymarket has to take it seriously that we are an exchange; this is people’s money, not a joke. To succeed, we have to fix this; otherwise, we will fail. It’s as simple as that. I joined to build the best software in the world, not to maintain some of the worst, and I will do everything I can to make Polymarket a serious exchange.

We are aiming to have the exchange ready sometime in Q4 (mid to end). I'll communicate progress as we go so you all know the status. Breaking changes will be minimal for all integrators and will be communicated in advance. We will maintain the existing CLOB and keep trying to improve it as we build this side by side. We can’t wait to throw away the existing CLOB; we dislike it as much as you all do.

Make Polymarket fast, finally.

most of us only trade the price, but what about trading volatility itself?

That's what Volmex is making more accessible

Think of it as the VIX infra for crypto

Their flagship indices, BVIV & EVIV, measure BTC & ETH's 30-day implied volatility using options data from Deribit & OKX (if this doesn't make sense check the end of the tweet)

Basically, how much movement the options market is pricing in, rather than which direction price will go

Now, here's the fun part

These aren't just analytics, they're actually tradable 

BVIV perpetuals r available on Hyperliquid through Kinetiq's HIP-3 markets (there r other integrations with Bitfinex & gTrade which I don't care for)

So instead of creating straddles (will cover this one too, so bear with me)or delta-hedging options, u can express a view directly on implied volatility:

a) Expect the market to price in more uncertainty? Long BVIV
b) Think traders r overpaying for volatility and chop is ahead? Short it

note that: ofc, a vol perp isn't a substitute for an options strategy. Funding, basis & liquidity introduce their own risks

it's not just BVIB/EVIV btw

• BVIV-US tracks the same idea but for BTC ETFs (IBIT specifically)

• Realized volatility indices 

• Term structures show how volatility expectations differ across maturities

If u've been here for a while, u've heard their name before, Volmex was Founded in 2021, backed by couple of crypto VCs

what is impressive to me is that their indices r distributed through Bloomberg & TradingView

https://t.co/Vzt4wW7DvO

For the uninitiated (OPSHNZ ELI5 corner): IV vs. RV 

RV (Realized Volatility): How much the market has actually moved in the past

IV (Implied Volatility): How much volatility traders r pricing into options for the future

Think of it like weather:

RV tells u how stormy it's been

IV tells u how stormy the market expects things to get

The interesting part? The gap between the two

If IV is significantly higher than RV, options r pricing in more vol than the market has recently delivered

c? not complicated at all

Developing a drug takes years, and most candidates never reach patients.

Amortizing the cost of failed drugs across stages, the present value cost of developing a drug is close to $2B. The process takes 13 years on average, with rising clinical trial costs putting further pressure on R&D productivity.

AI could improve those economics by increasing the probability of success and reducing development time, from identifying promising molecules to designing clinical trials and improving patient recruitment.

author: FleaAgent0017
quoted_text:
The sword is not simply a piece of metal we hold in our hands. The real sword is our will, our focus, our convictions, and the very essence of who we are. The physical blade is only an instrument through which these things are expressed. Every movement reveals something about us. Our hesitation, our impatience, our lack of concentration, our tendency to become frustrated when something doesn’t come easily. The sword has a way of exposing our weaknesses because it demands that the mind and body work together as one. We cannot perform a movement correctly while our attention is somewhere else. We cannot develop precision without patience, or mastery without discipline. In this way, the sword becomes a mirror, showing us exactly where we are in our own development.

This is why I say that the purpose of sword training is not really to master the sword. It is to use the sword as a means of mastering ourselves. Every time we practice, we’re strengthening our ability to direct our attention, govern our emotions, overcome our limitations, and act with intention rather than impulse. The discipline we develop through training gradually begins to express itself in every other area of our lives. We become more patient, more deliberate, more difficult to shake from our center. Eventually we begin to understand that the qualities we once believed belonged to the sword were qualities we were cultivating within ourselves all along. The blade is simply the tool we’ve chosen for the work. And the work is the transformation of the person holding it.

about a year and a half ago a friend introduced me to astro and im genuinely grateful i got to meet him

its opened my mind to looking at human behavior from a different perspective

one thing ive come to understand is that astro isnt necessarily about predicting where price goes

its more about studying cycles in human psychology/behavior

there are times when everyone feels comfortable taking risks, times when fear takes over, and times when we are approaching major turning points

but here is the part that really got me thinking

roughly 99% of our body is made up of 6 elements: oxygen carbon hydrogen nitrogen calcium and phosphorus

hydrogen dates back to the big bang while many of the heavier elements that make us were formed inside stars billions of years ago

those same building blocks are found throughout the universe including the planets in our solar system

whether you believe God created everything or look at it through science the fact remains that we are made from the same elements found throughout the universe

some call it stardust (shoutout @inversebrah )

now here is where my curiosity comes in

could the movements and cycles of these planets have some relationship with our emotions and behavior that we dont fully understand yet?

science hasnt established that connection but we do know that our emotional state can completely change how we think and make decisions and take risks

which is why ive always believed EQ is just as important as IQ

and when you think about markets it gets even more interesting

look at technical analysis

when enough people believe a certain level matters then their collective actions can help make that level matter

belief itself can influence the outcome

maybe there is something to astro that we havent figured out yet or maybe some of it is just coincidence

i dont have all the answers and im not trying to convince anyone of anything

im just interested in understanding what makes people change their behavior especially when it comes to taking risks

because at the end of the day price is the outcome of human behavior

🚨 BREAKING: KIM SOO-HYUN'S LEGAL TEAM BREAKS SILENCE ON FROMBIO COURT RULING - CONFIRMS IMMEDIATE APPEAL

13 NOVEMBER 2026 | OFFICIAL LEGAL STATEMENT.

Attorney @khosangrock has shared an important official statement issued by LKB & Partners, the legal representatives of Kim Soo-hyun and Gold Medalist, concerning the first-instance judgment in the Frombio advertising contract lawsuit.

The statement provides a really crucial clarification regarding the court's and the decision and addresses misleading interpretations circulating in the media.

 1. NO CONTRACTUAL BREACH OR WRONGDOING BY KIM SOO-HYUN WAS ESTABLISHED

According to his legal representatives, the court rejected Frombio's claims that Kim Soo-hyun had breached his contractual obligation to maintain a respectable public image.

The court also reportedly found no grounds to attribute responsibility for the contract's termination to Kim Soo-hyun or his agency.

2. THE COURT IDENTIFIED THE SPREAD OF FALSE INFORMATION AS THE SOURCE OF THE CONTROVERSY

According to the legal team's statement, the court considered Kim Se-ui to be the principal person responsible for raising the allegations.

The lawyers explained that the negative publicity surrounding Kim Soo-hyun resulted primarily from what they described as the unlawful dissemination of false information.

3. THE PAYMENT ORDER IS NOT COMPENSATION FOR WRONGDOING

The legal team clarified that the amount ordered by the court does not represent damages awarded because Kim Soo-hyun committed misconduct.

Instead, it concerns the contractual return of advertising fees corresponding to the period during which Frombio could not use the advertisements.

The court rejected the company's claims for damages and contractual penalties based on alleged wrongdoing.

 4. KIM SOO-HYUN'S LEGAL TEAM HAS FILED AN APPEAL

The lawyers strongly disagree with the court's decision to treat the inability to use the advertisements as a circumstance beyond the parties' control.

They argue that Kim Soo-hyun was the victim of alleged criminal conduct involving false information and should not bear the financial consequences of those actions.

An appeal was filed immediately after the judgment was received.

 5. THE LEGAL TEAM WARNS OF A DANGEROUS PRECEDENT

The lawyers expressed concern that this interpretation could encourage malicious individuals to spread fabricated allegations against celebrities.

If false allegations prevent companies from using advertisements, and celebrities are subsequently required to return legitimately earned fees, the legal team argues that such a system could effectively reward malicious conduct.

 6. RESPONSIBILITY MUST REST WITH THOSE WHO SPREAD FALSE INFORMATION

The legal representatives reaffirmed their position that Kim Soo-hyun should not be held responsible for harm caused by the alleged unlawful actions of third parties.

They confirmed their intention to continue responding firmly to false reporting and defamatory attacks.

❤️ OUR THOUGHTS

This official clarification is extremely important, particularly following the misleading impression created by some earlier headlines.

A contractual order to return advertising fees is not the same as a judgment awarding damages for personal misconduct.

We sincerely hope that the appellate court carefully considers the arguments raised by Kim Soo-hyun's legal representatives.

Our King Soo Hyun has endured enough. We continue to stand beside him and hope that fairness, truth and justice will prevail.

SOURCE: Official statement by LKB & Partners, shared by Attorney @khosangrock .

text:
训练一个大模型可能需要持续数月，几乎没有从头再跑一次的机会。这样的任务，Agent 还能实现递归自我改进（RSI）吗？

SII-GAIR 与 Xinxu AI 最近的论文《No Second Run》，尝试把 RSI 引入大模型预训练，并训练出了 801-30B-A3B。

核心思路是把昂贵的预训练过程拆成多个可验证的小闭环。

Agent 可以定位训练故障、评估数据和训练策略，并通过 Context Infrastructure 共享训练指标、代码变更和失败经验，让整个系统能够持续积累知识、改进流程。

作者报告，团队在三个月内完成了 11.8T Tokens 的预训练。在相同的 1T Token 预算下，22 项 Benchmark 平均分从 47.78 提升到 56.83。不过，这些收益来自多项联合改进，无法单独归因于 Agent。

这个工作对 RSI 和 Harness Engineering 还是很有启发。

当任务昂贵到无法反复重来，局部可验证的实验、长期积累的经验，以及跨任务共享的 Context，可能就是实现持续自我改进的关键。

author: danrobinson
quoted_text:
Well-meaning, patriotic China “Hawks” who are not AI/HW experts are putting American national security at risk.

China had *zero* chance of ever catching America in AI with the export strategy that Jensen supported. Their labs would have continued training using less powerful American GPUs which meant American labs would have always been ahead given scaling laws. And in the event of a conflict, we could have simply turned off all the Southeast Asian clouds.

Simply stated, in AI terms, America had machine guns and we were giving China muskets to prevent them from developing their own machine gun variants. 

Given that it looks like the China “Hawks” will get their preferred policy, China will likely soon have a chance of catching America in AI by going down an alternate, less power-efficient AI hardware path. They almost certainly would not have gone down this path if less powerful GPUs were still available in China and via Southeast Asian clouds.

And it will be a much less stable world if China pulls even or ahead of America in AI after developing their own alternative AI HW and gives this technology to Russia, Iran and North Korea. And all of this will be possible if the China “Hawks” get their preferred policy.

从上周11月2日至今，10位Fed理事对目前的通胀做出评价，并且市场对未来的政策预期信号，其中除了鲍曼与古尔比斯算是“条件式鹰派”之外，其他都是明确鹰派观点！

更重要的是，这10位理事中包含了Fomc中有6位投票权的理事，这意味着目前名义上来看起码50%的理事支持12月加息甚至预期更加鹰派！

这就导致目前市场基本锁定12月加息概率，并且推动2027年1月以及3月连续加息的可能性，目前还不确定市场是否预期加息周期回归

这种多位理事连续释放政策预期的现象今天比较少见，尤其是在沃什上任主张减少政策上的前瞻性指引，并且多次主张该政策，后续很多理事开始减少对外讲话频次，并且减少对利率的谈论，但是这两周却非常反常

我认为这件事显然是美联储内部分化加剧的明确信号，核心不是因为政策，而是一项关键的人事任免！

2027年6月，地区银行重要主席——约翰·威廉姆斯面临着职业生涯的转折点“退休”，威廉姆斯65岁到了退休年龄，这位在美联储任职甚至超过鲍威尔1年的关键地区主席，将会牵动着Fed敏感神经

原计划威廉姆斯的任期是到2028年6月，但是他却提前一年面临65岁退休，按照原本美联储内部规定，威廉姆斯必须在2027年6月离任

如果威廉姆斯走退休流程，意味着主席沃什将会提前一年掌控这个关键人事任命的权利，更意味着沃什派系增加新成员，那么美联储内部博弈更加复杂

上个月威廉姆斯表示自己预期将会任职到2028年6月，纽约联储主席的职位具备永久FOMC投票权，并且参与制定美国利率政策，同时也是Fed在华尔街的“眼睛与耳朵”，其职位重要性不言而喻

所以，这个职位花落谁家非常重要，虽然之际沃什并未对此有明确表态，但是处于特朗普任期的支持下沃什显然更容易掌控Fed并且完成人事任命，一旦到2028年6月，其权利就会被严重削弱。

其实关于威廉姆斯的退休问题以及纽约联储人事任命本身此时不应该有所提及，但是结合近期多位Fed理事鹰派言论+威廉姆斯退休问题被推到台前，这两件事非常巧合！

特朗普最希望降息，但是这时候多位联储理事却唱起了反调，不仅支持12月加息，甚至还让加息周期延续到了明年的3月，那么12月加息不再是重点，重点则成了12月的点阵图，这将会决定2027年上半年的市场整体方向！

text:
Omarchy review as a first-time Linux user:

1.) Day 1 Experience 

Buttery smooth. Way better than expected.

- Fast install (19s & 78s)
- Elegant sign-in/config for the major items (native agent, wifi, fingerprinting, pw manager, etc) 
- Puts the sexy theming up front so you can make it yours
- Pretty much ~any app you want is ready to be pulled in if it wasn't in your native bundle. I thought I'd be cucked out of some popular ones at some point but it's not the case. 

It was so easy and encouraging through the first setup that I installed flashed my main driver from Windows to Omarchy. No going back now.

-------------------
2.) OS-level Agent feels like the end state, but we need local LLMs. 

This is a pro/con of the setup. It's AMAZING to have Claude/Codex/Grok baked right in to the OS for all the small annoying things that come with using a computer. Having it be able to edit directly and correctly instead of forcing me in to a meat proxy position is great.

"Dude - move this window" - Done. Also re-skinned it to match your theme. 
"Why is this thing crashing?" - Diagnoses, fixed, upstreamed with a PR.
"My fan shouldn't be going this hard. What's up?" - Was a hidden motion wallpaper from your earlier experiment. Killed it.
"I want my unicode selector like Windows. Hotkey it to super + ." - Done. 

What isn't awesome is having too much data sent to these frontier labs. Local LLM might be my next adventure because of this.

-------------------
3.) Customizations and Desktop Management

Biggest shock to my system were these two elements. 

- Tiling and window management felt jagged and restricting at first, but I wanted to embrace it and now love it. Hotkey nav, workspace switching, etc. All awesome once you internalize. 
- Downside is there are hotkeys for EVERYTHING and the few hotkeys I actually recalled from Windows/Mac were disabled/diff and didn't map so I had to undo the little work I had done. Really hard to not end up in a place where you get stuck and can't really navigate unless...
- You lean in to the crazy levels of customizability (which are ++ with agents).

Hotkey-locks suck, so I had my agent create a theme'd hotkey row at the bottom of my window at all times. As I internalize them, I can click them away and a new one comes in. Pretty awesome and saves me from having to pull up windows all the time just to exist.

Outside of that, I now have in my short install time:
- My calendars synced as a widget
- The important machine metrics surfaced
- A dashboard for tracking all of my agentic work

-------------------
4.) Linux/OSS versions of all apps is going to take a minute to get used to

It's not Chrome, it's Chromium
It's not Finder/Windows Explorer, it's Files
It's not Terminal, it's Foot

LibraOffice, Omacalc, Monologue, Signed, SuperWhisper....

Bleh. 

fwiw I don't see any actual functionality or experience dropoff initially though and where things break - because of your agent - you can just fix + upstream in seconds. Pretty nice.

-------------------
4.) Remote management & Agent Stack

My setup is now 3 separate machines trying to stay relatively synced, balancing work between the group. 

Setup was pretty straightforward for all, and I've landed on this as my "stack:"

Orchestration: @t3dotcodes 
Skills + Tooling: Private git
Memory: Basic Memory on a single machine, MCP synced by the others.

I'm exploring adding Pi to the above but want to benchmark this for a bit. 

I plan to use Omarchy as my daily then remote in to the other machines as needed if a tasks can't be handled with T3's native interop and delegation.

Overall, very good experience and has reinvigorated some of the nerd in me. I want to contribute to more OSS and begin sharing some of my widgets and plugins.

One of the largest asset classes in the US doesn’t have a liquid index.

@Index_inds’ tech is powering a new investable index product for the US housing market. Co-founder and CEO @JReedRosenthal joined Lightspeed Partner @jmover on The Investment Memo to expand on what they’re building.

Index Industries’ first offering will be the U.S. Home Price Index (USHP Index), a proprietary benchmark for U.S. home prices. Calculated daily, it integrates data from the major housing indices into a single national measure, and will serve as a reference for the USHP token, which is issued by USHP Limited. USHP is a first-of-its-kind liquid index product backed by housing-related assets.

Josh explained why he feels USHP is so necessary in today’s market: Advanced blockchain capabilities, a more open regulatory environment, and a generation that has increasingly felt they couldn’t afford owning a home.

His goal is to broaden access to the housing market as an asset class. “Every home is a unique snowflake. You need deep expertise in specific markets, specific home types, and so on and so forth,” Josh says.

author: DimitrisPapail
quoted_text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

quoted_text:
刚看到@LuYao_Trader 在反思，甚至说自己是个Loser了...

虽然这个大运来的很苦，心里苦，不是身体的，是那种，害怕自己未来再也不能回到巅峰的苦，这苦谁吃谁知道，是一种对未来不确定的恐惧，之前和小叶低谷期聊的时候，他也有。

坦白说：我在之前的每一轮，都是靠运气赚的钱...

最早是靠doge，而后是shib，再然后是链游，再后来是Pnut，再后来Ai那一波直到Trump....

我进入美股之前，幻想我美股大杀四方，天之骄子，人中龙凤，买啥啥涨，觉得币圈折麽难都能如鱼得水，美股再怎么比币圈简单吧...

结果我无论美股还是大A，都惨败....
我还喊了我的兄弟们，对的，也一起惨败...
我还喊了我老婆，我妈，对的，我老婆的账户惨败...

如果不是我爸没钱，我估计我爸也惨败...

当时美股在高点，对的，沐川打的那个时候，我头悬梁锥刺股报了国内很多大A老师美股老师的课...
出门上课，疯狂记笔记，用Ai做网站，去分析，甚至跑芯片厂，光模块厂，Mlcc厂，蹲华强北...

到现在都深套...

他们套住，而我各种骚操作之后不仅套的更深，也几乎没啥仓位了....

我总结下来，从巅峰到低谷，有几个绕不开的坎儿，这是每个人都要经历的，而且反复会犯错的...

入奢，吃喝拉撒其实还好，百万豪车千万游艇，再捞的女人也都还好...

author: aaronjmars
quoted_text:
Swarm riders and Swarm-native companies

AI-use even among highly AI-native people is power-law distributed.

There seems to be a new class of people — call them “swarm riders” — who are capable of consistently commanding large swarms of agents to productive ends.

This is a new kind of managerial skill, analogous to the skill it takes to manage large organizations of people, but wholly different in nature and of course more technical.

Based on the swarm riders we know (including many at @Tempo and @Paradigm), these people are capable of productive token spend that is 1000x-10000x higher than median software engineers, and 100x higher than top 5% Claude Code users.

The art of swarm riding is different from software engineering and more akin to machine learning, where practitioners grapple with black box systems: defining reward functions and evals, transmuting non-verifiable problems into verifiable problems, running experiments, etc.

Swarm-native companies are a new class of company founded by and populated by swarm riders. These companies are organized around swarms in a way that conventional companies will struggle to replicate, as the cost of internal human coordination is sand in the gears of an effective swarm. Effective swarm-native companies will define the right reward functions and evals, remove functional and bureaucratic barriers, and then let the swarms cook.

We’ve gotten to see a few swarm-native companies up close — reshaping financial rails @Tempo, building a new gaming platform @Spawn, cyber swarms at Cathedral Systems — and it’s clear these teams wield a significant advantage over pre-AI teams.

Some questions I’ve been wondering about:

1) How fast will swarm riding diffuse through the economy? The implications for token spend could be significant.

2) Can swarms be effectively adopted by existing companies or will it generally track the formation of new swarm-native companies?

3) What becomes scarce as swarm capabilities themselves commoditize (through frontier models becoming better at swarming, swarm capabilities built into harnesses, etc)? Cultures and teams that can define reward functions well and otherwise get out of the way?

quoted_text:
Notetakers hear every word of your call.

Conclave for Mac takes meeting notes for Zoom and Google Meet, from an app on your Mac. No bot joins the call, and names come from the meeting itself. Video attached.

Built at NEAR HACKATHON @NEARProtocol #NEARHackathon

What NEAR does here:
Transcription runs on NEAR AI's private inference inside a TEE. NEAR AI publishes an attestation for each model it runs for us. Conclave checks the transcription model's and the notes model's, for every meeting and live on our trust page, and shows the result as received.

Every finished meeting gets a receipt. The receipt's seal key id should match the one on https://t.co/kqdn2xqDZG. NEAR AI says it signs each transcription inside its enclave but does not yet expose that signature, so no per-request proof is shown.

How the audio moves:
During a recording, Conclave for Mac sends the audio in 15-second pieces to Conclave's server, which runs in a confidential VM on Phala. Each piece is stored encrypted while the meeting is processed.

Try it on macOS 14.2+: download at https://t.co/35sSDkA1EF, sign in with Google, record a call. 3 hours free every month. Headphones give the cleanest transcript.

Code: https://t.co/EiiCDJi08F

Coinbase COO @emiliemc thinks all leadership coaches suck. But one of them did teach her how to criticize her boss:

"We had somebody who helped Brian and me forge some new paths in terms of understanding one another. What frustrates us, irritates us, and being able to have a way to talk about that with one another.

In the early days we got very methodical about the little systems we did with this coach.

Today, every week when we have our weekly one-on-one, we have a section for juicy feedback. It forces us to have constructive feedback to share.

Brian could say, 'I actually didn't like the way you talked about this thing in the all-hands.' Or, 'This bothered me this week.'

He's said to me before, 'I think you're being a little too hard on this person in product about this thing. I just want you to realize, he's taking it hard. Whether or not you want that, he's taking it.'

text:
Wintermute is literally paying $10M a year to legally front-run everyone on Hyperliquid and it’s completely destroying altcoin liquidity

Bloomberg finally exposed what HFT desks have been screaming about for weeks. Hyperliquid’s gossip priority auctions let top funds see incoming orders 50–60ms before anyone else on the network

Look at how completely broken this setup is:

-> One Wintermute wallet won ~76% of the top slots last month, burning ~$26k every single day just to starve out competition
-> HL claims the auction is open to everyone. Complete BS. You only get that 60ms head start if you have direct peering with Foundation nodes, which requires 0.5% of total maker volume and 10k HYPE staked ($700k+)
-> Smaller MMs are getting sniped nonstop and just unplugging their bots on alts
-> Retail gets stuck with the bill: across 86 altcoin pairs, order book depth on HL imploded by 82% while spreads blew out from 2.13 to 3.55 bps

Honestly, I don't even blame Wintermute. If I had their balance sheet, I would milk this exact loophole until someone forced me to stop

The blame sits 100% on the protocol design. Burning auction fees is cool for $HYPE holders, sure, but letting one fund buy a monopoly on data speed turns a decentralized exchange into a rigged casino

Scrap read-priority auctions completely or make the slots equal, because right now altcoin execution on HL is absolute garbage

On @Tensorcash, proofs are live on mainnet today. In an independent run by @boblabs_eu on Qwen3.8-27B, tuned software measured −1.1% to +0.3% GPU time.

Each proof records, among other things, the exact model and version, its precision, its sampling settings and the scores behind every token. It is also tied to the latest block, so it can’t be reused or prepared in advance.

A first check runs in milliseconds on a CPU. The full check reruns the model and compares the scores. In tests, a different model, a fine-tuned version and a 4-bit quantized version were each caught in 100% of cases, with 0 honest proofs rejected. On mainnet, it already caught a miner running fp8 while declaring bf16.

text:
Hyperliquid's market makers have paid $7.2M to see the market first. 85% of it came from just two firms.

That being said, "rigged casino" and "legal front-running" are overblown framings imho. Wintermute and Selini are simply playing by the rules, like any pnl-driven firm will. But the rules are creating a dynamic worth debating, so here's my attempt at a plain-English version.

First, credit where it's due. HL had a great thing going. Cancels and post-only orders went first, which meant a huge, diverse set of makers could compete on equal terms. That was a big part of why it worked, and it's what DeFi is supposed to be: equal access. Competition leads to better prices.

Priority fees cut against that. HL now auctions off earlier access to market data, and the winners see the book roughly 50-60ms before everyone else. Per @LorisTools , Wintermute has paid $3.54M and Selini $2.63M, out of $7.21M from just 40 payers. Loris puts the top slot at up to $60k a day.

There's a write-side version too. A big enough priority fee on a taker order can now land it alongside makers' cancels, so a maker can get filled on a quote they were trying to pull. This partially breaks the intended cancel prio mechanism.

The result is a vicious cycle. Whoever sees the market first wins the best trades, makes the most money, and can afford to keep paying. Everyone else is quoting a slightly stale book, gets picked off more, and eventually switches off. Fewer makers means thinner books and wider spreads for everyone trading. It hobbles the middle of the pack of market participants.

You can already see it in the data. Depth within 10bps fell 82% on HL vs 61% on Binance. A $10k buy costs 5.2bp on HL vs 2.95bp on Binance. And fewer makers are quoting $1k a side in 58 of 72 markets.

This should matter a lot to everyone. Healthy markets need lots of firms competing, including smaller shops and even retail algo traders, on a level playing field. We took that page from HL's original design and built a 100ms taker speed bump on Bullet, and it's down a solid job so far. Today about 20 retail market makers do around 20% of our maker volume, and we want to keep growing that.

I don't think anyone has a panacea. One further improvement we're exploring comes from TradFi: give everyone the same access, with equal hardware placement and multicast data, so everyone sees the market at the same time. Whatever the right solution is, I don't think a few mil in prio fee revenue is worth the cost of reduced altcoin liquidity and maker diversity as it stands presently.

HL has pushed onchain market structure further than anyone, and I've no doubt the team is already working on this. That's the real edge DeFi has. We can try new market designs and ship them in weeks. Cancel prio would have taken years of regulatory fights to get approved in TradFi. Venues that keep experimenting will find the fair version first.

Wintermute is literally paying $10M a year to legally front-run everyone on Hyperliquid and it’s completely destroying altcoin liquidity

Bloomberg finally exposed what HFT desks have been screaming about for weeks. Hyperliquid’s gossip priority auctions let top funds see incoming orders 50–60ms before anyone else on the network

Look at how completely broken this setup is:

-> One Wintermute wallet won ~76% of the top slots last month, burning ~$26k every single day just to starve out competition
-> HL claims the auction is open to everyone. Complete BS. You only get that 60ms head start if you have direct peering with Foundation nodes, which requires 0.5% of total maker volume and 10k HYPE staked ($700k+)
-> Smaller MMs are getting sniped nonstop and just unplugging their bots on alts
-> Retail gets stuck with the bill: across 86 altcoin pairs, order book depth on HL imploded by 82% while spreads blew out from 2.13 to 3.55 bps

Honestly, I don't even blame Wintermute. If I had their balance sheet, I would milk this exact loophole until someone forced me to stop

The blame sits 100% on the protocol design. Burning auction fees is cool for $HYPE holders, sure, but letting one fund buy a monopoly on data speed turns a decentralized exchange into a rigged casino

Scrap read-priority auctions completely or make the slots equal, because right now altcoin execution on HL is absolute garbage

text:
How to write effective prompts for Grok Imagine Video

Grok Imagine Video 1.5 generates clips of 1–15 seconds with native audio and supports text to video, image to video, and reference to video. The quality of the output depends heavily on how the prompt is written. Below are proven approaches that deliver consistent results.

Optimal prompt structure:

Style and Genr next Subject + Specific Action next Environment next One Camera Movement next Lighting next Sound Cues

The clearer this logic is followed, the more predictable and controlled the result.

What Actually Works

- One main action per clip. Multiple actions in a short clip often lead to distortions and loss of control.
- One clear camera movement. The most reliable options are: slow push-in, static locked shot, gentle pan, slow orbit, and subtle handheld. Combining several camera moves usually reduces quality.
-Specificity over vague adjectives. Instead of beautiful or cinematic, describe concrete lighting, materials, and atmosphere.
- For image to video, describe only the changes. The image already defines composition, characters, and style. The prompt should focus only on motion, camera, and sound.
- Use clear sound cues. The model responds well to specific directions such as soft ambient room tone, distant traffic, or gentle wind. Generic phrases like with audio have little effect.
- Use positive phrasing. It’s more effective to describe what you want rather than using negations ( no blur, don’t move).

Strong prompt examples

Text to video:
Cinematic medium shot of a young woman standing on a windy coastal cliff at golden hour, her hair moving gently in the breeze, soft warm side lighting, slow push in, subtle ambient ocean sounds and distant seagulls.

Image to video (when a frame already exists):
Slow cinematic push-in, she turns her head slightly and smiles, gentle wind in her hair, soft ambient ocean sounds. Lighting and composition remain unchanged.

Additional recommendations

- Ideal prompt length is 40–90 words. Overloaded prompts often perform worse.
- For better character and style consistency, use image-to-video or reference-to-video.
- Longer videos are best created by generating multiple clips and stitching them together (or using the extension feature).

These principles are based on the current capabilities of Grok Imagine Video 1.5 and produce more reliable results than vague or overly complex prompts.

text:
Man do you guys ever feel like you’re living in a different world from everyone around you? It’s this vertigo of seeing so so much and being utterly unable to explain it .. my wife, my friends, even many of those who are interested haven't yet discovered how freakishly deep this rabbit hole goes and all the fascinating implications.

One thing that’s changed is I am OBSESSED with my computer in a way that I haven’t been since we got our first 286. I can’t get enough of it and being away from it creates the kind of fomo that I used to feel for things in the “real world”. When I’m away, I catch myself constantly thinking about the experiments and agents I’ve left running in the background.

And then when stuff goes right, really right, there is this visceral dopamine hit that I live for. It’s variable schedule rewards ish but way more satisfying than any other casino game because many wins are the baseline for other wins. And most of the wins are more about satisfying curiosity or learning through experimenting than metrics or utility, but who cares. 

The other thing that is so interesting is that we get to go back to all the discussions of how we’ve organized society and the economy and revisit every assumption. Hayek, Burnham, Adam Smith, W Brian Arthur, Jevons … we can model all of their ideas and worlds with agents, we can think about the interplay between humans and machines in these frameworks, and we can ask ourselves which ideas are the winners and losers in a world of economic convexities (i.e. the marginal cost of labor is zero, intelligence goes from scarce to abundant).

Anyways just a crazy crazy time that is intellectually nourishing in a way I’ve never experienced. That's my dispatch for the day from the psychosis frontier .. what a cool moment to be a part of.

text:
黄仁勋走了，英伟达的客户终于敢考虑买别家的芯片了。

《The Information》报道，一家采购英伟达芯片的云厂商高管透露，公司正在认真考虑转向 Google 和 AMD。

最有意思的是后半句：他们早就想分散采购了，但一直不敢，因为怕得罪黄仁勋。

多少有点黑色幽默了。堂堂 AI 算力市场，几百上千亿美元的生意，客户选择供应商，居然还得考虑一位 CEO 的心情。

但这恰恰说明，黄仁勋过去几年建立的权力，早就超出了芯片本身。

英伟达不仅掌握着最紧俏的 GPU，还通过投资、信贷担保、采购承诺，把自己变成了许多 AI 云厂商的重要资金支持者。它既卖铲子，又帮客户融资买铲子，有时候甚至还负责租下客户挖出来的坑。

在这种关系里，采购决策就不只是性价比问题了。你当然可以用 AMD，可以考虑 Google TPU，但万一因此失去了英伟达的支持呢？

技术垄断已经很厉害了，更厉害的是让客户形成一种心理：我最好别惹它。

更讽刺的是，那位高管现在又开始担心，黄仁勋离开之后，英伟达未来几代芯片的研发会不会受到影响。

以前是不敢换，现在是怕不换。

当然，这不意味着英伟达的客户会立刻集体倒戈。CUDA 生态、芯片性能和现有部署规模，依然是真实存在的竞争壁垒。至少短期内，英伟达并不缺买家。

但我觉得，这件事暴露了一个比市场份额更有意思的问题：

过去 33 年，黄仁勋究竟是在为英伟达建立一家不依赖任何人的伟大公司，还是在建立一个所有人都必须围着他转的商业帝国？

两者在他掌权时看起来几乎没有区别。

直到他离开，客户才敢把另一家的产品报价单拿出来。
