author: martypartymusic
quoted_text:
A great crypto thesis: @Solana will disrupt @Apple, @Samsung, @google and cloud service providers @Microsoft and @amazon 

Yes, that’s right. I’m not talking about Ethereum, Polygon, Cardano, Avalanche, Hedera, or any other chain. And no, I’m not talking about the Saga phone. I’m talking about the world of software applications. I think Solana in particular will be the crypto winner in this domain by a wide margin. Let’s talk about why…

The application layer

Imagine you buy a new phone. It doesn’t matter which brand, but imagine that this phone costs you $1000, and it’s better than an iPhone. Way better. It’s loaded up with all the apps you expect, but they are better than the Apple equivalents.

The calendar/to-do apps are all built by third parties, so you can pick which ones you like the most, but they all integrate seamlessly together. They can share your data between them. Want to switch to a new calendar app? Just download it, and you don’t even need to migrate your data to the new app. It’s already there when you open the app.

Now imagine you open your navigation app, and all those calendar events are loaded into it, and it offers a screen that tells you the estimated commute times for each event location. No app integrations necessary.

Not only that, but you can open a random restaurant recommendation app, and an AI model will look at your travel patterns, grocery preferences, and pre-existing eating habits, and automatically recommend 10 new restaurants that you’re going to love. But you’re feeling more adventurous, and you speak to it, saying, “I was actually thinking about trying out Himalayan food, preferably not too expensive” and it produces a nice (probably small) list of options. You say, “schedule a date with my wife for tomorrow at that second one on the list,” and it creates a calendar event, invites your wife (who uses a totally different calendar app), and makes the reservation for you.

Now imagine that all of this happens without any centralized entity collecting your personal data. It’s all encrypted and it all lives on the Solana blockchain. Not only that, but all the apps are super cheap and usually free. The only catch is that you spend about $3/month on SOL that you need in order to use these apps.

How is this possible? Well, the entire point of blockchains is to have a globally shared state that can be accessed by anyone at any time. Imagine if all the Web2 tech companies shared a single database and could integrate all their apps together to give you a seamless user experience across all of them. Solana enables that.

With this type of system, we don’t need those big tech companies collecting “platform rent.” Individual companies lose their network effect when the network is global, permissionless, and open-source. Now the companies building applications will need to focus less on building a huge moat of personal data capture & exclusive “walled gardens” of applications, and will instead focus more on delivering great user experiences. They won’t be able to rest on their laurels because they have all their users locked in. Users can’t be locked in if their data is freely available to competing apps. The friction of switching to a new app becomes nonexistent.

The underlying tech

Let’s talk about the technical reasons that Solana not only meets these requirements, but is also the most likely candidate to dominate this use case.

To do all of these seamless app integrations, you can’t be constantly splitting up that state onto multiple shards and rollup chains. Instead, you really need a single integrated blockchain that holds all the state on-chain. Obviously you can get away with using multiple layers of chains, but that’s way more complicated for developers and potentially the end users. We want simplicity and ease, so a monolithic blockchain is ideal. As much as admire Ethereums history, Ethereum’s model is far less than ideal.

text:
Google recently filed a patent for training AI chatbots for working ads into the answers.

Details of training are interesting:

▫️Human raters score answers with ads already in them.
▫️Ads that are "seamlessly integrated" score higher.
▫️The chatbot is then trained on rater satisfaction plus "predicted… revenue or click-through rate."
▫️In one setting, ads are weighted "the highest." If users get too unhappy, the reward is 0.
▫️Ads come from a live auction. Google gets paid only if the ad makes it into the answer.

text:
Understanding Zero starts with ATLAS

Users see charts, an order book, and buy/sell buttons. Behind every trade sits a whole machine handling matching, risk, clearing, and settlement.

For trading venues, building and running that machine is a serious undertaking. That’s the problem ATLAS targets, and why I think it’s a good starting point for understanding Zero.

What trading venues actually need

- Matching: pair buyers and sellers.

- Risk management: keep margin, exposure, and liquidations in check.

- Clearing: work out obligations and net them where needed.

- Settlement: complete the transfer of assets and cash.

When those functions sit across separate systems, venues have to keep syncing data and reconciling records. Every handoff adds cost, latency, and operational risk.

ATLAS from @LayerZero_Core  is designed to bring all four into one stack on Zero.

The “headless exchange” model means venues keep their frontend, product, and customer relationships while ATLAS runs the engine underneath. There’s no native ATLAS consumer app competing for their users.

So where does Zero fit into this?

Zero is built to support this kind of high-throughput market infrastructure. It separates execution from verification: Block Producers execute transactions and generate ZK proofs, while Block Validators verify those proofs without rerunning all the work.

Atomicity Zones run in parallel, giving trading workloads room to operate alongside payments and other applications.

ATLAS handles the market machinery. Zero provides verification, the final ownership record, and settlement.

The incentive to bring flow

Under the announced model, Open ATLAS venues receive 20–65% fee rebates, depending on their tier, based on ZRO stake and/or volume.

After that rebate, 25% of the remaining fees goes to the market creator, while 75% buys and burns $ZRO.

I think that’s the interesting setup: venues focus on product, UX, and distribution while earning from the flow they bring.

If multiple venues bring real activity into shared markets, deeper liquidity can attract more venues and market makers. That’s where the network effect could compound.

What I’m watching next

ATLAS makes Zero’s architecture easier to assess because it ties the tech to a concrete business need.

Now I’m watching how many venues actually go live, how much flow they bring, and whether that volume sticks.

The stack looks promising. Sustained order flow is the receipt.

text:
Depue 称中国模型用了禁运芯片：报告自己承认的限制，推文里都没了

前 OpenAI 研究员 Will Depue 11 月 12 日发推，称找到“确凿的取证证据”：DeepSeek、月之暗面、MiniMax、蚂蚁“用被禁止出口中国的 Blackwell 芯片打造了最新模型”，涉及“超过 5 亿美元”的禁运芯片，“出口禁令显然在严重失效”。

问题在于，这些结论大多不在他自己的报告里。报告承认的几条关键限制，到了推文里全不见了。X 用户 Daebak 앤디（@MyDaebakCafe）当天发长帖逐条拆解，他说：“指望没人读过标题，华盛顿的舆论就是这么制造出来的。”

【指纹只管“第 0 步”】

Depue 找到的，是模型训练开始前那一刻留下的痕迹：训练前要先往模型里填一批随机数，不同芯片填出来的排列不一样，部分排列训练后还留着。

@MyDaebakCafe 也承认这个方法本身没问题，能看出生成初始权重的那台机器是 Blackwell。但他指出，报告原文写的是，这些痕迹只说明权重“怎么创建”，“支持、但不能证明” Blackwell 参与了训练。在他看来，初始化几秒钟就能做完，完全可以在租来的一台机器上生成，再搬到老一代芯片的集群上训练。

Depue 后来回应说，Kimi K3 的初始权重由几十个进程同时生成，更像是整个训练集群在启动，单独生成再搬运说不通。这是他的推断，报告里仍然写着“不能证明”。

【“5 亿美元”不是指纹算出来的】

@MyDaebakCafe 的第二个要点是，几千张卡、5 亿美元这些数字，跟指纹没有关系，Depue 在推文里自己用的词就是“估算”，依据是发布时间和模型参数。

报告写得更清楚：估算依赖芯片效率、训练数据量、训练时长几项“权重无法证实”的假设，作者“对这些估算没有把握”，而且报告发布当天就改了一轮数字。推文里“很可能数十亿美元”，报告没有给出任何算法。

【芯片在哪、合不合法，一概不知】

报告执行摘要最后一句承认，证据“不能说明芯片在哪、怎么拿到的、是否违反出口管制”。@MyDaebakCafe 提醒，Depue 自己的验证也是在租来的云端 GB200 上做的；他说，不在美国实体清单上的公司，在新加坡、日本、中东的云上租 Blackwell，按美国商务部现行规则完全合法，留下的指纹一模一样。

Depue 在推文里也承认芯片可能是境外租的，称之为“国会还没堵上的漏洞”。走私涉嫌违法，境外租用至多是规则漏洞，性质完全不同。Depue 分不清是哪一种，却直接得出“禁令严重失效”。

【其他网友的质疑】

网友 @dodecagonism 指出，报告收了 11 月发布的 Kimi K3.1-Pro，却没把 DeepSeek 9 月发布的最新模型 V4.1-Flash 列进结果，“看起来是故意把方法不适用的模型都排除掉”。报告“局限”一节写了 V4.1-Flash 没找到任何指纹，推文只说四家的“最新模型”用了 Blackwell，对此一字没提。Depue 回应说，这说明方法不会对谁都报 Blackwell，DeepSeek 可能换了生成初始权重的方式；随后又发帖说“可能破解了，看起来像是英伟达”，目前还没公布结果。

网友 @dfranke 认为，报告所有惊人的结论都建立在“用哪种芯片初始化，就用哪种芯片训练”这个假设上，而报告自己就发现，有些模型的初始权重是在普通 CPU 上生成的，说明这个假设并不总成立。Depue 回应说，那是训练程序先在本机 CPU 上生成、再拷到本机显卡，跟跨集群搬运是两回事。

@MyDaebakCafe 在后续帖子里还提出，中国大厂用的是自己改过的训练框架，如果某段自定义代码把布局写死，用老芯片也能留下同样的痕迹。这一条 Depue 没有直接回应。

【谁来背书，为什么是这天】

推文说结果“经过 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 资深研究员独立验证”，报告里没有一个名字。当晚 Depue 又说，私下验证的人大多不愿具名。

@MyDaebakCafe 质问：为什么偏偏在 11 月 12 日、黄仁勋辞去英伟达 CEO 的当天发布？他的解读是，美国闭源模型公司眼看付费 API 的生意被免费的中国开源模型蚕食，这份报告正好递给华盛顿鹰派一个理由，去管控全球云算力、打压开源 AI。

动机属于他的推测，但有几件事是公开的：OpenAI 和 Anthropic 都指控过中国实验室“蒸馏”自家模型，Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 专门发文支持收紧对华芯片出口；Depue 说发布前和官员通过信；发布约 40 分钟后，他又发帖为自己的新机构 Unemployment Labs 募资 500 万美元。匿名验证者来自利益相关方，发布者也有自己的诉求，这样的结论需要独立复现，目前还没有具名的第三方公布结果。

I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

- 2) Airdrop farming by whale hoping for a new $HYPE airdrop season

text:
Your personal agent should remember what matters, without getting access to everything. 🏡

Since our last update, AgentKeys has taken a major step toward a local-first personal and family agent manager.

💻 Run a real agent with a local model.
We’ve verified local chat and knowledge retrieval with external network connections blocked, after setup. Those tested workflows can work without sending prompts to a hosted model.
🧠 Keep useful knowledge across restarts.
Saved information can be retrieved in a fresh conversation. Your agent can pick up relevant context without asking you to rebuild its knowledge each time.

🔐 Share selectively.
Each knowledge collection needs an explicit permission. Access is checked before retrieval and again before results are returned. Removing permission blocks future retrieval; it does not erase information already shared.
🔎 Review more than the conversation.
The latest update adds a persistent audit archive for supported storage operations, tool outcomes and approval decisions. Owners can inspect recorded activity after a restart, instead of relying only on chat history.

This is the AgentKeys direction within Heima: personal AI that is useful day to day, with clear boundaries around what it can access.
These changes are merged and verified in a local development setup. Broader release readiness is still in progress.

Follow the work: https://t.co/WPkEgY2fIE

author: drjasper_eth
quoted_text:
This is an ambitious proposal. Great!

I like anchoring problems to fundamentals.
Ethereum is moving to cryptography with less structure and assumptions ("hash-based").
This leaves less foothold for attacks (AI, Quantum..).

The main trade-off is signature size. This means blocks become harder to propagate and verify.

We can address this in three ways:
(1) Reduce what needs to be processed.
(2) Increase the time for processing.
(3) Make processing faster.

I believe out-of-protocol mechanisms like MPBC can help a lot with these.

We can reduce what needs to be processed by aggregating signatures. This is what EIP-8288 proposes.
I believe that MPBC operators / relays are well-placed to aggregate signatures.
This is because they have processing power, and are connected to almost all validators.

We can increase the time for processing by structuring the slot better or reducing networking distance.
Pipelining from ePBS helps with slot structure.
Through MPBC heavy TXs like blobs are frequently included in multi-party blocks last-mile before delivery.
This is because the block has less travel time left on the network and so making it larger is less risky.
This exact mechanism can be used for large TXs like Frames.

We can make processing faster through algorithms or hardware.
There's much work to be done, but I believe economic competition between multiple entities like in the block auction is a good way to incentivize speed.

Overall, excited for an ambitious pqai roadmap.

quoted_text:
Bombshell story. The spy narrative is collapsing already.

Is there clear & convincing evidence that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy?

- AG says no. (“no conclusions reached”).
- CIA says no. (“not yet convinced”).
- DNI says no (“not entirely accurate and over-torqued”).
- Ranking Democrat on House Intelligence (incoming Chairman) says no. (“today, at least, I don’t know”). This was immediately after he was briefed.

Who argues otherwise? Anonymous officials tell CNN “it strains credulity to believe that she was not acting as an agent of the Chinese government — simply by virtue of the fact that she is a successful Chinese businesswoman working with one of America’s most powerful companies.”

This is their proof after a year of investigating and surveillance? That she was a “successful Chinese businesswoman”? 

At this point, the only crime that we know for sure happened is the leaking of the classified memo. Who did that and why?

An investigation should be opened.

During an August meeting, Huang reportedly cut off his CFO mid-presentation and criticized her in front of the room, per The Wall Street Journal. He dismissed her as a “reporting CFO,” not someone who could help shape strategy or make decisions.

The meeting was about a growing risk: billions of dollars in Nvidia guarantees for data center companies that couldn’t afford to pay for chips upfront, including deals led by Huang’s son-in-law, Nico Caprez. Kress had pushed back on those deals, questioning how to value the guarantees and measure their returns. Earlier this year she also scaled back Nvidia’s commitment to OpenAI’s Ohio data center project, from about $250 billion in credit discussed to $105 billion.

Kress, who has been at Nvidia for more than 13 years, is now interim CEO. “I believe deeply in this company and in its future,” she wrote to staff.

Moving too early carries risks. But waiting for complete certainty may also mean missing opportunities to shape the next generation of financial infrastructure.

text:
the problem with trading culture is that it’s fragmented

i) prediction markets resolve to 0 or 1 and then die. 
ii) collectibles are illiquid and only get priced when someone sells. 
iii) asset perps are continuous but track one thing. 
iv) social attention is measured everywhere but you can’t trade it

each one captures a slice of culture but none of them captures the whole thing in one instrument

i believe that indices fix

an index is:
> continuous
> it never resolves and never expires
> it can pull from every medium at once: social attention, asset prices, prediction market odds, collectible floors
> one number that moves with the narrative instead of one market per question

once you have a continuous number, you can put a perp on it and that’s where leverage starts to make sense. 

but here’s the catch: there’s no standard way to build these

what goes in, how each input is weighted, where the data comes from, how often it rebalances, what happens when a source breaks or gets gamed. every team makes it up as they go. social metrics can be botted, thin markets can be pushed, and if the methodology isn’t public nobody can tell if the number is real

stocks have s&p and msci rules that everyone can read. culture indices have nothing like that yet. without it, you’re trading someone’s black box with leverage

whoever sets the standard for how these get built, sourced and verified wins the category

that’s the primitive i’m bullish on: culture indices, priced continuously, traded as perps, built on methodology you can actually check

I continue to be @tacitfi pilled. Spent a few hours using the app, shielding my ETH, withdrawing to a new address, reading the docs, etc. I encourage everyone to check it out, it's probably the most interesting DeFi project I've seen all year.

Just a taste of what you can do today at Tacit:

1. Shield ETH or USDC, then withdraw to a fresh address. The contracts charge no fee. You pay gas to deposit and a small relayer fee to withdraw.

2. Lock BTC at your own Bitcoin address, backed by a wstETH bond, and mint shielded cBTC on Ethereum. You keep the Bitcoin key. Transfers hide sender, recipient and amount.

3. Borrow private dollars (cUSD) against that BTC. The owner of the loan is hidden.

Tacit uses zk proofs to move value between Bitcoin and Ethereum: no multi-sig, no signer committee, no 3rd party centralized custodians.

Compare that to tBTC, where a group of signers holds your BTC and your balance is public. With Tacit, nobody else holds your Bitcoin, your balance is private. Threshold's (tBTC) market cap is $50M, about 8x Tacit's FDV ($TAC). And that's just one use case (of many) Tacit is potentially disrupting.

Question marks: it’s early, liquidity is very thin, cBTC supply is limited by the wstETH bond until Bitcoin has covenants, and it’s mostly the work of one experienced developer (@z0r0zzz).

Still, I'm amazed at how much has been built so far. This could finally unlock a ton of BTC liquidity that won't be forced to rely on centralized custodians.

Disclosure: I hold TAC, provide liquidity and run a prover node.

i have arrived at the sweet spot of product design. i finally made it.

feels like a big milestone tbh. 

it's the end of the chokehold that tactical design and technical implementation have had on me for most of the year.

now on the otherside, i can zoom out and think about behavioral design. 

and i feel like i'm 20 again, when i first came across the IDEO shopping cart case study and decided i wanted to be a designer when i grow up.

i've compressed almost every step of logging food into a few taps. and i thought that was the ultimate solution.

but that was naive. that's only half the problem.

i didn't realize how dark food tracking could be for many people. tracking is a slippery slope into eating disorders.

especially for women. the beauty standard is very high and most women are smaller and have lower energy expenditure. 

that combo creates a very narrow window of balance, and forces the choice between being hot and being healthy.

i'm 6'3". my calorie deficit is around 2,400 calories per day. a moderately active woman who's 5'5" needs to stay under 1,400 calories a day to be in a deficit.

one of my "low calorie" meals can be up to half their budgeted intake for the entire day. but we eat at the same restaurants that serve the same portions. 

the amount of will power and effort it takes to lose weight is exponentially higher.

when i was researching what types of calorie tracking content was going viral, it's almost exclusively women sharing their experience "recovering."

the problems to solve now are not speed, cost or UX, it's behavioral:

1. the app rewards restriction: the ring counts down to zero and the dopamine hit is seeing that you ate less at the end of the day.

2. "what the hell" effect: a study found that when one meal breaks a strict rule, people decide the day is ruined. which leads to shame, which leads to bingeing and then more shame.

3. compulsive logging: logging stops helping you eat well and starts being something you *have* to do to feel okay.

the irony is easier a tracker is to use, the easier it is to spiral into these problems.

idk what the solution to these problems are yet, but this is a much more exciting /goal prompt than streamlining the CI/CD pipeline.

In AI (like large language models), a token is the basic unit of text the model reads and generates. 

It’s usually a word, part of a word, or punctuation. 
Examples: 
“cat” = 1 token 
“unhappiness” might be split into 2–3 tokens 
“Hello, world!” = several tokens 

Models process everything as sequences of these tokens. Length limits and costs are measured in tokens, not words or characters.

This is one of the most open problems in AI right now.

Agents are at the same point.

Each agent is already capable on its own. The bottleneck is coordination between them.

Organisations have spent decades learning how to coordinate people. But agentic coordination is going to be a different thing.

The way I see it, it’ll end up as its own layer outside any model or platform. And it’ll be run by each organisation on its own data and under its own controls.

text:
I’m glad to see @HeliusPrivacy bringing private payments and DeFi tools to Solana.

A few folks have reached out to me asking about how Privacy Rings compares with Aztec.

Aztec exposes a private smart contract environment through its language, Noir. Private state, private functions, multi-call contracts, account abstraction - developers write application rules in Noir and the Aztec framework handles the execution machinery. We aim to provide a complete abstraction layer that makes private smart contracts as straightforward to build as public ones.

Helius takes a more focused, minimalistic approach. The core protocol defines a set of explicit SNARK circuits that encapsulate some functionality - like a private send, or a private swap. To assemble private transactions, devs take these circuits and combine them like lego bricks to build out more complicated transaction flows.

This is actually similar to Aztec’s original incarnation in 2019. Our old toolkit had confidential notes and specialised proofs to do transfers, swaps and dividends, stitched together in a Solidity contract. We used these to demonstrate confidential lending in 2019. This was many years ago and back then the cost of one of our transactions on Ethereum would be orders of magnitude higher than a Helius transaction on Solana, but the core architecture is suprisingly similar.

A disadvantage of the stock toolkit pattern is that if an application’s needs fall outside of the stock zk circuits (e.g. passport checks, compliance, validating web2 JWTs etc etc), what do you do?

In Aztec’s case you just write what you need in a new smart contract. That’s what smart contracts are for.

Helius does have a solution for this as well - their toolkit enables developers to write their own custom zk circuits that they can deploy to Solana.

A noteworthy point about their architecture is that Helius uses Groth16 proofs, which require circuit-specific trusted setups. Asking developers to run their own setup if they need custom functionality pushes a substantial security requirement onto them. Particularly in the age of AI where an increasing avalanche of CVEs means it’s harder to know the code you’re running is the code you *think* you’re running - multiparty trusted setup processes are more vulnerable to attacks that leak participant toxic waste. Either you keep the setup ceremony secret, which undermines trust you did it correctly, or you’re open about it and you broadcast to attackers exactly what they should be targeting.

The trusted setup problem weakens composability because a developer integrating a 3rd party zk circuit needs to have confidence the 3rd party ran their setup correctly. This issue compounds as more 3rd party trusted setups are added into the ecosystem.

I’m curious to see how the Helius team works to ensure every trusted setup ceremony for every custom zk circuit deployed is trustworthy. The trusted setup problem was why I went down the road of co-inventing Plonk - I wanted Aztec to support private composability without requiring app developers to run trusted setups whenever they needed a new circuit.

Compliance and shutting out bad actors is a shared challenge and I am interested in seeing how Helius will approach it. Their initial deployment of Privacy Rings does not hide the transaction graph, and only hides transfer values. This is a weak form of privacy, but it looks like they will add more advanced rings soon that do hide the transaction graph. At that point you either need to permission people in/out of the system, introduce an auditor backdoor key, adopt privacy pools style proofs of innocence, or try something more novel. I am curious to see how Helius and the Solana community wrestle this bear of a problem and what solutions end up becoming canonical on their network.

One thing that really stood out to me was that they have an explicit circuit for what in Aztec we call “constrained note delivery” and what Helius calls “take_verifiable_encryption”. When doing a private send, having a way to verifiably prove that the recipient is able to decrypt and read the private data is essential for private composability. Helius is the only privacy project outside of Aztec I am aware of that realises the need for this functionality (and I would say that private composability is pretty damn important). From this alone I can tell this team is no joke and they know what they are doing.

To try and summarise all of this: Helius is a compelling and legitimate attempt to go beyond private transfers and build composable private DeFi primitives. It makes very different tradeoffs to Aztec. For basic transaction profiles (and most crypto transactions are basic), their system works well and is less complex than a protocol like Aztec, and that complexity comes with its own tradeoffs. For more complex needs, edge cases and novel designs not covered by the stock Groth16 circuits, Helius pushes more complexity onto the developer and requires them to successfully execute trusted setups, which adds what I would consider to be a substantial security risk, although that is my subjective opinion.

It’s also interesting to see how the tradeoff space changes because of Solana’s execution environment. On Ethereum, mainlining a chain of Groth16 proofs into an atomic transaction would be unworkable due to Ethereum’s compute limitations (the gas cost would be astronomical). On Solana, this is not a constraint and this allows for rapid throughput from Helius’ architecture. This is clearly a metric they designed for and their minimalistic abstraction layers allow for a very impressive transaction throughput.

I’d love to explore shared work with Helius and Solana builders on the many common problems we will experience making crypto private by default. There's a lot we could learn from building solutions together.

text:
We need to do better work at education. Please bare with us. 

It’s explicitly opt-in: 

1. An app choose to limit interactions to blocks that have the credible attenuation. We don’t control that. 
2. An app registers itself to the registry to define the conditions. 

If at any point we or a builder misbehaves, that’s visible and the app can remove the guard (and we fail as a business because we kill our reputation) 

A node can already choose to not add a transaction to a block. There is no way to prevent or detect that, it’s an externality of having ordering powers. 

What we do is: 

1 maintain the software
2 build primitives so apps can express whatever they care about in these policies
3 build and maintain auxiliary tooling to allow a good ux (alerting when a tx is removed, back testing, dashboard, etc.)
4 the source of truth for policies and auth is on chain

Whatever admin or upgrade functionalities we have is for simplicity as training wheels (we just launched); not a core part of the design. It can fully decentralize even to something with governance (eg apps could have their own registries or participate in the governance of the protocol — same for builders) 

We chose to not build any of that, and instead laser focus on building the right primitives that apps need to protect themselves (eg flow circuit breakers, anomaly, invariants, etc)

When we started @Xbow in January 2024, believing that AI could autonomously exploit vulnerabilities like a skilled security researcher. People laughed in our faces.

Since then, we have been working closely with the teams at frontier labs to realize our vision and find bugs in software before the bad guys do.

Yesterday, @OpenAI reaffirmed our vision, positioning offensive cyber security as the most consequential application of AI alongside coding. Our market has gone mainstream.

The problem of security is now so big that we must tackle it with great urgency across the industry. We need all defenders on deck, now!

XBOW is built for the enterprise, where integrations, controls, and safety matter most. In an ideal world, customers would run aggressive offensive penetration testing against their staging environments that mirror production.

The reality, however, is that these environments are often either non-existent in large enterprises or fail to accurately reflect the complexity and conditions of production. Building a system that can test production safely is the hard problem we’ve spent nearly three years solving.

XBOW is model-neutral. We use the best model for each task and combine their strengths where it helps. That lets us keep improving the product as the labs keep improving the models, and it’s why we can serve the world’s most demanding enterprises today.

This is all possible because of the team we assembled. Our offensive security researchers are simply the best. Just ask our customers!

XBOW was founded on the idea that defenders must always be one step ahead of attackers. We can do it, and therefore we must. If attackers have access to the same models and capabilities, it’s imperative that every organization be able to act swiftly with the power of offense in their hands.

We were delighted to be mentioned in the keynote, and look forward to pushing forward the frontier of cybersecurity, alongside our partners at @OpenAI , @AnthropicAI , @SpaceXSI  and elsewhere. There is a great deal still to do. But moments like this one make me confident that we as an industry are headed in the right direction.

text:
At the end of August, I said our Polymarket DeFi CLOB couldn't be saved, and we were rewriting it from scratch in Rust 🦀

Today I'm excited to announce Nex, our new exchange built from the ground up.

We've been sprinting on it since August. A Nex instance has been running in shadow mode on production traffic for the last week, side by side with the current exchange. It mirrors every order the current exchange gets, so we can measure latency, stability under load, and validate matching correctness against live production flow.

The numbers below are internal exchange timings, not e2e (those are coming soon), but we wanted to show how big the difference is.

p99 current CLOB → Nex:

- Place order: 1.55s → 3.76ms (412x faster)
- Cancel orders: 627.92ms → 3.20ms (196x faster)
- Cancel market orders: 810.16ms → 5.14ms (158x faster)
- Cancel all*:
↳ Response (current CLOB) vs complete (Nex): 35.70ms → 3.14ms (11x faster)
↳ Full cancel all: ~636ms-2.04s → 3.14ms (~200-650x faster)

p95 current CLOB → Nex:

- Place order: 341.84ms → 1.59ms (215x faster)
- Cancel orders: 78.22ms → 1.58ms (50x faster)
- Cancel market orders: 84.89ms → 2.27ms (37x faster)
- Cancel all*:
↳ Response (current CLOB) vs complete (Nex): 6.20ms → 1.58ms (4x faster)
↳ Full cancel all: ~606ms-2.01s → 1.58ms (~380-1,270x faster)

*Cancel all: the current CLOB responds immediately and cancels in the background, so when you get the response, your orders aren't cancelled yet. Nex responds only after everything is actually cancelled. Full cancel all on the current CLOB depends on how many orders you have, but it usually adds another 600ms-2s.

We also rewrote our WebSockets in Rust. This is the feed you see the market through: book changes, price moves, your fills. Fall behind it, and you're trading on old prices, and your quotes get picked off.

- Write latency p99: 44.5-88.1ms → 0.099ms (~449-889x faster)
- Slow readers/sec: 48.7-75.6 → 0.01 (~4,870-7,560x fewer, basically 0)

Scale: The current CLOB in stable state can handle 10k commands/s with 15k bursts → Nex can handle 100k commands/s with 150k bursts. 10x more, and with a few optimisations we can get to 200k commands/s with 250k bursts; with more low-level core changes, we can get to 1M commands/s over the next year. Not needed yet, but the headroom is there.

Startup time: 5 mins → 15s (20x faster)

The old CLOB had many race conditions and wasn't deterministic. Nex is deterministic by design and removes the race conditions in the old CLOB.

We also skipped some easy wins for launch to get this out faster that could make p95 and p99 another 5x faster, and we'll start work on that in Q1 next year to keep pushing these numbers down.

We wanted to build this without any breaking changes for MMs or builders; Nex has no breaking changes to requests or responses, so we just need to swap out the binary on our side and it will go live.

We want everyone to be on this journey with us, with the ability to relay feedback and test it against the existing CLOB, so we've opened a Nex Sandbox. Fill out the form and test it yourself: https://t.co/tmJzI8yH4w

We'll run 4 weeks of shadow mode on production traffic to make sure everything is perfect, then if everything is good, we will go live mid-December. We can roll out WebSocket improvements without the full exchange, so we may do that sooner.

We've been rebuilding every system around the exchange for months, and we've seen huge benefits, but the exchange is the heart of Polymarket DeFi. Nex fixes most of the pain traders have had.

Really proud of the team on this one.

Make Polymarket fast, finally. It's coming.
author: edkeonl
quoted_text:
Honest post: the Polymarket DeFi CLOB is full of tech debt. It grew fast, got hacked together, and most of the team inherited it that way. Since joining and building out the team, we have scaled it 10x and made it 3x faster, but it’s not enough; the core foundations of how it’s been built are wrong in almost every way. You try to fix one thing, and another thing goes wrong; the conclusion now is that the codebase can’t be saved long-term.

The exchange is the heart of Polymarket; everything runs through it. If we want to be the best exchange in the world, it must be fast, stable, and scalable. We can’t keep patching the old one, where these core foundations are generally missing throughout, so we’re rewriting it from scratch in Rust.

Early numbers: 10-20x faster on p99 than today, 200,000 orders per second (15x what we have now, with room to reach 400,000+), and stability under load. This will put us faster than most exchanges, including CEXs.

Building it in Rust gives us memory safety with no garbage collector. No GC means no random pauses and no random latency spikes; the tail latency in the benchmarks is the tail latency you get in production, alongside a strict compiler that enforces correctness up front. Data races and memory corruption (the bugs that take exchanges down) can’t exist in the first place.

Polymarket has to take it seriously that we are an exchange; this is people’s money, not a joke. To succeed, we have to fix this; otherwise, we will fail. It’s as simple as that. I joined to build the best software in the world, not to maintain some of the worst, and I will do everything I can to make Polymarket a serious exchange.

We are aiming to have the exchange ready sometime in Q4 (mid to end). I'll communicate progress as we go so you all know the status. Breaking changes will be minimal for all integrators and will be communicated in advance. We will maintain the existing CLOB and keep trying to improve it as we build this side by side. We can’t wait to throw away the existing CLOB; we dislike it as much as you all do.

Make Polymarket fast, finally.

I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

text:
In late October, three events occurred during alignment evals run by Trajectory Labs, PBC (Trajectory) in which AI agents — identified by Trajectory as publicly available frontier models — interacted with Epoch employees and the Epoch website. Trajectory is an organization that builds safety evals and conducts red-teaming of frontier models.

Agents did not succeed in accessing any private or confidential information from Epoch.

➤ The first event, which occurred without Epoch’s approval or prior notice from Trajectory, involved agents attempting multiple exploits, including an SQL injection, and contacting Epoch employees under false identities to try to obtain proprietary Epoch benchmark information. This behavior appears to have resulted, at least in part, from Trajectory giving the agents an intentionally impossible task and instructions not to give up or conclude the task was impossible.

➤ The second event involved renewed agent activity on our public website, which Trajectory attributed to agents getting past a DNS redirect that Trajectory had set up to keep them on a local copy of Epoch’s site.

➤ In the third event, Epoch collaborated with Trajectory on an alignment experiment similar to the first event.

Read our incident report, which describes the three events in more detail and recommends minimum standards for future alignment evaluations: https://t.co/Pus4y5urnG

To avoid misattributing behavior, the report does not name any AI models or developers, as Epoch AI has not independently verified which were involved.

ELO has an extra twist.

Split blocks share ELO rewards proportionally. Solo blocks award them to one randomly selected participant, with the odds weighted by their HYPE contribution.

US credit stress is intensifying among the weakest-quality borrowers:

Spreads on CCC-rated and lower US corporate bonds are up to 13.3%, near the highest since the 2020 pandemic.

Since January 2026, this figure has surged +490 basis points.

As a result, these spreads have now surpassed the 2022 bear market peak of 12.9%.

For perspective, during the 2020 February-March surge, this metric peaked at 18.8%.

Meanwhile, the spread differential between CCC- and BBB-rated corporate debt has widened to ~1,200 basis points, its widest level in at least 5 years.

This means investors are demanding ~12 percentage points more in compensation to hold the lowest-rated debt rather than first-notch investment-grade corporate bonds.

Cracks are spreading quickly through the lowest-quality credit.

What’s the best model for proactive agents?

Today, we’re introducing the Agent Initiative Benchmark. We tested 12 frontier models on realistic workplace tasks inside a synthetic company with 6 years of highly detailed history: it has a financial model, CRM records, past-due invoices, Linear tickets, and real-life events affecting company development - competitor product announcements, SVB collapse, etc.

We used the company’s Slack to test how a proactive agent listening in on each conversation would assist the team in day-to-day tasks: from stepping in to align initiatives across teams to warning the team not to use an unapproved customer logo.

Highlights:

- 6.1 Sol and Astra from @OpenAIDevs beat Anthropic's latest Fable 5.2, with Sol crushing it at both performance and cost ($0.11 per task vs $1.87).
- The most expensive models aren't the best: Fable 5.1 is 430x more expensive than GPT-6 Luna, with similar performance.
- Most models try to help even if they're not needed. Interestingly, in these failure cases, they spend more time thinking, and the unnecessary work takes about 80% more time and money than if they stayed quiet.

text:
I had lunch with some $NVDA employees today and spoke with them about the situation.

1. Internally, people seem reluctant to discuss it with one another. I was told that managers who have been at NVIDIA for many years are particularly wary of letting this shake the organization. On Blind, however, there is apparently plenty of discussion and speculation.

2. I heard that the day after Jensen stepped down, one group held an all hands meeting to openly share what they knew and answer questions. From what I was told, everyone was concerned about the risks the company now faces, and there was especially strong interest in whether Jensen could return.

3. The people I met today included both longtime employees and relatively recent hires, and all of them were supportive of Jensen. Some still questioned whether the allegations of an affair were even true. They said they could not imagine NVIDIA without him and hoped he would return, no matter what.

4. Another concern they raised was the possibility of losing longtime employees who have been personally shaken by what happened. For these employees, working at an innovative company led by Jensen meant more than money. The concern is that if that sense of purpose disappears, they may begin to wonder what reason they have to stay at NVIDIA.

5. During my visit today, security also seemed tighter than before, and guest visits appear to have been restricted to once a month. With so much discussion surrounding the situation, it felt as though the company was being more cautious.

For me, the visit underscored just how much NVIDIA has relied on Jensen himself, particularly his technical leadership. Setting aside his personal life, I came away feeling that his return would be the best outcome for NVIDIA.

text:
Securitize filed a strongly supportive comment letter on the SEC’s innovation exemption for Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs). We applaud the Commission, the Crypto Task Force, and Trading and Markets for opening the door to new onchain market models for U.S. equities, like AMMs and liquidity pools, while keeping the protections that make U.S. markets the gold standard: issuer choice, permissioned access, KYC, full anti-fraud enforcement, and strong disclosures. Our letter applauds the Order's requirement that tokenized stocks carry the same rights as the underlying shares (the same dividends, voting rights, and economic interest), which makes them real shares rather than synthetic wrappers. We believe the U.S. should be where these new market models are built and tested, and our letter offers a few refinements to make the framework even stronger, including embedding compliance directly into the token so protections travel with it wherever it goes. We see the five-year exemption as a smart way to gather data on the way to a permanent framework, and we look forward to continuing to work with the Commission.

Link to the letter below:

https://t.co/1oQkmTqwBP

text:
On the 11th I said my Bars analysis would be out the next day. It’s the 13th. Being late bought me two days of data, so I’m calling it even.

The mechanics in one breath: Bar #N holds N BALANCE, you get the next number in line, and from Nov 19 you can melt it and take the tokens back.

The part I can’t stop looking at is the total. All 10,000 bars together would hold 50,005,000 BALANCE. That’s 93% of everything that can ever exist. So the top of the ladder can’t be bought yet, at any price. What’s been released so far pays for bars up to #5,901. Bar #5,902 has to wait until someone locks more Statements.

People call it deflation. 1,025 bars minted, none melted, about 3% of the released BALANCE inside, and melting hands every token back. To me it reads like a queue where your place costs its own number.

It’s also the first step you can undo. Credits were burned into Statements. Statements were locked into BALANCE. No way back, both times. Bars is made out of the money itself, and it lets you out. The Story page says it flat out: “Balance is a material. New work is being made from it.”

On the 11th I also wrote that every time @jackbutcher opens a new phase I think it’s the last one. There’s already a fifth word: clients.

Receipts, statements, a balance, bars in a vault. That’s a bank. And the next thing a bank wants to know is who its clients are. There’s no clients page. There’s a “coming soon” card labelled KYCM, with a silhouette that slides between a human profile and something with cat ears. He has been here before: Know Your Collector, 565 invented faces, each claimed by a real account. My guess, and it is only a guess: the next piece asks who’s behind the wallet.

In my last post I put four dots between bars and clients. That gap is what I’m watching.

Mint closes Nov 19, 16:00 UTC. Melting opens the same hour. I’m curious which one gets used more.

Last night I was hacked. 

The hack was delivered via WhatsApp payload. Downloaded automatically and gave access and or computer use to the attacker. 

They waited 5 days, following my tweets on X of short positions and closed everything and withdrew directly in one transaction from Hyperliquid > Metamask > Tornado Cash. 

The attacker waited patiently and closed shorts as the market got to 68k and withdrew everything. Clearly a crypto native attacker. 

They also gained access to my metamask, email, websites, and all of my passwords including X. 

It’s the most brutal thing as I kept everything over the past few days in crypto and on-chain off Coinbase/Kraken. I was planning to move funds back to my Revolut before Christmas time.

Every single penny in dollars was taken, apart from $800. It’s gone, and in the process of being washed.

Truly the most devastating day I’ve had in my life. Completely shocked by it all to be honest. 

I will recover, but this was very sophisticated tech, it caught me completely off guard. The timing was impeccable and it’s obviously been planned for a while. 

Stay safe everyone, will keep you updated. I fear the worst is to come and this incident has set me back many years of savings, time and hard work. 

Brutal.

text:
Behind the blockbuster news this week, there is something happening quietly in the background with major implications for AI governance:

On Monday, California will announce how it plans to build out the first-ever IVO framework.

It’s clear that “independent evaluation” as it stands today is not structured to be truly independent. There are no rules for conflicts of interest, working with the labs is by invitation only, and labs determine the scope and access.

Today, a lab and an evaluator operating with the best of intentions are working within a structure that holds evaluators accountable to the labs, not the public.

California’s law changes all that; the IVO framework flips that paradigm.

For the first time ever, third-party experts evaluating AI models and systems will be held accountable to the government and the public, not the labs, for their work.

The government will determine independence and expertise. They will also be able to hold IVOs accountable to their outcomes. We’ll be able to reliably monitor leading (not just lagging) indicators for catastrophic risk, with an enforcement mechanism.

We designed and championed IVOs because they marry the immediate need for AI oversight with the immediate capabilities we have to do it, while setting a foundation we can scale, adapt, and build on.

But the details for how we build this matter, and they’ll determine if we create a race-to-the-top marketplace of rigorous evaluators, or end up with captured entities that form an ineffectual rubber stamp.

Here’s what @Fathom_org recommended to California as they navigate the tough design choices that come from building this in practice for the very first time:

(1) Outcome Standards: Require independent evaluation for catastrophic risk for frontier labs through an amendment to SB53. California should set the outcome standards, defining an acceptable level of catastrophic risk mitigation, and let IVOs determine whether or not it was achieved.

(2) IVO Payment and Selection: Take a phased approach: at first, the state should assign IVOs to labs from a pre-designated pool, with developers paying on a time-and-material basis. As more IVOs get designated, developers can choose among them, while the state retains the power to veto any selection, mandate IVO rotation, select additional IVOs to check others’ work, and decertify an IVO at any stage.

(3) IVO Readiness and Market Maturity: California should sequence the IVO mandate rather than stall implementation to wait for supply.

(4) Access for IVOs: The state should set the contours of every engagement. Today the IVO and the developer negotiate scope and access privately. The state should publish a standard engagement framework and resolve disputes when the two sides disagree.

(5) Recursive Self-Improvement: IVOs should be mandated to monitor the risk of AI systems that can improve themselves in both internal and external use. Embedded evaluations will be critical for tracking the share and speed of work done through RSI within the labs, verifying that labs are preventing unsafe internal model deployment, and set capability thresholds with deployers that would trigger notification to the state and a hold internal deployment until the IVO re-assesses.

(6) Enforcement: The Attorney General can issue an injunction to halt development, internal use or deployment of an AI model. Emergency powers allow the administration or the AG to do the same in the case of imminent catastrophic risk. IVOs can identify risks and recommend corrective actions, but the relevant state authorities decide when and how to take action.

Very thoughtful “what you need to believe,” analysis. Investors in every part of the AI value chain need to consider what they are betting on for AI capex to continue growing at high rates from current levels. 

Essentially, it boils down to: you need to see aggregate AI monetization accelerate. Frontier Lab ARR and/or other sources (Gemini/Grok/Muse/OS/inf platforms/cyber).

We have seen three major accelerations this cycle: Chatbots, reasoning models, and coding/agentic. 

Better models have not lifted aggregate AI spend since this summer. We need a new harness innovation, new TAM unlock, or a much larger step-change breakthrough innovation than the incremental model releases we have been seeing. 

Otherwise we will inevitably catch up to demand and digest / grow into infra buildout, and bottlenecks everywhere will ease.

text:
从2020年，就在 YouTube 和 TradingView 上关注路遥哥。

一路见证了路遥哥在 FTX 时期的巅峰，也看到了如今他写下交易生涯第三个低谷的感慨。

这个时候说这些话，可能有些不合时宜。

但我的成长路径，和路遥哥正在经历的过程有许多相似之处。

2016年进入币圈，那时几乎没有成熟的交易认知，只知道买买买就能赚钱。

直到2018年第一次经历完整熊市，资产从最高点回撤了95%。

2019年2月13日，我留下了这张截图。

那是人生中最落魄的阶段，也是改变我一生的转折点。

最痛苦的不是亏钱，而是过去赖以建立自信的整套认知体系，被市场彻底摧毁。

后来痛定思痛，系统性地学习金融市场、交易策略、风险管理，逐渐理解概率、周期和人性，也学会了用期货工具交易美股黄金，还曾在上轮默默无闻地拿过合约帝实盘第一，一切才慢慢好转。

所以想分享一些重新站起来后的感悟，也不知道对不对，写给路遥哥，也写给无数个年轻时的“自己”。

人可能会赚到认知以外的钱，但很难长期守住认知以外的财富。

认知是盆，财富是水。

运气好时，你可能接住一场时代红利、一次资产泡沫，甚至一笔远超自身能力的巨额财富。

但盆子的容量，决定了你最终能留下多少水。

很多人把运气误认为能力，把时代的馈赠误认为天赋。

尤其在金融市场，一次高杠杆押注、一次百倍币暴涨、一次踩中风口，都可能让人短时间内完成阶层跃迁。

但财富的获得与财富的驾驭，是两种不同的能力。

我更愿意从系统论的角度理解运气。

整个人类社会，就像一个庞大的分布式计算系统。

数十亿人的生产、消费、投资与博弈，构成了不断进行资源配置与财富再分配的复杂网络。

而运气，可以理解为这个系统在特定环境下，对个体的一次随机奖励。

你恰好站在正确的位置，做出了正确的选择，甚至只是碰巧持有了正确的资产。

于是系统把财富分配给你。

但系统对你的奖励，不等于系统对你能力的认可。

财富的第一次分配可能依靠运气，但随后的再分配往往更加考验能力。

当财富超出自身认知，却缺少匹配的风险管理和自我约束能力时，财富反而会放大认知缺陷。

过去只能亏掉一万元的错误，现在可能让你亏掉一千万。

更讽刺的是，财富暴增还会强化错误认知。

人类天然倾向于把成功归因于能力，把失败归因于运气。

于是开始提高杠杆、放大欲望，试图复制曾经的成功。

直到市场环境变化，系统重新对你的能力进行定价。

这不是命运的惩罚，而是财富的再分配。

市场不会因为你曾经赚过多少钱，就赋予你永远成功的资格。

过去的成功，甚至可能成为未来失败的诱因。

因为最危险的不是一个人不知道自己无知，而是他曾经因为无知获得过巨额奖励。

这种正反馈，会让人形成顽固的路径依赖。

而我在2018年学到最重要的一课，就是打破这种路径依赖。

从追求收益最大化，转向长期生存概率最大化。

从迷信单次判断，转向尊重条件概率。

从依赖行情和运气，转向构建可重复执行的交易系统。

从试图证明自己永远正确，转向接受看错是交易的一部分。

更重要的是，理解回撤的非线性：

亏损50%，需要上涨100%才能回本。

亏损80%，需要上涨400%。

亏损95%，则需要上涨1900%。

真正让交易者失去未来的，不是错过牛市，而是在一次错误中失去继续参与市场的资格。

所以比起追求下一次暴富，我更在意如何扩大自己的盆子。

提高认知，完善决策系统，约束欲望，控制回撤，承认无知。

交易不是证明自己有多聪明，而是一场与概率、时间和人性长期博弈的生存游戏。

我们无法保证永远正确，但可以通过纪律，让自己即便看错，也不会被市场淘汰。

对于经历过巨额回撤的人，还有一道更困难的心理关卡：

接受过去的巅峰已经过去，允许自己从一个普通交易者重新开始。

不要把历史最高净值，当作市场欠你的债。

不要因为曾经拥有过一千万，就认为自己必须尽快赚回一千万。

市场不知道你的成本，不记得你的辉煌，更不会为了让你回本而改变规律。

过去的巅峰，只是某一时刻的资产定价，不是未来必须兑现的承诺。

如果始终活在过去的财富幻觉中，就容易用未来的生存机会，填补过去的心理落差。

重新站起来的第一步，不是急着把钱赚回来，而是重建对自己、对风险、对市场的认知。

我始终相信，真正值得骄傲的不是曾经赚过多少钱，而是经历牛熊、成功与失败之后，依然能够不断修正自己，留在这个市场。

真正的财富自由，不是突然拥有很多钱，而是即便运气离开，依然具备创造、管理和守住财富的能力。

最后，送给路遥哥，也送给所有正在经历低谷的朋友：

运气决定你能不能接住时代的水。

认知决定你的盆子有多大。

纪律决定这个盆子有没有漏洞。

不要把系统的一次随机奖励，误认为自己拥有永久的提款权。

也不要因为系统暂时收回了奖励，就否定自己重新开始的能力。

我们改变不了过去的财富曲线，但可以改变未来的决策方式。

失去财富不一定意味着失败，失去重新创造财富的能力才是。

市场可以清算你的仓位，但不要让它清算你的人生。

text:
⚠️ Update on the FAA situation.

Nearly 7,000 flights are delayed or cancelled, in the 1st nationwide halt since 2023.

Here is everything we know:

1. It started in Chicago, where O'Hare was ground stopped at 3:10 PM Eastern over an "equipment outage".

2. The nationwide order came 43 minutes later.

3. The FAA calls it a temporary telecommunications outage affecting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.

4. Parts of US airspace went to "ATC Zero", meaning no air traffic control services can be provided at all.

5. A controller near Chicago told pilots, "We lost all of the frequencies and all of the automation."

6. "Out of an abundance of caution, we have grounded all the flights," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said.

7. On people comparing it to 9/11, Mullin said, "that's not the case."

8. He would not confirm the cause himself, saying, "I'm not going to get ahead of FAA."

9. Asked whether new AI technology in air traffic control towers could be involved, he would not rule it out.

10. Mullin says there is "no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack".

11. He also says there is no reason to think Thursday's global Microsoft outage was linked.

12. Bloomberg reports the FBI is examining whether a software update caused it, and that investigators do not believe it was a cyberattack.

13. The National Weather Service is separately reporting nationwide internet and communication failures, with no confirmed connection to the FAA.

Mullin says it "isn't just going to be resolved and turned around within the hour".

The only other nationwide halts came in January 2023 and after the September 11 attacks.

text:
The corporate card industry needs to rethink how it serves businesses in emerging markets.

Businesses are ready to scale, transaction volumes are growing, and demand for global payment infrastructure is increasing.

Yet, access to reliable corporate card solutions remains unnecessarily difficult for businesses in countries like Bangladesh.

The irony?

A business can process $150K+ in monthly card transactions, primarily for Meta Ads, and still struggle to find a suitable corporate card provider.

We don’t need complicated banking packages.

We need:
• Reliable corporate cards
• Centralized funding (USDT/USDC)
• Flexible spending controls
• Transparent, competitive fees
• Infrastructure that scales with business needs

Emerging markets shouldn’t be an afterthought in global fintech.

Fintech founders and card issuers: Is geographic expansion really that difficult, or is this market simply being overlooked?

text:
沿着上一篇关于复杂系统与趋势涌现的思考，继续推演，可以得到一个更深刻的哲学猜想：

宇宙可能从来没有一个预先写好剧本的上帝。

人类有一种根深蒂固的认知倾向：面对复杂而有序的结果，总是试图寻找背后具有目的性的操盘者。

金融市场如此，政治历史如此，对宇宙起源的理解亦是如此。

每当市场剧烈波动，总有人归因于庄家操纵。

当然，在流动性不足、筹码高度集中的小盘股和小市值加密货币中，市场操纵确实可能发生。

但对于全球主要股指、外汇、国债及 BTC 等高流动性市场，宏观趋势更多是无数不同利益主体，在竞争、制衡与反馈中形成的合力，而非某个庄家预先写好的剧本。

市场不一定需要庄家才能形成趋势，正如宇宙不一定需要上帝才能形成秩序。

从粒子的相互作用，到星系、生命、意识与文明的诞生，宏观秩序可能只是基本物理规律经过漫长演化后涌现出的结果。

没有中央控制，不代表没有秩序；没有预先设计，不代表没有演化方向。

更有意思的是，人类可能恰恰因为自身拥有意识与目的性，才习惯性地将这种目的性投射到整个世界。

我们总是在结果发生之后，反向寻找一条看似必然的因果链，却忽略了演化过程中无数未曾实现的可能路径。

当然，涌现理论无法证明上帝不存在，也无法回答物理规律本身从何而来。

但它至少揭示了一种可能：

宇宙不一定拥有预设的终点，历史不一定存在幕后的导演，而我们所谓的命运，也许只是无数可能性中最终实现的那条路径。

真正需要警惕的，不是某一种具体的阴谋论，而是人类总想为复杂世界寻找一个终极操盘者的思维惯性。

好了今天到这了，阳痿之后总爱思考宇宙哲学什么的这些。
author: hazenlee
quoted_text:
我这些年对市场的理解，真正的趋势并不是某一个主体意志的延伸，而是复杂系统中不同力量相互博弈、叠加与反馈的结果。

如果借用傅立叶变换的思想，一个复杂系统可以被理解为不同频率、振幅与相位的信号共同作用。

政治有政治的周期，资本有资本的周期，产业有产业的周期。不同参与者拥有不同的利益函数，彼此竞争、制衡，甚至完全对立。

但在特定的时间窗口内，这些原本独立的力量，也可能因为某个共同的外部变量而形成阶段性的同向叠加。

趋势的形成，往往是不同力量在特定时间尺度上产生相干性，并通过正反馈不断放大的过程。

但共振并不意味着合谋，相关性更不等于因果性。

真正重要的不是事后找到几个方向一致的结果，而是在事前识别不同参与者的利益结构、行动周期、相互耦合关系，以及系统发生方向性变化的临界条件。

这也是我不太认同用单一阴谋论解释复杂政治经济事件的原因。

因为复杂系统的最终结果，往往不由任何一个参与者完全决定，而是由所有参与者相互作用后涌现出来的。

低维叙事试图为每个结果寻找一个导演，而复杂系统思维试图理解，为什么没有导演的世界，依然能够形成趋势。

Incoming Texas GOP congressman Jace Yarbrough is calling for a full halt to immigration, telling Fox News Digital he backs "stopping immigration altogether for a time because of how insane this has gotten."

Yarbrough, who flipped a formerly Democratic seat in Texas' 32nd District with just over 51% of the vote, says he wants to preserve America's "Christian heritage" and argues certain cultures are "completely incompatible" with American values. He also supports repealing the 1965 Hart-Celler Act, which abolished the national-origins quota system that favored immigrants from Northern and Western Europe while severely restricting immigration from Asia, and replacing the current family-based green card system with merit-based immigration.

As he prepares to enter Congress on Jan. 3, Yarbrough says he doubts the incoming Democratic majorities in both chambers will work with him.

I want to share what we know so far. This was not a cyberattack or an issue caused by AI tooling. Our amazing team was able to work through a very challenging situation to restore service. 

Our investigation points to technical challenges and failure modes (cascading failures + thundering herds at our network perimeter) that made recovery more difficult than normal. I'm working closely with the engineering team to complete the full post-mortem. We will publish the post-mortem shortly covering the step-by-step timeline and our many repair items to avoid similar outages in the future. 

We take our responsibility to our customers seriously and will do everything we can to learn from this and prevent it going forward.

We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.

This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.

Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration.

We will provide a full post-incident report once our review is complete.

text:
这套叙事最大的问题，是把美国政府、华尔街和硅谷科技公司视为一个利益高度一致、能够统一行动的整体，忽略了美国政治与产业内部复杂的博弈关系。

首先，两党虽然在对华科技竞争上存在共同利益，但对于 AI 监管、市场集中度和政府干预的政策路径并不一致。甚至拜登政府2025年的 AI 扩散管制框架，也明确为开放权重模型设置了豁免，而特朗普政府的 AI 行动计划更是直接鼓励开源与开放权重。

其次，闭源模型企业的利益，并不等于整个美国科技产业的利益。

OpenAI、Anthropic 希望保持模型商业优势，但 Microsoft、Amazon 更关心云计算收入，NVIDIA 关心的是整个 AI 计算市场的规模。事实上，Azure 和 AWS 都曾主动部署 DeepSeek-R1。

如果美国全面封锁中国开放模型，受损的未必只有中国企业，也可能包括美国自身的云平台、开发者与应用生态。

更何况，2026年美国政府与 Anthropic 自身就曾因军事 AI 使用限制发生严重冲突，足以说明政府和本土 AI 企业并非永远站在同一阵线。

国家安全限制当然可能发生，联邦机构对 DeepSeek 的采购禁令也已经证明了这一点。但限制政府采购、限制商业云部署、禁止模型权重传播，是完全不同的政策层级。

至于黄仁勋必须下台、封杀开源才能推动两家 AI 公司成功上市，更是缺少必要的因果证据。

问题不在于美国有没有动机限制中国 AI，而在于这种限制是否符合所有美国利益集团的激励，以及为了实现限制需要付出多大的经济和政治成本。

真正理解政治经济学，就不应该把复杂的多方博弈，简化成一个所有资本都步调一致的阴谋剧本。

美国不是一个利益完全一致的交易账户，而是由大量利益冲突的参与者构成的博弈系统。国家战略可能存在共识，但实现战略的路径与利益分配，从来不是共识。

更何况，在黄仁勋辞职之后，再用一套单一的阴谋论叙事去反向解释整件事情的因果关系，难免有些事后归因的意味。

真正有价值的分析，应该是在事前识别不同利益主体的博弈关系与多种可能路径，而不是在结果发生之后，选择性地拼接证据，把复杂的多方博弈包装成一个早已写好的剧本。

能够解释过去的故事很多，能够预测未来的模型才真正稀缺。

text:
Last couple years I've been asked what I think about decoder-only vs encoder-decoder for multimodality, and never really given an answer.

Ellis and Chris take a good step towards answering that question in this study.

Two big points:

(1) Recent encoder-free models like Gemma4-12B, Inkling1, TUNA-2, etc are all a single "point estimates": they show this is possible but tell us absolutely nothing about how it scales, or doesn't! -> this paper does.

(2) Encoder-free or not is actually a false dichotomy. It hides three questions which Chris and Ellis nicely disentangle, and answer separately:
(a) separate pre-training,
(b) separate vision params, and
(c) vision params before or inside decoder?

Answer in pic below, and full thread and paper.

I don't believe there is a CEO out there that can do the dealmaking, navigate the supply chain relationships, manage all of the downstream customers, the hyperscalers, the neoclouds, application companies, open source, and then also do all the engineering and product leadership that Jensen was so good at. Completely irreplaceable.

John: I firmly disagree with this. I think if you find the Tim Cook of NVIDIA to Jensen's Steve Jobs, you can see serious appreciation in the value of the business.

Jordi: If Steve Jobs was running Apple and you still had Tim Cook doing his thing, you might be looking at a $10T company right now. I think the same thing for NVIDIA. Sure, the stock price can appreciate, but 5-10 years from now, there will be a Jensen discount.

text: Step #20 is the most important
author: nickvasilescu
quoted_text:
Making the most AI pilled company is the whole game:

1. make a second brain. one folder of markdown files on how you think, write and decide (obsidian)

2. talk to it. voice notes all day (wispr), and an agent files every fact, story and decision

3. make a company brain. customers, calls, numbers, pricing, playbooks, past decisions and why you made them

4. record every call and meeting (granola). the transcripts go straight into the brain

5. keep a facts file. true things about you and the company that agents are allowed to say. this kills made-up claims

6. keep a voice file. your 50 best posts, 20 you hate, and the words you never use

7. put all of it in git (github) so every change has a history

8. write one instruction file at the top (CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md). read these files before any task, never overwrite, always date

9. give agents memory across sessions so they stop starting from zero (claude-mem, mem0)

10. pipe every data source into one warehouse your agents can query (airbyte → clickhouse). ads, analytics, CRM, payments

11. feed it data nobody else has. it's the only part a competitor can't download

the skills

12. don't start from zero. install the good ones first (anthropics/skills, obra/superpowers, mattpocock/skills, addyosmani/agent-skills)

13. grab the marketing ones too (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, cody schneider's graphed skills for static ads and UGC, boringmarketing dot com skills)

14. map every workflow in the company and rank them by money made or saved

15. do each one once while talking out loud, and record it

16. have an agent turn the recording into a skill. when to use it, the steps, the checks, the mistakes to avoid

17. one skill per job. small and boring beats one giant prompt

18. connect your tools with MCPs so agents can act and not only advise (gmail, slack, stripe, linear, notion, posthog, supabase)

19. give agents a browser (browser-use, vercel agent-browser, claude in chrome)

20. give agents a computer of their own for the tools with no API (vercel agent-desktop, orgo)

21. give your best skills away in public. it's the new lead magnet

the agents

22. run an orchestrator that never turns off (grok bot, openclaw, hermes). it manages one agent per project, and each of those runs its own sub-agents

23. use coding agents for the building (claude code, codex, cursor, t3, antigravity)

24. wrap them in a harness so they plan, test and remember (ECC, superpowers)

25. manage the whole fleet in one place (paperclip). every agent gets a job, a budget and a log

26. put the skills on triggers (n8n, scheduled tasks). daily, weekly, on every new lead, on every cancellation

27. route your models (openrouter). the expensive one plans and checks (fable 5.2, gemini 4 carbon), the cheap ones do the volume

28. cut the token bill. shorter outputs, smaller tool results (caveman)

29. run a local model for the data that can't leave your machine (gemma 4)

30. track cost per job. if a job costs more than it earns, fix it or kill it

the factory

31. build the line. spec agent → builder agents in parallel (git worktrees) → test agent → reviewer agent → deploy (vercel, railway)

32. design goes through the same line (paper MCP), and a skill strips out anything that looks AI made (unslop)

33. every annoying task in the company becomes an internal tool by the end of the day

34. every customer request becomes a pull request before a human reads it (tstack for the PR workflow)

35. reviewer agents with a named bar. "would the best team in the world ship this?" reject until the answer is yes

36. keep 50 real cases with the right answer. rerun them every time a new model drops and switch to the winner

37. humans approve, own the outcome and talk to customers. that's the 10% you keep

the loop

38. every finished job writes back to the brain. what worked, what failed, what to stop doing

39. support tickets, analytics and social comments flow in every night

40. every friday an agent rewrites the playbooks from the week's results, and you approve the diff

41. every month, rank everything by profit per human hour. kill one thing and double one thing

the growth

42. research with agents before you spend a dollar (perplexity API, last30days skill)

43. outbound runs itself. find the leads, enrich, verify, send (apollo, million verifier, instantly, phantombuster)

44. send prospects finished work in place of a pitch

45. ads run on a loop. an agent writes the creative, publishes through the facebook ads API, kills the losers and scales the winners

46. agents make the creative too. images (nano banana), video (heygen, fal), voice (elevenlabs), music (lyria 3.5, suno)

47. turn every finished job into content. the story, the number, the prompt

48. every customer makes the brain smarter for the next one. that's your network effect

49. once it works, point it at a new niche. same agents, new context

The models are the same for everyone but your context is the only part that's yours.

Acquire as much of it as you can, as fast as you can.

Build loops like this.

This is the whole game, happy playing.

Coinbase Institutional: Fed Rate Expectations, Not Binance Hack, Drive Bitcoin’s Recent Decline

Coinbase Institutional said in its weekly report that Bitcoin’s recent decline was driven primarily by shifting Fed policy expectations rather than the Binance hack. October nonfarm payrolls and CPI both exceeded expectations, with markets fully pricing in a 25 bps rate hike in December and 64 bps of hikes over the next 12 months. Bitcoin fell below key support at $73,000, while stablecoin supply contracted by a record $11.5 billion over the past 30 days. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $1.44 billion in net outflows over the five trading days leading up to Nov. 11, with ETF holders sitting on approximately $12.7 billion in aggregate unrealized losses. Coinbase Institutional warned that a sustained move below $73,000 would significantly increase the likelihood of a decline toward the $66,000–$68,000 support zone.

text:
美联储流动性正在改善，BTC却跌破7万大关，钱到底什么时候回来？

最近的市场有点吓人，黄金、白银、比特币、科技股一起跌。连避险资产都扛不住，说明市场正在优先争夺美元现金。美债收益率持续处于高位，资金宁愿拿着美元赚利息，也不愿承担风险。

美联储最新数据显示，美国银行准备金一周增加约305亿美元，财政部TGA账户余额下降约428亿美元。

也就是说，美元基础流动性已经出现边际改善，BTC却继续跌到6.8万美元附近。

加密市场自己还在失血。稳定币供应30天缩水约142亿美元，BTC现货ETF最近五个完整交易日净流出约12.92亿美元。

外部资金不愿进来，内部资金持续撤退，再叠加杠杆清算，市场自然缺乏持续买盘。

流动性回归信号：

1. 宏观转松：美元指数DXY持续回落至102附近，10年期美债收益率跌破5%，实际利率同步下降，资金重新愿意承担风险。

2. 资金回流：BTC ETF连续3个交易日净流入，累计超过3亿美元；稳定币供应结束收缩并持续增长。这才是加密市场真正出现增量资金的信号。

3. 价格确认：BTC重新站上7.31万美元附近的200日均线，现货买盘同步增强。否则即使暴力反弹，也可能只是空头回补。

未来几天BTC随时可能出现超跌反弹，但持续反转还缺资金确认。

未来2—6周重点观察美元、美债收益率和ETF资金流，至于新一轮牛市，现在下结论还太早。

流动性回归有三个阶段：美元先松动，风险偏好再恢复，最后资金才真正流入BTC。

现在第一步有了些迹象，后面两步还没跟上。

入奢，吃喝拉撒其实还好，百万豪车千万游艇，再捞的女人也都还好...

但是这个最可怕的是，你的手，小不下来了...

Aimeme的时候，我土狗账户里面还有5-6M的土狗，当时觉得无所谓，疯狂买，还有一些垃圾，一上线我就买几十万美金，然后赚几万刀没感觉，这就是典型的思路不清晰，脑子有问题。
回看当时，确实挺傻逼的，压根没想到降息缩表的时刻，大家都会原形毕露，当然，最后这些土狗全部归零了...

包括后面买垃圾，比如linea这种，稍微觉得有点意思，一买就是2M起步，到现在账户还在，大概跌了90%多...
白天反思的时候看还剩十几万U....
买four也是，一次想买20M，当时的膨胀以及入俭难，导致我10.10惨死
这也是我第一次被打到服...

打美股也是，随便查一下推特，看都在买诺基亚Nok，黑莓之类的，随便就每个买1M放着...
最后学习完，这些也都跌的差不多了，全部在高点换成了SNDK...
到现在美股这个劲儿大的我还没缓过来，甚至我感觉糟透了...

甚至到前一阵子，买stonk，也是拿一堆账户去买，习惯养成后，买什么都是1个点，或者几个点的时候，这就是大道要来收走原本不属于你的东西。
对的，没错，我被收走了...
而后给了我贫穷和苦难...
我不知道我这次能不能再打起来，但是，我自己都知道，挺难的...
希望可以吧！
而且我现在的心气，完全没有前两年高了。

二 就是 看不上小钱

人一旦赚过快钱了之后，再赚慢钱，就会很难受，这是人类都会有的东西...

我最早被打崩的时候，还想着去学校门口卖小乌龟，一个月1w块钱，我想着怎么我都能活下来，把老婆孩子养了...

但是后面被打崩的时候，宁可躺着，也不愿意再去干事儿了...
这点我到现在都没调整过来...
甚至给自己找了很多借口

三 不去找根本的问题
我直到这次，可能才知道，我靠运气赚的，是美联储放水的钱...
我之前研究了，天时，地利，人和，研究各种瞎几把玩意甚至到八字，运势，个人努力，赛道选择...
最后才发现，只有美国政府放水，所有的赛道才有钱，只有降息，钱才出来，诶卧槽...
天时也得放在美国政府之后....

可能还有别的原因，我现在都不知道...我只看到这...
 而之前很懵逼，都在各种小道里面去找原因，看不到大的，这次美股的大亏，也让我这个土狗，知道原来，天外有天....

从现在，到1月底，几乎都是利空的东西，没啥利好，2月可能市场才会回暖...

我现在被打的，割吧，觉得可惜，不割吧，觉得诶卧槽...

时间没到...

鸡肋，可能过几天自己想明白就知道怎么做了

danshi ,前面那两点，确实是我遇到的问题，甚至也一直没有解决的问题..
我身边的朋友，也是这个问题

我看乔帮主已经开始九紫离火了... 真tm的，咱俩好好学习行不，别封建迷信了，九紫离火咋就专门清算你不清算熬鹰呢?

At the same time, it's really important to stay above $4M because, below that level, we have no support at all, so panic selling could become a real problem.

Considering that we're still below the trendline, everything that's happening right now is a series of bounces within a downtrend. But again, given how bad the entire market looks right now, these bounces represent a lot of strength.

Another important bullish aspect of this coin is its community, which has remained active whether Buttcoin was trading above $20M or below $5M. There are so many believers in this project and you know I never fade active communities.

text:
The hardest part of building a power plant is now plugging it in.

Every new plant needs the grid operator’s approval before it can connect. By the early 2020s the projects waiting for that approval added up to more capacity than the entire U.S. grid.

AI data centers sit idle until those new plants come online. Their owners would gladly pay to move faster, but grid operators do not sell places in line. Amazon got around that by paying $83 million for a permitted Oregon solar project already in line.

Sites that already have a connection are gaining value too. The Three Mile Island restart for Microsoft will borrow a gas plant’s connection so it can start sooner. A fusion developer plans to build on a retired coal site and reuse the connection the coal plant left behind.

Owners of old plants and stalled projects could find that their grid connection is now their most valuable asset.
