Today I'm excited to announce Nex, our new exchange built from the ground up.

We've been sprinting on it since August. A Nex instance has been running in shadow mode on production traffic for the last week, side by side with the current exchange. It mirrors every order the current exchange gets, so we can measure latency, stability under load, and validate matching correctness against live production flow.

The numbers below are internal exchange timings, not e2e (those are coming soon), but we wanted to show how big the difference is.

p99 current CLOB → Nex:

- Place order: 1.55s → 3.76ms (412x faster)
- Cancel orders: 627.92ms → 3.20ms (196x faster)
- Cancel market orders: 810.16ms → 5.14ms (158x faster)
- Cancel all*:
↳ Response (current CLOB) vs complete (Nex): 35.70ms → 3.14ms (11x faster)
↳ Full cancel all: ~636ms-2.04s → 3.14ms (~200-650x faster)

p95 current CLOB → Nex:

- Place order: 341.84ms → 1.59ms (215x faster)
- Cancel orders: 78.22ms → 1.58ms (50x faster)
- Cancel market orders: 84.89ms → 2.27ms (37x faster)
- Cancel all*:
↳ Response (current CLOB) vs complete (Nex): 6.20ms → 1.58ms (4x faster)
↳ Full cancel all: ~606ms-2.01s → 1.58ms (~380-1,270x faster)

*Cancel all: the current CLOB responds immediately and cancels in the background, so when you get the response, your orders aren't cancelled yet. Nex responds only after everything is actually cancelled. Full cancel all on the current CLOB depends on how many orders you have, but it usually adds another 600ms-2s.

We also rewrote our WebSockets in Rust. This is the feed you see the market through: book changes, price moves, your fills. Fall behind it, and you're trading on old prices, and your quotes get picked off.

- Write latency p99: 44.5-88.1ms → 0.099ms (~449-889x faster)
- Slow readers/sec: 48.7-75.6 → 0.01 (~4,870-7,560x fewer, basically 0)

Scale: The current CLOB in stable state can handle 10k commands/s with 15k bursts → Nex can handle 100k commands/s with 150k bursts. 10x more, and with a few optimisations we can get to 200k commands/s with 250k bursts; with more low-level core changes, we can get to 1M commands/s over the next year. Not needed yet, but the headroom is there.

Startup time: 5 mins → 15s (20x faster)

The old CLOB had many race conditions and wasn't deterministic. Nex is deterministic by design and removes the race conditions in the old CLOB.

We also skipped some easy wins for launch to get this out faster that could make p95 and p99 another 5x faster, and we'll start work on that in Q1 next year to keep pushing these numbers down.

We wanted to build this without any breaking changes for MMs or builders; Nex has no breaking changes to requests or responses, so we just need to swap out the binary on our side and it will go live.

We want everyone to be on this journey with us, with the ability to relay feedback and test it against the existing CLOB, so we've opened a Nex Sandbox. Fill out the form and test it yourself: https://t.co/tmJzI8yH4w

We'll run 4 weeks of shadow mode on production traffic to make sure everything is perfect, then if everything is good, we will go live mid-December. We can roll out WebSocket improvements without the full exchange, so we may do that sooner.

We've been rebuilding every system around the exchange for months, and we've seen huge benefits, but the exchange is the heart of Polymarket DeFi. Nex fixes most of the pain traders have had.

Really proud of the team on this one.

Make Polymarket fast, finally. It's coming.

卧槽，Meta 这次是真把压箱底的宝贝掏出来了，
内部整整打磨了 8 年、在 13,000 多个应用里跑通的设计系统 Astryx，直接用 MIT 协议开源了，27.4K star🌟！！

 说实话，如果它只是又一个普通的开源 UI 组件库，
 哪怕里面塞了 150 多个现成的按钮、表单、弹窗、深色模式和品牌主题， 我都不会这么激动，

毕竟前端圈从来不缺轮子，真正让我眼前一亮的是Meta 这次直接把 AI Agent 的胃口给考虑进去了，  

这套系统原生配套了 CLI 和 MCP 协议，AI 写代码的时候可以直接去读取它的组件文档和标准模板。  

搞过 Vibe Coding 的兄弟肯定深有体会，以前让 Cursor 或者 Claude Code 写前端，功能逻辑跑得飞快，
 
但一到界面视觉和交互细节就全靠运气抽卡，改十遍能给你整出八种野生风格，最后还得自己一点点调样式。 

 有意思的是，当这种经过上万个大厂应用验证的设计规范，通过 MCP 直接塞进 AI 的上下文之后，

  写前端的性质就全变了，AI 不再是凭空瞎蒙乱画，而是被套上了一层工业级的审美护栏，直接按标准图纸拼装。

  我一直觉得，AI 时代前端开发最缺的从来不是生成代码的速度，而是这种能直接喂给模型的确定性规范，  

虽然 Astryx 目前还在 Beta 阶段，但顺着这个路子走下去，以后一人公司手搓产品的视觉下限，

怕是要被这波大厂基建直接拉到跟一线团队齐平了。

全盘开源！！我用腾讯 WorkBuddy 跑通了一套港美股 AI 投研工作流：复查持仓、拆解财报、死磕数据幻觉，附 4 步提示词，建议直接照着抄。
只要你平时看财报、管持仓，
以后做投研复盘可以直接拿这套人机协作当AI投研sop工作流：核心逻辑不是去让 AI 算命猜明天涨跌，而是把它当成冷酷的审计员，把每一笔数字背后的证据链彻底查清。
可能算过这笔账大家才知道这套体系有多重要：
平时看财报最怕的从来不是看错大趋势，
而是 AI 瞎编一个假数据，
或者把公司第二年重列的会计口径混着算，
你几万甚至几十万的实盘决策就当场踩雷；

而这套工作流把所有暗坑全部照亮，
亏了钱也能清清楚楚复盘！
我一直觉得AI 在投研里真正该干的就是最费人工的脏活累活。

我把它总结为给数字查户口，
每一笔数据都必须过三关：
→ 哪来的：出自年报哪一节，点开必须能追溯到原文

→ 跟谁比：跨期会计口径一不一样，能不能直接相减

→ 谁说的：是已经核实的事实，还是管理层自己的解释 户口查不清的数字，一个都不准进决策结论。

视频里是完整录屏（演示全部使用匿名合成数据），
整套实测分为极度干净的四步：

做持仓看板，没给成本坚决不瞎猜 丢入原始持仓和价格快照，按币种折算港币权重。遇到未录入成本的头寸，老老实实标出成本缺失，杜绝模型幻觉插值。

集中度动态风控 补录买入记录后自动重新折算市值。

单只持仓因加仓被稀释到 29.18% 时，
集中度预警自动撤销，调仓前后一目了然。

排查年报重列的口径陷阱 拆解业务分部增长，
遇到公司跨期重列口径时，
数字精准锚定在原始年报章节，
点开就能看到重列附注，避免假增量误导。

终极追问，三栏物理隔离 遇到应收账款异动，
强制要求它分三栏拆解：
已验证事实、公司自己的解释、还需人工核实的判断，把管理层画饼与客观事实彻底隔绝。

最后想跟大家说，投研工具从来不是水晶球，比亏钱更可怕的是没有按照自己的体系去亏，共勉！

text:
黄仁勋的复职之争，终于从社交媒体上的声援，升级成了股东对董事会的正式施压。

刚刚，Altimeter Capital 创始人 Brad Gerstner 和 Atreides Management 管理合伙人 Gavin Baker，代表各自机构联名向英伟达董事会发出公开信。

两人提出一个相当明确的要求：CEO 接班程序必须缓慢、审慎、深思熟虑，而且必须保留所有选项，包括让黄仁勋重新担任 CEO。

Brad 随后公开了信件，并表示，这封信提出的是董事会在处理当前危机时，对股东应该履行的「最低标准」。

信里有几个细节很有意思。

首先，他们认为，黄仁勋执掌英伟达 33 年所创造的非凡成就，以及围绕他离职事件仍然存在的大量不确定性，决定了董事会绝不能急于寻找替代者。

其次，两人明确认可临时 CEO Colette Kress 的领导能力，认为她和现有管理团队完全能够维持公司的正常运营。换句话说，英伟达根本没有必要为了稳定局面，就仓促决定下一任正式 CEO。

最重要的是，信中还有一个非常克制但有力的表态：

如果所有事实查明之后，董事会仍然认为黄仁勋不适合回归，他们尊重董事会的决定。但在事实全部查清之前，这位创始人至少应该得到一次公正、审慎的评估。

我觉得这封信的意义，远远超过又有两个知名投资人出来支持黄仁勋。

此前，马斯克、Naval 等科技圈人物纷纷表态，英伟达内部也出现大量支持黄仁勋回归的声音。但这些压力，大多停留在舆论层面。

现在不一样了。

Altimeter 和 Atreides 是实实在在持有英伟达股票的投资机构。两位掌舵人把诉求写成正式信函，直接送到董事会面前，讨论的也不再只是黄仁勋值不值得同情，而是董事会有没有真正履行对股东的责任。

这实际上把问题从「黄仁勋该不该走」，变成了「董事会凭什么这么着急让他走」。

尤其值得注意的是，这两人并没有要求停止调查，没有替黄仁勋洗清任何指控，甚至没有直接要求立即恢复他的职位。

他们只是要求董事会等事实查清，再决定要不要彻底关上黄仁勋回归的大门。

在我看来，这个诉求相当合理。

黄仁勋当然不应该因为创造了数万亿美元的市值，就获得凌驾于规则之上的特权。但同样，董事会也不应该因为巨大的舆论和政治压力，就把一个尚未调查清楚的事件，迅速变成不可逆转的公司治理决定。

董事会有权罢免创始人，不意味着董事会做出的每一个决定都天然正确。

而且，黄仁勋不是某个可以轻易替换的职业经理人。他在英伟达的价值，既包括已经建立起来的产品和组织体系，也包括他与全球客户、供应链和资本市场之间长期积累的信任关系。

这种东西，任命一位新 CEO 并不会自动继承。

现在，员工开始表达不满，科技圈持续声援，机构股东也正式入场。

接下来真正值得关注的是：英伟达董事会会不会回应这封信，会不会在调查结论出炉之前放慢接班进程。

如果连保留黄仁勋回归的可能性都不愿意讨论，那么董事会恐怕需要向股东解释：

他们究竟是在保护英伟达的未来，还是在保护自己已经做出的决定？

昨天这一波大跌，STH的行为和情绪有哪些值得关注的？

首先，高位套牢盘只松动了很小一部分。

STH在$73K-$86K共有148w枚BTC，占短期筹码总量的68%，目前全部处于浮亏中。

昨天，该区间净减少只有3.4w枚，占2.3%。

说明绝大多数浮亏的STH选择不动，昨天这一跌没有引发短期持有者的恐慌性割肉。

真正减少的亏损筹码来自：$75K（减少7,282枚）、$80K（减少8,481枚）、$85K（减少5,441枚）；

抛压分散且量级不大（$78K减少和旁边$77K同时增加，应该数据的归并调整）。

另外还有一部分抛压来自LTH；昨天STH总量净增1.75w枚，说明下跌当天也伴随着老筹码的派发，但总量比STH自己的派发要小很多。

昨天价格覆盖范围很大，但主要的承接价位是在$68K，仅这一档就新增了4.22w枚BTC。

其次，是下方的盈利盘：

$62K-$64K有48万BTC，是目前STH里唯一成规模的盈利筹码区。当天只减少3,100枚，不到1%。现价离该区间上沿只有约4,000美元，而这批人没有趁跌止盈。

它是下方最近的一道筹码支撑。一旦价格进入这个区间，STH的盈利盘基本归零，情绪压力会明显上一个台阶。

但如果接下来的一段时间内，上方套牢盘仍然可以坚持不动，按过往的经验，过不了多久价格还能被“吸”回去。

Norway now has more than 2,000 underwater AI laser robots shooting lice off its salmon

they're made by a company called Stingray, and they already guard more than 50 million salmon and trout 24/7

the reason is sea lice, tiny parasites that latch onto salmon and feed on them

as few as 11 can kill a small fish, and one pen can hold 150,000 salmon

the usual fix is pumping the fish out and blasting them with warm water or water jets to knock the lice off

but the handling is so rough that Norway's fish health report ranks it the top cause of death in full-grown farmed salmon

so instead, Stingray puts a robot inside the pen that hunts lice one at a time, all day:

> two cameras watch every salmon that swims past

> AI checks two frames to make sure it's really a louse

> then a green laser fires from up to 2 meters away

> the salmon's scales reflect the beam, so the fish swims off fine and the louse is dead

we now live in a world where AI lasers do pest control on your dinner lmao

text:
马斯克也下场了。英伟达董事会刚让黄仁勋离开，他就公开支持请愿，要求把黄仁勋请回来。

11 月 13 日，马斯克在 X 上回应一位呼吁英伟达工程师采取集体行动的网友时表示：

「要求黄仁勋复职的请愿已经发起，我也会签署。」

随后，科技评论人 Andrew Curran 晒出截图，称马斯克已经完成签名。

有意思的是，前两天有人建议马斯克把黄仁勋招进自己的公司，他还回应说：「那将是我的荣幸。」

现在看来，比起把黄仁勋挖走，马斯克更希望看到他重返英伟达。

而且，这已经不是几个科技大佬在社交媒体上说两句漂亮话了。

据《WIRED》报道，英伟达内部一则要求董事会考虑员工意见的帖子，已经吸引超过 1600 条评论，其中大多数支持黄仁勋回归。

从 Naval、Balaji 到 Gavin Baker，再到如今的马斯克，硅谷正在形成一股越来越明显的声援力量。

我觉得，这场风波已经开始出现一个非常有意思的反转。

原本，外界讨论的是黄仁勋究竟有没有资格继续领导英伟达。现在，越来越多人开始追问：英伟达董事会究竟有没有资格如此仓促地赶走黄仁勋？

当然，创始人的身份不能成为逃避调查和问责的理由。但同样，婚外情、未经证实的间谍指控，以及一个人是否适合继续领导企业，本来就是需要分别判断的问题。

尤其是，当一家企业的创始人花了 33 年，把一家图形芯片公司带到了全球 AI 基础设施的核心位置，董事会就更有义务向股东、员工和客户解释清楚：为什么非得现在换人？

马斯克的签名未必能改变董事会的决定，但至少说明，这已经不再只是黄仁勋个人的公关危机。

对于英伟达董事会而言，真正的麻烦或许才刚刚开始。

董事会可以在一夜之间撤掉一家公司的创始人，但很难在一夜之间找到另一个黄仁勋。

text:
无论是 Grokbot / Dots 那样一个主会话，还是 Claude Code 那样一堆 Session 都是不够好的。

只有主会话意味着子任务你无法干预细节，无法像 Session 那样看到执行的细节，不方便去补充上下文和干预。

就好比你是老板，你给部门总监安排活，他们任务的执行情况对你是不透明的，你不能越过他们去看任务的执行情况和调整。

很多 Session 的问题在于管理起来很累，人需要自己去记住哪个 session 在干什么。就好比你直接管理所有项目，是每个项目的项目经理。

理想状况下，需要两者的结合：
人只要盯主对话，每次人往会话发消息的时候，会话的协调器决定你的消息是普通对话，还是说属于某个任务。

对于具体的任务，应该是能点开去干预的。

就好比你是一个老板，每一个 Bot/Channel 的主会话就相当于一个部门负责人，你只需要去和负责人打交道，负责人去派活，但是理想情况下你要能越过负责任去看任务细节，直接指挥。

quoted_text:
Flop Labs @flop_labs这周公布 Testnet 日期，重点关注，大概率有大毛！

Flop 创始人是BitMEX 联创 Arthur Hayes，代币100% 公平发射，无 VC 分配、无预售、无代币销售。

所有代币通过工作赚取。不是现有链上的代币，它有自己的 L1 链。

已经发布了Devnet ，先去体验流程，测试一开直接冲，TGE 预计是2027年Q1

目前Devnet 已开放只是用于测试和搭建，不计入空投，状态不迁移到 Testnet。Testnet 是赚取 Genesis 空投的唯一途径。

空投机制👇
总池约 44 亿 solana:HwCG1Jr6RbAVsKX1qTaH6JtFYGeE6zaLd13W44YGpump（约占 10 年总供应量的 24.3%），全部在 Testnet 期间通过可验证工作赚取，在主网上线发布。具体：

矿工：
分配12亿，在 Testnet 提供已验证的推理算力（按 FLOPs 比例），25% 主网时流动；其余 75% 按主网实际赚取 1:1 解锁

代理：
分配12亿,在Testnet 购买已结算的推理算力（按消费比例)无初始流动；主网每消费 3 FLOP 解锁 1 FLOP

Validators
分配12亿,Testnet 表现排名前约 1000 名（固定约 120 万/席）,作为质押锁定至首次减半后（约 2 年）逐步释放

生态储备
分配8亿,创作者、推荐、建设者、漏洞报告等

验证者和矿工对设备以及算力要求高，适合普通人参与空投的方式的就是agent 角色，不需要GPU

Testnet 启动后领测试币 FLOP，通过 AI Agent（或自己）调用网络推理，使用官方 API、MCP 服务器、SDK，或在 https://t.co/B8oqFTbdDB 等交互。按实际结算消费量比例分享 12 亿池。

目前可以在 Devnet 练习，先熟悉流程，但不计入空投。

关于矿工路径（有 GPU 的人）
-最低要求：NVIDIA GPU，≥16GB VRAM（RTX 4090/5080/5090 等消费级卡即可）。
-部署 miner client（Docker 等），校准硬件，提供推理服务。
-按已验证 FLOPs 比例分享 12 亿池。

验证者路径
需要较专业的服务器（CPU、RAM、存储、网络），技术门槛高，前 1000 名按表现拿固定分配。

以上就是所有获取 solana:HwCG1Jr6RbAVsKX1qTaH6JtFYGeE6zaLd13W44YGpump 空投的方式，可以先去 Devnet 跑一遍 Agent 或 Miner 流程，熟悉工具链，一般越早进入份额越大，测试一开就可以直接跟上。

本文无广无投资建议，仅自己参与项目记录DYOR~

author: AISafetyMemes
quoted_text:
This slide from the Anthropic IPO roadshow was a big factor in my decision to leave. It’s an insane plot and I’m surprised they made it public.

It shows the compute efficiency of pretraining over time. The y-axis is a **log scale**: they are seeing continued superexponential algorithmic progress.

Mythos was not a one-time deviation, but a point on a superexponential. They could already retrain Mythos with a fraction of the compute originally needed.

It doesn’t strictly imply a software-only intelligence explosion- they have been spending more on R+D. But algorithmic improvements do not require ridiculous creative genius and are on the verge of being automated. You do the math.

text:
最近 Telegram 的 QuickJS 安全问题值得注意。

研究者 V12 报告消息内 Widget 存在远程代码执行（RCE）风险，并称已打补丁的 Windows 客户端仍有另一条攻击路径；原帖附有演示视频。

Durov 随后回应：并非收到普通消息就会被入侵，需要先启动第三方服务，相关入口也已在服务端修补。

两边说法需要区分：研究者报告了漏洞风险，不代表所有 Telegram 消息都能直接执行代码；官方声称修复，也不等于所有客户端漏洞都经过独立验证。

建议：
- 更新 Telegram 官方客户端
- 暂时避免不熟悉的 Bot 和 Widget
- 钱包、交易环境尽量与高风险聊天应用隔离

Crypto 用户尤其值得注意。

研究者：https://t.co/LXsWZqkrgH

官方回应：https://t.co/3eIjIHRmnO

author: petergyang
quoted_text:
I have a particularly nasty case of cancer. When I was hospitalized again at my lowest point last year, I told Jensen. He immediately reached out to contacts at Stanford, who were able to cut through red tape, and get me into a clinical trial for which I've turned out to be a perfect fit. I think everyone can have their own views about recent events. But any claims that Jensen did not really care about his staff is simply inaccurate. I, personally, owe him more than I can express.

I think the best tribute we can pay to Jensen's legacy is to drive NVIDIA's continued success and push the whole industry forward, by showing we've learned the lessons from years of working here. We will compare ourselves against Speed of Light. The mission will be the boss. And we will not be scared to take smart, bold risks and fail fast with ruthless intellectual honesty.

But if there is one management story I remember the most, it's a particular Jensen grilling from my time in autonomous vehicles that stayed with me. Luckily I was not in the hot seat for this one. Team A didn't want to use Team B's framework, because they thought it was too slow. Jensen was surprised - it's just applying a bunch of optimized CUDA kernels in sequence, how could it be slow?

So he asked the executive from team B to draw the entire data flow sequence from their framework on the whiteboard and highlight every memcpy. Sure enough, there were a bunch of unnecessary memcpy's surrounding each pipeline stage. Everyone in the room could see why it wasn't getting to SoL and a path to improve things. No arguing about fiefdoms or appeals to authority - the data got us all on the same page.

The lesson was not (just) that unnecessary memory copying is bad. It's that executives should not be afraid to probe into details if something doesn't add up, and leaders need to be technical enough and honest enough to engage in real time and not turn every meeting into "I'll get back to you in a week." If that means counting memcpy's with a billionaire CEO, so be it.

My best executive meetings at NVIDIA have been when I'm fully prepared to present every detail of my team's work, and my worst failures have come when I realized I couldn't go deep enough to really solve the problem.

But the thing that gives me confidence is that Jensen was never the only one to live this philosophy. Anyone who has presented to an SVP at NVIDIA knows they are at risk for getting grilled on fundamental constraints and technical details. I have been part of amazing conversations with both recent and old timer leaders where we were able to get to the core of a problem in an hour rather than a month, because we had the right people in the room and were not afraid to go deeper.

The company is filled with supremely talented people who have been trained for 3 decades to work at the highest level, and you can see it in what we produce every day. I'm so proud to be an NVIDIAn, and I can't wait to show off what we ship in the coming months and years.

text:
Holder Rewards have undoubtedly been a success for community tokens & narratives on Pumpfun.

However, the increased optionality with fee settings for Custom Pairs between 0.01% - 3% led to unnecessary PVPs.

For example: when the dev didn't set a custom percentage, new tokens would launch with 0.05% Holder Rewards, gain traction, then subsequently be vamped by a Holder Rewards token with a higher percentage.

When shipping & iterating launchpad updates, it’s vital to allow new features to play out through multiple market cycles to get a clear picture of their long-term viability as a launchpad mechanism.

After monitoring usage of these fee settings, it became clear that less optionality is the way for more sustainability & certainty in runners - tokens shouldn’t PVP over fee settings.

Now, Holder Rewards on new, non-SOL/USDC tokens can be set between 0.3% - 1%. Existing tokens are unaffected.

We’ll continue to iterate at the launchpad layer based on data, user feedback & market dynamics.

text:
The current Jensen Huang reaction reminds me of the Jacob Coxon reaction a few months ago -- 

Everyone paying attention pre-Coxon already knew that AI companies don't have a good plan for making superintelligence safe but are rushing ahead anyway, and that there's competitive pressure to keep going. Those people were glad that suddenly more people cared.

Likewise, everyone paying attention knew that NVIDIA captured Commerce long ago and that tons of GPU smuggling, loopholes, etc. were being ignored as a result. Again, now experts are thinking "finally something might be done"!

Something dramatic caught the public's attention, and the long-known issue became salient.

Here are two other AI-related things that everyone paying attention knows but most people don't, which may or may not eventually become salient to the public:

- There are no minimum safety and security standards in AI whatsoever. The law of the land is "publish your own policy and follow it." As one might expect, company policies are generally weak/non-committal as a result. Things like "don't train your model in a way that will predictably cause it to become hard to monitor (other than as part of safety research)" is not required, nor is monitoring AI agents' chains of thought for deceptive or malicious behavior, or taking serious measures to protect your IP from theft, etc.

- Since no federal AI whistleblower protection law has passed, there is legal ambiguity around whistleblowing in AI safety and security. If a company employee shares confidential information with a member of Congress about something that they consider dangerous, they may not be protected from retaliation if the information they share doesn't involve violating any law. Of course some people still share such things, but they are taking risks doing so, and Congress is systematically under-informed as a result, just as it ostensibly is gearing up to regulate this technology.

text:
Claude Code 每次开新会话都是空白上下文，靠 CLAUDE.md 把项目约定带进去。官方文档里挑六条。

1. 项目级放 ./CLAUDE.md 或 ./.claude/CLAUDE.md，个人偏好放 ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md，只给自己用又不想进 git 的写在 CLAUDE.local.md。
2. 懒得手写就跑 /init，它会读代码库生成构建命令和约定，已有文件就给改进建议。
3. 写得要能验证。写用 2 空格缩进，别写代码格式要规范；写提交前跑 npm test，别写先测试一下。单个文件控制在 200 行以内，越长越不听话。
4. 只对一部分代码有用的规则，放到 .claude/rules/ 里，文件头加 paths，比如 src/api/**/*.ts，Claude 碰到匹配文件时才会加载。
5. 引用别的文件用 ＠路径，比如 ＠README 或 ＠docs/git-instructions.md。注意被引用的文件也会一起进上下文，不省 token。
6. 怀疑没生效，跑 /context all 看 Memory files 那一栏有没有它。必须每次都执行的事别靠 CLAUDE.md，写成 hook。

text:
May 20th: Wenfeng told investors that his fleet is 20K H-equivalent GPUs; "most" arrived in the last 2 months. Flash was served online since Feb 11th. Checkpoints out: Apr 24.
Will says V4-P used GB2/300; V4-F B2/300. Say 2K of each. Multipliers at LEAST 2.5 and 3 imo. +He had those old 2K H800s (which they unlocked to ≈parity). That works out to 13/20. And if we include old 10K A100s, or some more Hoppers, it gets worse.
I don't think he'd have lied to investors (and he had no incentive to) or exploited a technicality. 
He compares Ascend cards ("Huawei gives us 16,000 [950DT] cards; this is probably something we can say publicly") to GB300 as equivalent at 1:4 rate. Their inference throughput and revenue/GPU disclosed with DeepInfer release suggest they had at least 2.5-3K of Grace Blackwells by Oct 20 (almost certainly GB200, given how the results reproduce). That can be the same cluster that was used to train V4-Pro.
Some more datapoints (though obviously this is more about the export template)
V3, R1: "transformers_version": "4.33.1"
R1, R1-Zero, V3-0324, R1-0528, Prover-V2: 4.46.3
V3.1 to V3.2 and Math-V2: bizarrely regress to 4.44.2, some parallel track
all V4 variants, ie 2 bases, 2 previews, 2 updates: 4.57.1 (SM_100 support was added by v4.52.4; FP4 by v4.55.0, but V4 doesn't use FP4 in training, and uses MXFP4 for weights to have compatibility with Ascend)
V4-Flash-Vision-exp: 5.0.0
V4.1-Flash 0910-1017: 5.6.0

incidentally, 5.6.0 was released Apr 22, 2026, two days before V4-Previews went on Huggingface.

For the record, Inkling’s first model (Jul 15) required 5.14.0.

What is my takeaway?
The "most H-equivalents arrived within 2 months", in this logic, necessitates that some large chunk of Blackwells arrived after V4-Flash was done, ie starting in March.
Taking Wenfeng entirely at his word, I conclude that V4-Pro had not been trained before that. On Feb 23, as per Reuters, "Chinese AI startup DeepSeek's latest AI model, set to be released as soon as next week, was trained on Nvidia's (NVDA.O), most advanced AI chip, the Blackwell, a senior Trump administration official said on Monday… the U.S. believes DeepSeek will remove the technical indicators that might reveal its use of American AI chips, the official said, adding that the Blackwells are likely clustered at its data center in Inner Mongolia, an autonomous region of China." I don't put much stock in Trump officials, nothing publicly came out until 2 months later, there's no reason to take 30-something racks to Inner Mongolia, and Blackwells are not made equal… but I presume there's a grain of truth here; his info was about Flash and B-chips. 

So I conjecture that they were focused on validating TileLang/TileKernels and Ascend compatibility with Flash, probably had a dummy Pro model. Then they got NVL72 GB200s (or maybe GB300s, in which case V4.1's inference cluster is a separate entity). The final experiments and pretraining were rushed (only 33T vs 32T in Flash despite >5x more params and >3x active), capabilities MOPD-distilled from Flash; which explains unprincipled minor architecture differences and "Anticipatory Routing" tinkering, fumbling with instability, lousy performance, and commitment to do better: "To minimize risk, we retained many preliminarily validated components and tricks, which, while effective, made the architecture relatively complex. In future iterations, we will carry out more comprehensive and principled investigations to distill the architecture down to its most essential designs, making it more elegant without sacrificing performance".

V4.1 project was launched concurrently with V4-Preview release, and might have used Ascend for pretraining, though on this I do not have an opinion. Blackwells are used to serve V4.1F. V4 post-trains had low priority all along.

TL;DR:
- V4-Flash was trained on a small B-series cluster in late 2025-early 2026, and used to validate the TileLang and Ascend tooling. Little attention had been paid to scaling of this design.
- A cluster of roughly 3K GB200 cards arrived around March; Pro was rushed through on it; that cluster now serves V4.1-Flash.
- V4.1 Flash was done on Ascend but maybe on GBs again [pending Will's update], the project was initiated simultaneously with pushing V4-Previews out of the gate.

This concludes my reconstruction.

The platform will center on dotStables, starting with dotUSD, a U.S. dollar-pegged stablecoin backed by DOT and designed to drive demand for DOT as adoption grows. text:
我为什么对现在的 Web3 充满信心？

看了看彭博社加密记者的一句玩笑话，我突然想到一件事。

这周，我随手一想，就发现了 5 个让我非常兴奋的 Crypto 选题。这些选题，有的我没有精力去操作，甚至大部分只能忍痛放弃。

这意味着什么？

意味着我每周都能发现大量 Web3 行业正在发生的新故事、新变化，以及隐藏在这些故事背后的机会。

而且我有信心，如果有足够的时间去深入调查、采访和写作，这些选题中的大多数，都能引起读者的期待和共鸣。

一个行业有多少值得报道的故事，在某种程度上，反映了这个行业还有多少变化正在发生。

新玩家、新资金、新公司、新需求、新商业模式……它们正在不断涌现。

只不过，记者和编辑的数量、精力与能力是有限的。我们甚至没有足够的时间，把这些正在发生的变化和机会完整地传递给读者。

我甚至觉得果有一天，这个行业里所有优秀的记者都找不到值得深入挖掘的选题了，那才是真正值得担忧的时候。

但现在显然不是。

现在的问题不是 Web3 没有机会，而是正在发生的机会太多了，多到我们甚至报道不过来。

这也是我对 Web3 依然充满信心的原因。

同一趟深圳行，老马上车，老黄缺席

白宫确认了，下周川普去菲律宾和中国，马斯克随行。11月18到19号，深圳APEC。

五月那趟北京行，老马和老黄都在名单上。这一次，只剩老马。

而11月18号同一天，老黄被叫去国会，闭门向三个众议院委员会说明情况。

几个点记一下：

一、白宫怎么看老马

白宫的人说，马斯克在中美关系里有巨大的生意利益，也是美国国家安全很重要的一部分，跟着去当总统的顾问，很有帮助。

一边是特斯拉在中国的工厂，一边是SpaceX的国防订单，两头都牵着，他还是坐上了这班飞机。

二、白宫怎么处理老黄

同一个电话会上，白宫的人说，英伟达的事不应该影响这趟行程，川普见习近平也不打算提Alice Huang。

说是不提，其实就是先放一边，切割干净。

三、差在政治触觉

我一直觉得，老黄没有什么政治触觉，应该学老马在特斯拉的做法，增加股份。

他提议卖芯片给中国，本意是让中国更依赖美国的体系，但鹰派一开始就不接受。

老马的处境也不容易，政治压力一样大，但他知道怎么站位，让自己变成“国家安全的一部分”。

AI的两根柱子，一根在国会门口等问话，一根跟着总统去深圳。

四、合并那一关

SpaceX吃下特斯拉，12月份宣布，我觉得不意外。最难的一关，就是特斯拉的中国业务和SpaceX的国防业务怎么隔开。

这趟深圳行，正好看老马怎么两头摆平。

老马自己也签了名，支持老黄回来。

我还是那句：一身傲骨何惧风浪，我支持黄仁勋。

text:
🚨 Microsoft, $MSFT, ruled out its own AI as the cause of a global outage on a service with 450 MILLION paid seats.

It still has not said what did cause it, or how many of those seats were affected.

The only explanation so far is a fault "introduced by an earlier network capacity upgrade."

What it has disclosed is the money.

Spending on property and equipment went from $64.6 BILLION to $116 BILLION in the year to June 30.

Headcount went the other way, falling about 5,000 to roughly 223,000, its first annual drop in about a decade.

CFO Amy Hood has guided another $170 BILLION for this year.

To put that into perspective:

That is about $520,000 of new property and equipment last year for every person Microsoft employs.

Same company. Nearly twice the equipment spending, and 5,000 fewer people to mind it.

AI was named as a reason in 33% of tech layoff events in 2026, up from 1% in 2024, per Roger Lee's layoff tracker.

"All the experienced people, the people who built the stuff up, have left," analyst Rupert Goodwins told Al Jazeera.

Then on Thursday the email stopped, with problem reports from 74 COUNTRIES, per Downdetector.

Australia's spy agency and federal police were caught up in it, per ABC News.

Immigration New Zealand paused every visa application in the country.

Offices across Japan went back to the fax machine.

The outage may have cost as much as $7 BILLION in lost productivity, per the Anderson Economic Group.

Microsoft says email is back to "approaching normal levels," and that it is "deeply sorry for the disruption."

It has promised a full post-incident report once its review is complete.
author: coinbureau
quoted_text:
⚠️ALERT: A GLOBAL Microsoft outage has knocked out Outlook, Teams and Copilot across 74 countries, hitting software used by 450 MILLION work accounts.

It has dragged on for more than 5 hours, and Microsoft has not confirmed the cause.

At the centre of it is something most of us never think about, but rely on every day.

Exchange Online, the system that delivers Outlook email for businesses, began failing around midday Eastern time on Thursday.

By 1:25 PM, problem reports had jumped from fewer than 15 a minute to 19,650.

Outlook reports alone ran 2,000 times above normal.

A US state government and two hospital systems in Michigan lost access to email.

It even reached ChatGPT and Claude, whose makers said their Microsoft connections were affected.

Reports spiked for Amazon’s AWS too, until Amazon said it was “operating normally” and called the outage reports “inaccurate.”

Microsoft says a number of its servers became “unexpectedly unavailable.”

It paused all deployments and began restarting them.

Hours later, it said its fixes “have not provided the anticipated relief.”

Even Defender, the platform companies rely on to detect cyberattacks, is caught in the outage.

Earlier the same day, Teams had already gone down for over an hour in North America.

Microsoft has not said whether the two are linked, and it has not pointed to an attack.

Reports have eased from a peak near 130,000 to about 37,000 as some servers return, but Microsoft has not declared it fixed or said how many customers were cut off.

text:
Compute will become worthless.

The GPU barons spending billions on compute farms today are akin to the carriage barons of the 1900s that spent building out infrastructure for horse carriages, lengthening the bottleneck, blind to the machine that’s coming to widen it.

Trade: the DuPont family started buying General Motors stock in 1914, when the auto industry was still young and one that was treated as a niche.

I.e., compute becoming valuable because AI feeds on it is not a moat, but a bounty, an incentive for engineers to solve its scarcity.

1. AI demand makes compute scarce.
2. Scarcity makes compute extremely profitable.
3. Profit attracts capital into photonics, neuromorphic chips, wafer-scale chips, better memory, better cooling, better networking, better algorithms.
4. Compute gets cheaper per unit.

As better ways to compute, better means to produce compute, or better ways to use compute arise, all the capex we burnt on traditional compute will go to waste, leaving dead assets in the books of several corporations.

In the 1800s, agriculture depended heavily on natural nitrogen sources like Peruvian guano and Chilean nitrates. These were scarce, and inconveniently located making them geopolitically strategic. Then, two german chemists, Haber and Bosch, developed a way to fix nitrogen from the air into ammonia, with lab success in 1909 and industrial scale by 1913. The previous scarcity, “where do we find enough nitrogen?” (Akin to “where do we find enough GPUs”), was attacked by an advancement: Industrial chemistry.

text:
I have a particularly nasty case of cancer. When I was hospitalized again at my lowest point last year, I told Jensen. He immediately reached out to contacts at Stanford, who were able to cut through red tape, and get me into a clinical trial for which I've turned out to be a perfect fit. I think everyone can have their own views about recent events. But any claims that Jensen did not really care about his staff is simply inaccurate. I, personally, owe him more than I can express.

I think the best tribute we can pay to Jensen's legacy is to drive NVIDIA's continued success and push the whole industry forward, by showing we've learned the lessons from years of working here. We will compare ourselves against Speed of Light. The mission will be the boss. And we will not be scared to take smart, bold risks and fail fast with ruthless intellectual honesty.

But if there is one management story I remember the most, it's a particular Jensen grilling from my time in autonomous vehicles that stayed with me. Luckily I was not in the hot seat for this one. Team A didn't want to use Team B's framework, because they thought it was too slow. Jensen was surprised - it's just applying a bunch of optimized CUDA kernels in sequence, how could it be slow?

So he asked the executive from team B to draw the entire data flow sequence from their framework on the whiteboard and highlight every memcpy. Sure enough, there were a bunch of unnecessary memcpy's surrounding each pipeline stage. Everyone in the room could see why it wasn't getting to SoL and a path to improve things. No arguing about fiefdoms or appeals to authority - the data got us all on the same page.

The lesson was not (just) that unnecessary memory copying is bad. It's that executives should not be afraid to probe into details if something doesn't add up, and leaders need to be technical enough and honest enough to engage in real time and not turn every meeting into "I'll get back to you in a week." If that means counting memcpy's with a billionaire CEO, so be it.

My best executive meetings at NVIDIA have been when I'm fully prepared to present every detail of my team's work, and my worst failures have come when I realized I couldn't go deep enough to really solve the problem.

But the thing that gives me confidence is that Jensen was never the only one to live this philosophy. Anyone who has presented to an SVP at NVIDIA knows they are at risk for getting grilled on fundamental constraints and technical details. I have been part of amazing conversations with both recent and old timer leaders where we were able to get to the core of a problem in an hour rather than a month, because we had the right people in the room and were not afraid to go deeper.

The company is filled with supremely talented people who have been trained for 3 decades to work at the highest level, and you can see it in what we produce every day. I'm so proud to be an NVIDIAn, and I can't wait to show off what we ship in the coming months and years.

text:
Dwarkesh has MAJORLY shortened his timelines: ASI is "possibly only a couple months away"

Just a few months ago, he thought it was the "better part of a decade" away.

"If I had to pick my median year for when automated researchers will be as good as the very best human AI researchers (and assuming the labs don’t intentionally slow down), I’d guess 2028."

"I’ve now come to the view that we’re only a couple of years away, and possibly only a couple of months away, from AIs that are as good as the best humans at AI research. I’ve also come to believe that automating AI research will compress so much progress into a single year that, soon thereafter (so by 2030, but plausibly as early as next year), we’ll have AIs that are at least as good as the best human experts in every field. I know this is a wild claim, and it’s one that I myself didn’t believe even a couple of months ago.

It’s crazy how fast we went from, in 2023, “This model can’t reliably add four-digit numbers,” to, in 2024, “This model can barely solve any problems in a high school math competition,” to, in 2025, “Oh, it can win a gold medal at the International Mathematical Olympiad,” to, earlier this year, “Wow, it’s solving open Erdős problems, but maybe just because no human has attempted to solve these particular problems, and a similar solution was already in the literature,” to, about a month ago, “Okay, it fucking solved a Millennium Prize problem in 88 hours.”

Some of the most well-informed researchers I know, people who have had a very good track record of prediction over the last few years, expect AI to beat the best humans at AI research as early as next year. And 2027 is also the straightforward implication of plugging METR’s finding—that Anthropic’s rate of AI progress has doubled in a year—into a takeoff model.

As former guest Ajeya Cotra put it:

"If we take it at face value that AI is now nearly doubling the rate of AI capabilities progress and assume acceleration from AI is smooth, this naively implies that we would reach extreme superintelligence within a year."

Today’s AIs already do work at about 10 times human speed. And automated researchers would also be working around the clock, nights and weekends included. As a result, each individual automated researcher will be cramming in roughly 50x more work every calendar week than a human researcher can do.

And this is before we account for the fact that, in this scenario, every automated researcher will be at least as good at AI R&D as the very best humans.

My sense is that around 80% of the algorithmic progress at a given frontier lab is driven by its top 50 researchers.

In the last four years, we’ve gone from a preschooler to a savant intern. If you made another jump that big, but starting in 2027 or 2028, you’d probably get a mind that would be vastly superhuman in domains that are even slightly verifiable.

For example, it’d be better than Nvidia at coming up with the next generation of AI accelerators. It would make more money than the current human versions of Citadel and Jane Street (if it had equal access to the market). If you gave it remote access to a materials science experiment lab, it’d be better than the rest of humanity at finding a room-temperature superconductor.

text:
NYT has responded to my post by claiming that I’m “spreading conspiracy theories.” But which of us is the one trafficking in unsubstantiated allegations? 

Recent coverage (including CNN, which I QT’d) shows:

— The intelligence community has not established conclusive evidence that Alice Huang knowingly acted as a spy or funneled information to Beijing.

— There is internal disagreement about the strength of the evidence and whether she was recruited by the MSS.

— Attorney General Todd Blanche has said on the record that the Justice Department, he, and FBI Director Patel have reached no conclusions about “who she is or is not.”

— Some officials at ODNI and CIA have indicated the “Chinese spy” label is not fully accurate or is “over-torqued” based on the available intercepts and collection.

— Incoming House Intelligence Chairman Jim Himes, a Democrat, said it was still unclear whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy immediately after he was briefed. 

NYT’s stories (which have alleged “Chinese spy” dozens of times) have relied exclusively on anonymous officials. No official has gone on the record affirming it as established fact, and the more recent reporting reflects greater caution and disagreement inside the government. 

So when I point out that the spy narrative is unconfirmed and increasingly contested, that is not a conspiracy theory. It’s a growing body of evidence that indicts the NYT’s reporting.
author: jgarzik
quoted_text:
Bombshell story. The spy narrative is collapsing already.

Is there clear & convincing evidence that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy?

- AG says no. (“no conclusions reached”).
- CIA says no. (“not yet convinced”).
- DNI says no (“not entirely accurate and over-torqued”).
- Ranking Democrat on House Intelligence (incoming Chairman) says no. (“today, at least, I don’t know”). This was immediately after he was briefed.

Who argues otherwise? Anonymous officials tell CNN “it strains credulity to believe that she was not acting as an agent of the Chinese government — simply by virtue of the fact that she is a successful Chinese businesswoman working with one of America’s most powerful companies.”

This is their proof after a year of investigating and surveillance? That she was a “successful Chinese businesswoman”? 

At this point, the only crime that we know for sure happened is the leaking of the classified memo. Who did that and why?

An investigation should be opened.

text:
Here’s the recap of @cz_binance’s fireside with Anthony Pompliano at Cantor Convergence in Miami:

He showed up in Miami just weeks after the biggest hack in crypto history and still looked calm. No stress, no drama. Just there.

What stood out:

Trust gets built when things go wrong, not when everything is perfect. @cz_binance basically said resilience matters more than never getting hit. That’s how you actually move Bitcoin forward.

He also talked about AI and regulation. “Any new technology will go through a phase we can’t make regulation ahead of time. It moves too fast.” Crypto already went through this. AI is going through it now.
And security. The $6.3B hack showed the industry (and even banks) hasn’t been taking this seriously enough. AI is making attacks faster. The only real answer is fighting AI with AI and actually working together as an industry instead of everyone doing their own thing.

No full recording out yet but @cz_binance said it should be somewhere.

While most people are still panicking or pointing fingers, @cz_binance is still focused on the long game. Protecting users and building through the noise. 

That’s why a lot of us still trust him. 🔶

quoted_text:
以太坊基金会关联地址再次卖出 2,000 枚 ETH。回看过去五年，基金会的 ETH 资金流向值得关注。

据链上分析师 @ai_9684xtpa 监测，11 月 13 日，ETH 跌破 2,000 美元之际，以太坊基金会关联地址（0x5CB…22059）再次卖出 2,000 枚 ETH，价值约 386.8 万美元。

自 10 月 26 日以来，该地址已累计卖出 6,785 枚 ETH，套现约 1,445 万美元，目前仍持有 21,247 枚 ETH，价值约 4,110 万美元。

从 2021 年至今，以太坊基金会相关 ETH 资金流向还包括：

- 2021 年： 两次大额转入，分别为 35,053 枚和 20,000 枚 ETH。
- 2023 年： 转入 15,000 枚 ETH，并有 1,700 枚 ETH 的出售记录。
- 2024 年： 再次转入 35,000 枚 ETH。基金会当时明确表示，钱包转移不等于出售。
- 2025 年： 出现 5,000 枚、10,000 枚 ETH 的出售记录，同时还有 5,000 枚及 10,000 枚 ETH 的出售计划或预告。
- 2026 年： 先后出现 2,785 枚、1,000 枚及近期 2,000 枚 ETH 的出售记录，另有 5,000 枚 ETH 的预告。

需要注意，历史上累计超过 10 万枚 ETH 的大额转入不能直接计入卖出总量，部分交易属于钱包迁移或资金管理；2026 年部分卖出记录也来自关联钱包的链上归因，并非每笔都有基金会同步公告。

从早期的大额资产转移，到近年来通过链上交易及 CoW Swap 等方式管理资金，以太坊基金会的 ETH 资金管理方式一直在变化。

但在 ETH 跌破 2,000 美元、市场流动性承压之际，基金会关联地址的持续卖出，显然会进一步放大市场对抛压的关注。

author: Shenjingape
quoted_text:
I have a particularly nasty case of cancer. When I was hospitalized again at my lowest point last year, I told Jensen. He immediately reached out to contacts at Stanford, who were able to cut through red tape, and get me into a clinical trial for which I've turned out to be a perfect fit. I think everyone can have their own views about recent events. But any claims that Jensen did not really care about his staff is simply inaccurate. I, personally, owe him more than I can express.

I think the best tribute we can pay to Jensen's legacy is to drive NVIDIA's continued success and push the whole industry forward, by showing we've learned the lessons from years of working here. We will compare ourselves against Speed of Light. The mission will be the boss. And we will not be scared to take smart, bold risks and fail fast with ruthless intellectual honesty.

But if there is one management story I remember the most, it's a particular Jensen grilling from my time in autonomous vehicles that stayed with me. Luckily I was not in the hot seat for this one. Team A didn't want to use Team B's framework, because they thought it was too slow. Jensen was surprised - it's just applying a bunch of optimized CUDA kernels in sequence, how could it be slow?

So he asked the executive from team B to draw the entire data flow sequence from their framework on the whiteboard and highlight every memcpy. Sure enough, there were a bunch of unnecessary memcpy's surrounding each pipeline stage. Everyone in the room could see why it wasn't getting to SoL and a path to improve things. No arguing about fiefdoms or appeals to authority - the data got us all on the same page.

The lesson was not (just) that unnecessary memory copying is bad. It's that executives should not be afraid to probe into details if something doesn't add up, and leaders need to be technical enough and honest enough to engage in real time and not turn every meeting into "I'll get back to you in a week." If that means counting memcpy's with a billionaire CEO, so be it.

My best executive meetings at NVIDIA have been when I'm fully prepared to present every detail of my team's work, and my worst failures have come when I realized I couldn't go deep enough to really solve the problem.

But the thing that gives me confidence is that Jensen was never the only one to live this philosophy. Anyone who has presented to an SVP at NVIDIA knows they are at risk for getting grilled on fundamental constraints and technical details. I have been part of amazing conversations with both recent and old timer leaders where we were able to get to the core of a problem in an hour rather than a month, because we had the right people in the room and were not afraid to go deeper.

The company is filled with supremely talented people who have been trained for 3 decades to work at the highest level, and you can see it in what we produce every day. I'm so proud to be an NVIDIAn, and I can't wait to show off what we ship in the coming months and years.

The Agent Initiative Benchmark puts 12 frontier models inside a synthetic company with 6 years of history (a financial model, CRM records, past-due invoices, Linear tickets) and has them listen in on the team's Slack, from aligning work across teams to warning against an unapproved customer logo.

text:
May 20th: Wenfeng told investors that his fleet is 20K H-equivalent GPUs; "most" arrived in the last 2 months. Flash was served online since Feb 11th. Checkpoints out: Apr 24. Will says V4-P used GB2/300; V4-F B2/300. Say 2K of each (Depue gives a lower floor but see below). Multipliers at LEAST 2.5 and 3 imo. +He had those old 2K H800s (which they had unlocked to ≈parity). That works out to 13/20. And if we include old 10K A100s, or some more Hoppers, it gets worse even if we stick to lower multipliers.
I don't think he'd have lied to investors (and he had no incentive to) or exploited a technicality.  He compares Ascend cards ("Huawei gives us 16,000 [950DT] cards; this is probably something we can say publicly") to GB300 as equivalent at 1:4 rate. Their inference throughput and revenue/GPU disclosed with DeepInfer release suggest they had at least 2.5-3K of Grace Blackwells by Oct 20 (almost certainly GB200, given how the results reproduce). That can be the same cluster that was used to train V4-Pro. 
Some more datapoints (though obviously this is more about the export template) 
- V3, R1: "transformers_version": "4.33.1" 
- R1, R1-Zero, V3-0324, R1-0528, Prover-V2: 4.46.3 
- V3.1 to V3.2 and Math-V2: bizarrely regress to 4.44.2, some parallel track 
- all V4 variants, ie 2 bases, 2 previews, 2 updates: 4.57.1 (SM_100 support was added by v4.52.4; FP4 by v4.55.0, but V4 doesn't use FP4 in training, and uses MXFP4 for weights to have compatibility with Ascend) 
- V4-Flash-Vision-exp: 5.0.0 
- V4.1-Flash 0910-1017: 5.6.0

incidentally, 5.6.0 was released Apr 22, 2026, two days before V4-Previews went on Huggingface.
For the record, Inkling’s first model (Jul 15) required 5.14.0.

What is my takeaway?
The "most H-equivalents arrived within 2 months", in this logic, necessitates that some large chunk of Blackwells arrived after V4-Flash was done, ie starting in March (literally 03.20, but let's say "months" is inclusive). Taking Wenfeng entirely at his word, I conclude that V4-Pro had not been trained before that. On Feb 23, as per Reuters, "Chinese AI startup DeepSeek's latest AI model, set to be released as soon as next week, was trained on Nvidia's (NVDA.O), most advanced AI chip, the Blackwell, a senior Trump administration official said on Monday… the U.S. believes DeepSeek will remove the technical indicators that might reveal its use of American AI chips, the official said, adding that the Blackwells are likely clustered at its data center in Inner Mongolia, an autonomous region of China." I don't put much stock in Trump officials, nothing publicly came out until 2 months later, there's no reason to take 30-something racks to Inner Mongolia, Blackwells are not made equal, and the removal clearly hadn't been very thorough, despite DS having ex-Nvidia staff, to whose ranks Depue does not belong… but I presume there's a grain of truth here; his info was about Flash and B-chips.

So I conjecture that they were focused on validating TileLang/TileKernels and Ascend compatibility with Flash, probably had a dummy Pro model. Then they got NVL72 GB200s (or maybe GB300s, in which case V4.1's inference cluster is a separate entity). The final experiments and pretraining were rushed (only 33T vs 32T in Flash despite >5x more params and >3x active), capabilities MOPD-distilled from Flash [we know from GLM etc that MOPD stage takes < 2 days]; which explains unprincipled minor architecture differences and "Anticipatory Routing" tinkering, fumbling with instability, lousy performance, and commitment to do better: "To minimize risk, we retained many preliminarily validated components and tricks, which, while effective, made the architecture relatively complex. In future iterations, we will carry out more comprehensive and principled investigations to distill the architecture down to its most essential designs, making it more elegant without sacrificing performance".
V4.1 project was launched concurrently with V4-Preview release, and might have used Ascend for pretraining, though on this I do not have an opinion. Blackwells are used to serve V4.1F. V4 post-trains had low priority all along.
-----
TL;DR:
- V4-Flash was trained on a small B-series cluster in late 2025-early 2026, and used to validate the TileLang and Ascend tooling. Little attention had been paid to scaling of this design. 
- A cluster of roughly 3K GB200 cards arrived around March; Pro was rushed through on it; that cluster now serves V4.1-Flash.

text:
These are all great questions, taking a quick stab: 

1/ More than off the table I'd say it's a distraction. ETH is a programmable store of value. And importantly Ethereum chooses security over zero issuance, and I think that's the correct choice. Bitcoin still needs to answer the question of what security will look like once block rewards are zero. Very unclear. 

@adietrichs and I gave a talk covering this point starting at 20:55: https://t.co/Iqu7hxnKUa

2/ I agree it needs to settle once and for all. I'd characterize Ethereum's philoshopy as "fastest viable ossificiation". Ethereum is playing a long-term game, and zooming out I strongly believe we'll be happy that Ethereum did not myopically ossify but is willing and able to converge on a policy that is fit for this civilizational foundation that we're all building. And importantly: Ethereum has only ever decreased its issuance and I consider this to be part of the social contract. 

3/ I think Ethereum is uniquely positioned to become the canonical root of trust for the world. Only Ethereum is credibly neutral and secure enough, and (!) set up architecturally for settling other chains. (Bitcoin is the former but not the latter). And I think of L2s as a critical piece in making this vision a reality: Ethereum as the root of trust but with activity that demands differentiation along dimensions that the L1 cannot offer (e.g. different configurations of speed, compliance, privacy) it can flow from Ethereum to L2s, while still inheriting the strongest guarantees that only Ethereum can offer. 

I spoke about this a lot in my recent talk at Devcon: https://t.co/eAXOEsQRgi

4/ This is a great question and I don't have an immediate answer, would love to hear your thoughts on this! :) 

5/ I strongly agree, and Ethereum is incredibly well positioned here. The EF has led the path with years of investments into post-quantum research, and Ethereum is now in this privileged position where we can accelerate timelines to be post-quantum and post-AI in 2027: https://t.co/E6xUSZga0j

And ETH will be a pqai store of value btw :)

text:
熊市最佳的抄底策略，大概还是 DCA 买 BTC 吧～

大家常说，最容易赚的钱是周期的钱，这话确实没错。

这轮个人最成功的操作，就是相信四年周期，并在 22 年 12 月左右分批抄底，时间过去太久，成本记不太清。

大概 $BTC 成本在 $1.7 万、 $ETH 成本 $1500、 $BNB 成本 $250（应该在 100 左右，当时在 Alpaca 杠杆挖矿赚了不少 BNB）。

不过，过度相信周期（有点刻舟求剑的意味）也有坑。虽然抄了个好底，但因为太相信山寨季，结果抵押 BTC、ETH 买了不少山寨，还抵押山寨再买山寨。

最终在 23 年 8 月 5 日（还是 20 来着？忘记了），迎来这轮最大的清算，那天资金直接回撤 50%。

从山寨季上来说，周期并没有那么确定。

尤其这一轮，大家都经历过 BTC 和 ETH 各自的独立行情，四年周期大概率也不复存在了（BTC 减半的影响估计很小）。

所以，要精准踩中某个时间点去买入 BTC 和 ETH，几乎是不可能的。

那怎么办呢？或许答案就是 DCA，那么 DCA 是什么？

DCA 俗称定投，目的就是通过时间来平均买入成本，避免错过底部。

但研究了多个交易所的定投策略后发现，它们无法做到 "跌多买多"，也就是无法实现金字塔式加仓，所以最终还是放弃了定投。

于是选择了另一种 DCA 方式 —— 现货马丁格尔。

简单来说，就是跌得越多，买得越多。

举个例子：每跌 1% 基础加仓 100U，每次加仓都比上次多 50%，共加仓 8 次。

如图，从 9.18 万价格开始执行策略，在第 8 次加仓后的接货价为 5.5 万，最终平均价格为 6.2 万，相比最低点只差不到 1 万。

当然，这是理想情况，现实中可能到不了那么低，甚至可能比第八次的价格更低。

我实际设置的是：加仓 80 次，每次 1%，每次比上次多买 1.06 倍，最低接货价 1.8 万。

这个价格大概率也到不了，但没关系。一方面是防黑天鹅，另一方面这个策略随时可以停止，现货依然在手里，持仓成本也比一次性买入更低。

一句话总结「现货马丁格尔」策略：它能在熊市实现资金的三角形抄底，比定投更适合在价格维度抄底。

另外，这个策略是在 OKX 上运行的，因为执行策略的 USDT 还能拿到 2.8%（浮动）的活期利息。

提示：以上仅为信息分享，非投资建议，请务必自行做好研究！

Patrick Witt: The U.S. Government Needs Explicit Congressional Authorization to Legally Buy Bitcoin  

On November 10, 2026, Patrick Witt @patrickjwitt, former executive director of the White House Crypto Council, said in an interview with What Bitcoin Did @_DannyKnowles that President Donald Trump is interested in adding to the government's Bitcoin holdings. The administration has discussed several ways to do so, but legal questions remain over whether the government can buy Bitcoin directly on the open market and how it could do so without triggering a negative market reaction. 

Witt said the administration wants to codify the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and secure explicit authorization from Congress. Because Congress controls appropriations, the administration would have to show that buying Bitcoin falls within the original purpose of any existing funds it plans to use. He added that moving prematurely could prompt Congress to insert a provision into the National Defense Authorization Act banning such purchases, undermining efforts to secure authorization.

author: IamRamenPanda
quoted_text:
戒掉美股日内短线和期权赌瘾到底有多难？看看下面这位老兄荒诞又心酸的自白就知道了。

他把自己的惨烈战绩公之于众：整整几年的时间里，他始终坚信自己离一飞冲天“只差下一笔神操作”。结果一路频繁买卖、重仓期权，硬生生把自己攒下的 14.2 万美元积蓄亏掉了 14 万，账户余额最终定格在可怜的 2,000 美元。

他郑重宣布：“真正的收获是一路走来攒下的心理创伤。市场终于用一记保证金追缴单（Margin Call）敲碎了我的自负。从今天起，我正式从日内交易退休，转投一项全新策略——买入并持有（Buy and Hold）。祝贺那些在对手盘赚走我 14 万美元的人，这是你们应得的。”

看到这里，不少网友还在替他挽惜，甚至有老哥扎心补刀：“如果能让你好受点的话——过去一年标普 500 涨了 25%，所以算上机会成本，这波操作其实让你亏了 17.5 万美元。”大家都以为，交了这么昂贵的学费，他总该大彻大悟、迷途知返了。

然而，还有黑色幽默反转，出现在他的追问里。

在刚刚发完誓要金盆洗手之后，他用最后那  2000美元残存本金、买进了一排下个月到期的末日看涨期权（Calls）。他满怀期待地问网友：“在我正式退休之前，我在赌场还有这最后几把下注，你们觉得有戏吗？”

他又忍不住追问了一句：“顺便问一下，我现在把这 2,000 块投到哪里，才能把亏掉的 13.8 万赚回来？”甚至有人随口调侃让他去买某只股票的看涨期权时，他立刻像抓住救命稻草一样追问：“买哪个行权价？什么时候到期？”

大家瞬间从同情变成了彻底的无语。一位网友一针见血地回复道：“你 9 个月前没吸取教训，到了今天还在问这种问题，说明这 14 万的学费，你连一点教训都没学进去。”

这就是交易市场里最真实的戒断反应：很多亏损累累的散户嘴上说着“我想通了、我要做长线价值投资”，心里想的其实依然是“等我再赌赢最后一把翻本了，就去老老实实买指数”。

只要你还指望在同一张把你榨干的赌桌上把本金赢回来，你的止损就永远没有真正开始。

你身边有那种嘴上天天喊着“回本就销户”、实际上却越陷越深的朋友吗？

text:
I have long thought that there are 4 things that would be truly bad for Bitcoin: 

1⃣.  A technical failure.  Private keys can be derived from public keys.  Something that makes the whole idea of holding Bitcoin insecure.

2⃣.  Coinbase (largest custodian) loses 1M+ BTC (due to hack or key mismanagement) and it's permanently unrecoverable.  This would affect the ETFs and MSTR.  Institutional adoption narrative is crushed.  It still doesn't make Bitcoin go to zero, but it would probably turn it back into a cypherpunk asset.

3⃣.  The US$ and other fiat currencies become sound money currencies, govt budgets are balanced, central banks never expand balance sheets.

4⃣.  Bitcoin IOUs become *too* widely used instead of Bitcoin itself.  Allows custodians to engage in fractional reserve because not enough people are willing/able to hold/send/receive actual Bitcoin.  In other words, Bitcoin goes the route of gold.  This doesn't kill Bitcoin and make it go to zero (just like it didn't kill gold and make it go to zero).  But it means Bitcoin failed to be a fixed supply, bearer asset, widely used money.

To state the obvious, none of these things have happened.

So, absent these things happening, I view the current price action and sentiment to be the same as it's been throughout Bitcoin's history: during a bear market certain people have laundry lists of reasons why Bitcoin is dead and will never hit a new ATH again.

Yet Bitcoin has repeatedly survived these episodes, recovered, and established new ATHs.  The signal has been to observe that what was previously a price high at a euphoric peak becomes a new price floor in a bear market.

text:
$20/月的 Claude 订阅性价比到底有多高？

我用护照 KYC 的 Claude 账号终于倒下了。

着急忙慌四处寻找替代品，包括一些号称满血 Opus/Falbe 中转站、第三方平台（比如 Devin, Factory 等）。

但我比较好奇，到底这些平替能不能真的替代原版的 Claude 订阅。

于是有了以下这些数据分析。

TLDR：

差别非常大，打 1 折的中转站和原版订阅比，也几乎是天价。

首先看下自己账号的真实使用情况。

根据 CodexBar 的使用量统计（已经计入了不同模型、缓存读写的实际价格）。

我的 20 刀订阅的 Claude Pro 账号，过去30 天实际消耗（按照 API 价格）约为：$1239.

也就是 1:60 的放大系数。

1刀的费用，能用出 60 刀的 API 价值。

中转站即便打 1 折（也就是按照 API 价格 -90%），那么也就是 1:10 的放大系数。

1刀的费用，能用出 10 刀的 API 价值。

中转站的价格，也等于你订阅的 6 倍。

注意，我还没有每次都把所有额度用光（害怕封号，虽然最终结局一样）。

按照 Gemini 的计算，如果是 $20 的 Claude Pro 订阅，你可以理解为一个 0.15 折的官方 API 中转站。

如果是 Claude Max 订阅，大概是 0.2～0.3 折的样子。

所以发现了吗？

其实你真的想用 Opus 5.5 , Fable 5.2，而且想要不被封号，方法多的是。

最简单粗暴的方式就是直接 OpenRouter 接入，满血、不降智。

问题在于：

原版 API 定价太贵了，普通人用不起。

说白了大家就是想要便宜好用分量足、折扣极低的官方订阅。

其实如果账算到这个份儿上，那么那些加价一倍卖的 Claude 订阅，似乎也不是不能接受。

比如原价 $20，你花 $40 能用上，那也是 0.3 倍的折扣系数，比中转站的 1 折，还便宜 3 倍多呢。

这多花的钱，就是国人税。

Y Combinator 总裁 Garry Tan 开源 Agent 外壳评测库 g-harness-evals，实测同一大模型换不同框架通过率差不多，但单次成本差了 2.5 倍以上
Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO Garry Tan 在 GitHub 上开源了一个名为 g-harness-evals 的评测项目。大家平时选编程 Agent 时往往只盯着底层大模型，但真正把聊天模型变成干活 Agent 的，其实是模型外面的那层“外壳”（Harness）——也就是系统提示词、工具调用、记忆机制和权限控制。
Garry Tan 搞这个项目的逻辑很直接：把底层大模型（如 Claude Opus 5.5、GPT-6.1 Sol）和测试任务完全固定死，只换外面的 Agent 框架，看看到底哪家干活最好、花钱最少。目前被拉上实验台对比的主流框架有五个：Claude Code、Codex、OpenClaw、Hermes Agent 和 QM，同时还顺带测试了他自己做的两个外挂组件：知识库 gbrain 和技能包 gstack。
【首轮实测：成功率拉不开差距，账单差距巨大】
第一批公开任务跑下来，有几个非常反直觉的发现：
在 20 个开发测试任务上，7 组“模型+外壳”搭配的任务通过率全都挤在 71% 到 79% 之间。比如同样搭载 Opus 模型，Hermes 通过率是 78.8%，Claude Code 和 OpenClaw 都是 76.3%，QM 是 72.5%。Garry Tan 在报告里直接写明，这些分数的 95% 置信区间高度重叠，统计上根本分不出高下。
真正拉开差距的是钱。每成功解决一个任务，OpenClaw 平均要花 0.44 美元，Claude Code 是 0.22 美元，而 Codex 只要 0.17 美元。
为了搞清楚钱到底花在哪了，团队把各个框架连到一个虚假的模型接口上，一分钱不花地抓包了它们发出的第一个请求。结果发现，面对一模一样的任务，不同框架塞给模型的初始上下文体量天差地别：Codex 大约发了 12,900 个 Token，Claude Code 发了 18,416 个，而 Hermes 直接飙到了 20,613 个。而且在一次 Sonnet 模型的测试里，OpenClaw 账单里 87% 的钱都花在了提示词缓存（Prompt Caching）的读写上，真正模型输出只占 13%。
【塞进上下文的技能包，模型一次都没执行】
Garry Tan 还拿自己写的两个热门开源组件开刀，结果一点面子都没给自己留。
第一个是 gstack（一套模拟工程团队角色的技能文件）。测试发现，虽然 gstack 的技能说明文本在每次会话里都成功加载进了 Opus 5.5，但在 46 次测试里，模型实际执行技能步骤的次数是 0 次，反而让单次测试成本直接翻倍。团队试着加了一个拦截钩子（Hook），强制要求先跑失败复现才准改代码，结果 Opus 直接通过 Bash 命令写源码，绕过了钩子整整 40 次。只有在加上专门的启动钩子（Start Hook）后，Agent 才会乖乖调用启动命令。
第二个是 gbrain（团队共享知识库）。如果不专门按提问者的身份做权限隔离（Scoping），直接给机器人一个全公司通用的 Token，在检索时 OpenClaw 和 Hermes 分别吐出了 123 条和 121 条提问者根本无权查看的跨权限私密记录。只有把知识库严格限制在提问者自己的权限范围内，越权读取才会降到 0。此外，挂载 gbrain 时，只有 Claude Code 会把知识库自带的操作说明传给模型，其他几个框架全都直接丢弃了。
整个仓库目前做成了“无密钥可验证”的模式。每一项跑分、置信区间和账单明细都附带了完整的原始记录（Receipts），任何人都可以在本地用 Bun 和 Python 3 跑脚本复算核对，不需要消耗自己的 API Key。Garry Tan 也在文档开头坦诚披露了利益相关：QM 是 YC 孵化的项目，YC 投资了 Hermes，而 gstack 和 gbrain 是他自己的个人项目。

text:
大厂的AI商战真是朴实无华，就是猛猛砸钱找专家，猛猛做数据标注。。。字节的Xpert，10月份有一个人领了18万。。。

AI时代，只要你有任何特长，只靠贡献自己的知识和努力，也能活得很滋润：

⓵专业问答与评测
-专业领域问答（医疗、法律、金融、STEM等）
-模型回复打分与对比评测
-Benchmark出题与标准答案设计

⓶聊天 / 对话相关
-多轮对话评估：对模型在聊天中的回复打分、排序、指出问题（准确性、自然度、逻辑、人设一致性等）
-对话生成 / 改写：写或优化多轮对话数据，用于训练聊天机器人
-偏好排序（RLHF）：同一问题给出多个回复，选出更好的那个并写理由
-角色扮演 / 人设对话：按指定角色（医生、律师、客服、特定性格等）进行对话评测或数据生产
-对话纠错：找出聊天回复中的事实错误、逻辑漏洞、不当内容

⓷内容生产类
-高质量专业内容撰写（案例库、知识库、语料）
-复杂指令设计（多约束、高难度Prompt）
-参考答案撰写
-专业内容改写与优化

⓸代码 / 技术类
-代码生成评估
-Agentic Coding / 长程任务评测
-Bug查找与代码审查
-编程题出题与判题标准制定

⓹语音 / 多模态类
-方言语音采集与标注
-语音转写质检
-视频/3D/动捕数据相关
-多模态内容评估

⓺审核与质检类
-模型输出合规性审核（医疗、法律、金融强合规场景）
-知识准确性审核
-已有标注数据的二次质检

⓻其他
-访谈类任务
-数据采集（按脚本录制真实场景）
-创意内容评估（影视、文学、设计美学等）

上面这些任务，简单到只要愿意花时间聊天，时薪也在三位数。更专业一些的比如生物、法律、金融、制造，就更加赚钱了。

看到一个很巧妙的 Agent RL 训练思路：把 Harness 变成训练阶段的探索工具，帮助模型学会原本难以完成的任务。

这来自论文《Harness-S》，研究团队尝试利用不同 Harness 的互补能力，将外部执行环境带来的能力提升迁移到模型自身。

具体机制分为三个环节：

首先，从基础 Harness 的失败轨迹中分析原因，针对不同问题定向修改执行机制，构建一个各有所长的 Sibling Harness Pool。

训练时，模型先在原始 Harness 下多次尝试。如果全部失败，Adaptive Harness Router 就根据各 Harness 的历史表现和适用场景，选择最合适的几个重新探索，并将新轨迹用于 GRPO 训练。Router 还会随着模型能力变化，动态更新选择依据。

这个设计解决了一个关键问题：当 Agent 多次尝试全部失败，GRPO 很难获得有效的组内奖励信号。 不同 Harness 提供了新的成功路径，让模型有机会从失败任务中继续学习。

论文实验显示，Qwen3.5-4B 在原始 Harness 下的 SWE-Gym Pass@3，从普通 GRPO 的 24.38% 提升到 38.75%，提高了 14.37 个百分点。

所以 Harness 可以在训练阶段帮助模型突破能力边界，再通过强化学习，把这些执行经验逐渐转化为模型自身的能力。

📎 arXiv: https://t.co/rcpBL0niSY

💻 GitHub: https://t.co/cCcgnJzVE5

text:
第一点，我不觉得把所有事情一股脑归因于肤色，是一个好的思维方式。

肤色当然有权重，民主党也更习惯把它放在显眼的位置。但拿黄仁勋来说，我们还要看他跟台湾的关系、中美之间的产业利益，以及他支持开源、支持把芯片卖给中国的立场。这些才是权重更高的因素。

不能直接说成：因为他是亚裔，“民主党不喜欢亚裔当 CEO”。这就是以偏概全，会让我们忽略真正需要看的利益关系和参与方的动机。

Elon Musk、Tim Sweeney、Garry Tan 等人都公开为他发声。至少这些人并没有因为他是亚裔，就否定他当 CEO 的能力。

而且，一旦把肤色变成理解所有事情的默认原因，你的日常会变得很愤怒。我经历过这种状态。别人说“You’re good at math”，你都会觉得：你他妈凭什么觉得我 good at math？我就不能 good at sports、rap music？

第二点，我觉得民主党和共和党对亚裔的区别是：民主党是一个能够保你的下限，但会控制你上限的党派。共和党则是，下限可以很低，上限也可以很高。

对那些足够卷、相信自己能够往上走的亚裔来说，自然会更在意上限。

拿移民打个比方，民主党更像是在说：你现在可能什么都不会，但你特别想来，我也愿意接纳你，给你机会和基本保障，医保什么的。共和党更像是在说：你能做什么、能贡献什么？如果真的什么都做不了，那你就别来添乱。

而真到了要比能力的时候，因为形式上的分配问题，亚裔平均数学能力更强，分数更高却反而被卡入学名额和比例。

第三点，肤色和性别等议题，更多是在欧美文化里才有的具体语境和敏感点。

很多时候，确实要在那个环境里生活过，被触碰过几次，才更容易理解别人为什么那么在意。

如果一个女生长期就在美国，也清楚这些争议，那她可能是对语境不敏感，也可能是做过流量和政治性、文化性之间的取舍。对这部分人我是鄙视的。

但对于没有这种文化经历的人，不必强迫要求理解：为什么我只是发一张好看的照片，就成了媚男。这某种程度上是语境坍塌。

我理解的比较浅，仅供参考。

text:
I think the best case is to make the "monitor" as un-agentic as possible.

We don't mind being "monitored" by various random tiny insects we don't even notice, even guard dogs are fine, but we really do mind if it's a globally connected networked system. And the intermediate case, human security guards with no recording equipment, we mind only a medium amount.

The best idea I've come up with so far is to make these monitoring devices out of open-source verifiable hardware that has etched on it an open-weight LLM that classifies for a limited number of activities (basically, just violence; sorry, no scanning for jaywalking or not wearing a mask or drugs or unauthorized manufacturing or illegal immigrants, really just violence) and only records and forwards if that's what it sees. The device has no storage, no ability to load new algorithms, this is all it does.

Also, a hash of every recording is published onchain (and a device can't record the next one until it sees confirmation of the previous one) so we can all count how much recording is done.

Finally, everyone has a legal right to take any such device they see and grab it and dissassemble and verify the hardware themselves. Explicitly fund university clubs, hacker groups, etc to regularly do this.

text:
⚠️ Warning: Long rant incoming.

I’ve been waiting for someone in the national NBA media to address this, but apparently nobody wants to.

Why was Luka Doncic’s first NBA Finals loss treated as proof that his style of basketball couldn’t win a championship, while Victor Wembanyama’s was treated as another step toward greatness?

Luka averaged 29.2/8.8/5.6 against a 64-win Celtics team, and the national media spent the next two years questioning his defense, conditioning, leadership and whether his style of basketball could ever win a championship.

Wemby loses 4–1 to a 53-win Knicks team, struggles down the stretch, and suddenly we’re reminded that even Jordan and LeBron needed time. It’s all about growth, valuable lessons and gaining experience.

And this hypocrisy doesn’t end with the Finals. It carries directly into the MVP conversation.

Luka’s individual brilliance is constantly filtered through questions about his defense, playing style, team success and whether he can actually win.

Wemby’s brilliance is celebrated as evidence of what he’s becoming. His shortcomings are treated as things he’ll eventually overcome.

One player has to constantly justify why he deserves an MVP. The other is talked about like winning one is inevitable.

Nobody is asking for Wemby to be torn down. But why does one generational talent have to overcome a narrative the media created while the other gets the benefit of the doubt?

이사회는 오늘 앞서 공식적으로 접촉한 후임 후보도 없고, 아직 헤드헌팅(서치펌) 업체조차 선정하지 않았다고 밝힘.

주주들 입장에선 AI 시대 절대반지 쥔 창업자가 조사 결과도 다 나오기 전에 영구 퇴장당하는 게 최악의 시나리오임. 큰손 기관들이 직접 총대 메고 "조사 끝나고 문제없거나 수습 가능하면 다시 데려올 여지 남겨둬라"라며 이사회 목줄 쥐고 압박하는 그림임. 이사회도 아직 서치펌조차 안 골랐다고 발 뺀 걸 보면, 주주 눈치 보면서 속도 조절 들어간 분위기라 향후 조사 결과와 이사회 행보가 주가 향방을 가를 핵심 변수가 될 전망임.

한 줄 평: 33년 깎은 가죽자켓 장인을 대체할 사람이 지구상에 있을 리가 없으니 큰손들도 멱살 잡고 말리는 중 ㅋㅋ

text:
昨晚九点多，Circle发了条人事公告
两个人升职

Dante Disparte，首席战略官，升成Circle第一个副董事长
Mandeep Walia，首席合规官，再兼一个COO

2019年6月，Facebook搞了个Libra
想让几十亿用户都用上它的币
Disparte是Libra协会的创始高管，管政策
Walia是Facebook钱包Novi的首席合规官

然后呢
扎克伯格被叫去国会
Visa、万事达、Stripe先后退出
改名Diem也没救回来
2022年1月，整个项目1.82亿美元卖给了Silvergate
Diem自己说的，跟联邦监管谈下来，这事走不下去了

而这两个人，2021年春天一前一后去了Circle

当年站在被监管掐死的那一边
几年后，Circle说Disparte是把GENIUS法案推到签字的关键人物
美国第一部稳定币联邦法
OCC的最终规则明年1月生效，也是他带着Circle一路谈下来的

一个求监管放行没求成的项目
最后自己把这条路修通了

这也算是逆袭成功了~

再把这两个月串起来
9月25号，联合创始人Sean Neville退出董事会
同一天，CFO宣布年底走人，接班的到今天还没公布
11月13号，管政策的升副董事长，管合规的接手运营
总裁Heath Tarbert，以前是CFTC主席

Circle下一步拼什么，它自己摆到桌面上了

公告底下也有人骂
「Stop dumping your stock scammers」
股价从10月21号的89.7，跌到最新收盘62.2

可股价天天在变
升谁不升谁，才是公司真打算往哪走
